payload.text:
# Remove the deprecated verbs.json glob from the auto-managed lists

## Problem
`.endless/verbs.json` is deprecated (superseded by `.endless/verbs.jsonl`); it is
untracked and no longer written. Two mirrored glob lists still name it:

- `src/endless/worktree_cmd.py` `AUTO_COMMIT_GLOBS` (line ~62):
  `".endless/verbs.json",  # legacy — still seen during E-1268 migration`
- `internal/monitor/worktree_anomalies.go` `AutoManagedStatusGlobs` (line ~40):
  same entry, but with **no comment** — an undocumented dead glob.

The two are required to stay in sync (per the doc comment on the Go list:
"Mirrors src/endless/worktree_cmd.py AUTO_COMMIT_GLOBS — keep the two in sync").

## Fix
If the E-1268 migration is complete (verbs.json no longer produced anywhere),
drop the `.endless/verbs.json` entry from BOTH mirrors. If it must linger, at
least add the same "legacy — E-1268 migration" explanatory comment to the Go
copy so the two agree and the entry isn't mistaken for a live path.

## Notes
- Harmless today (the glob matches nothing), so this is pure hygiene.
- The sibling entries `.endless/db-ledger/*.jsonl` and `.endless/verbs.jsonl` are
  live and must stay.

## Origin
Found auditing the worktree unsettled/dirty predicate (`taskWorktreeDirty`) and
its auto-managed filter during E-1834.

payload.title: Implement the description-sufficiency evaluator job
payload.description: The bespoke job that registers with the E-698 fire-once runner. For each unevaluated task it assembles the persisted-artifact context (description + parent + sibling titles + linked decisions — deliberately NOT the filing session's context) and calls a model via the shared run_internal_claude helper with a config-resolved model (standardize the config key so verb auto-registration and this evaluator resolve their model the same way; do not hardcode 'claude -p'; see E-1849 for making the harness itself pluggable). It then sets status to submitted or unplanned and emits the transition as an event with evaluator attribution. Runs as belt (inline at file time) and suspenders (background sweep over the unevaluated queue).

fields.title: Build auto-routing of new tasks to unplanned or submitted
fields.description: Container for the feature that removes the manual submit-vs-plan judgment: new tasks land in unevaluated and an evaluator routes each to submitted (description is a sufficient spec) or unplanned (needs a planning session), with status — not complexity/risk — routing the workflow. Completion derives from its children (the unevaluated status wiring E-1845 and the evaluator job E-1859); the opt-out E-1847 is a related maybe. Rides the E-698 fire-once runner; orthogonal to auto-spawn (E-1812), which shares only that runner.

fields.analysis: Epic-definition correction (2026-08): the definition must lead with CONTAINER-NESS, not size/duration. An epic is a container - never directly implemented, completion derives entirely from its children's states, no deliverable of its own; size and duration are NOT criteria (epics can be small). The 'multi-week narrative initiatives' phrasing in this description and in ED-1503 misleads by implying a size bar - it led a session to wrongly reject a small container as 'too small to be an epic.' When E-1545 writes the guide definition, lead with container-ness and omit 'multi-week' as a criterion. Scope note: 'completion derives from children' is defined for EPICS ONLY; non-epic parent-child completion semantics are unsettled.

fields.description: Add epic to authorized task types. An epic is a CONTAINER task: never directly implemented, and its completion derives entirely from its children's states - it has no deliverable of its own. Size and duration are NOT criteria (an epic can be small); what makes a task an epic is that it is complete only when its children are. Children may be known up front or emerge through planning. Status in_progress/completed auto-derive from child states; revisit/ready/declined/obsolete/blocked are explicit overrides. Terminal status is completed; no verify in v1 (maybe E-1535); all statuses reopenable. CLI aliases (endless epic) and pause-on-revisit hook are implementation details.

payload.title: Surface proposed decisions in session status for review and approve/modify/decline
payload.description: Product gap: proposed decisions are invisible in session status, so they sit unreviewed and get treated as settled. session status (and/or session next) should surface open proposed decisions so the user can approve, modify, or decline them, closing the loop that currently lets a proposed decision masquerade as authority.

payload.title: Explore decision storage (dedicated table vs task_content) and how decisions are arrived at
payload.description: Two threads Mike wants captured, not tackled yet. (1) Storage: reconsider whether decisions belong in a dedicated table (E-1511) or move back onto tasks as a typed content item sibling to tasks.outcome, riding the task_content model (E-1531) - so 'decision' becomes a content type, not a task type. (2) Process: how to arrive at decisions more organically than the current propose/accept flow. Contingent on E-1531 landing.

payload.title: Endless sessions must not actively use the file-based memory system (MEMORY.md auto-recall)
payload.description: Decision (Mike): Claude Code sessions must NOT actively use the file-based agent memory system — the per-project memory directory and its MEMORY.md index that Claude Code auto-loads and surfaces as recalled-memory system-reminders. Sessions must not create, update, or read memory files, and must treat recalled-memory reminders as inert background, never instructions. Rationale: actively using memories MASKS product and behavior defects that must instead be fixed at their source (CLI, hooks, guide); memory-sourced context also drives sessions off the rails on stale or wrong facts. Instead, capture corrections to ~/.claude/LESSONS.md as a write-only log for periodic human review — recording is fine, per-session use is not. Scope: global. Existing memory files are preserved intentionally, not deleted. Enforcement: global CLAUDE.md updated, and Claude Code auto-memory disabled via autoMemoryEnabled false. Reference this when a session goes off the rails relying on memory.

fields.analysis:
The gate ships an escape hatch (--allow-path) that the error names, so this false positive is workaround-able but still wrong — ordinary prose should not need an escape hatch.

Key reframing (Mike): 'kill the false positive so the escape hatch is never needed' is the ideal but is NOT achievable — deterministic detection cannot catch 100 percent of true positives without also producing some false positives, and vice versa. So the escape hatch is permanent and false positives will recur. The fix must therefore be MORE than tightening detection:
1. Fix the obvious safe wins (the bare-slash and bare-tilde cases) so common prose stops tripping.
2. Accept residual false positives as inevitable and make that path safe and correctly handled — e.g. error UX that makes the escape hatch the obvious next action, or a design where blocked content is never silently worked around. The observed failure was an agent degrading its own content to dodge the gate instead of using --allow-path; the design must make that wrong move hard and the right move easy.
Consider whether the escape-hatch flag needs a clearer name or behavior (a --allow-slash style affordance was floated), though step 1 removes the need for it in the common case.

fields.title: Add --status and --proposed filters to decision list for reviewing open decisions
fields.description: Interim, low-throwaway mechanism for periodically reviewing open/proposed decisions: add --status (e.g. proposed) and a --proposed shortcut to 'decision list'. Chosen over surfacing decisions in session status because decisions are moving back onto tasks (E-1861), which would make heavier session-status work throwaway. Lets the user run 'decision list --proposed' periodically to catch decisions still awaiting approve/modify/decline.

payload.title: Support recording global (cross-project) decisions in Endless
payload.description: Decisions are project-scoped: endless decision add requires a project and stores the decision under it, so a decision whose scope is genuinely global (applies to all projects and sessions) has no accurate home. Motivating case: ED-1541 states it is global but was necessarily filed under project 'endless', mislabeling its scope. Endless needs a way to record and surface global, cross-project decisions accurately (design open: a decision scope field, a reserved global project, or a separate global store). Surfaced by Mike.

payload.title: Explore task-relationship semantics: parent-child meaning by task type

payload.outcome:
# Task-relationship semantics — working agreement (2026-08-03)

Captured here (in a task outcome) rather than the decision table, because decisions
are moving back onto tasks (E-1861). This supersedes proposed decisions **ED-1517**
(relationship taxonomy) and **ED-1514** (bugfix diagnosis child), which are being
rejected in favor of this capture.

## Decided

- **Parent-child means different things by parent type:**
  - **Epic parent = containment.** An epic is never directly implemented; its
    completion derives entirely from its children's states; it has no deliverable
    of its own. (per accepted ED-1503)
  - **Non-epic parent (todo / research / bugfix / brainstorm) = grouping/provenance,
    NOT containment.** A non-epic parent may reach a terminal status while it still
    has incomplete children. The relationship is for grouping and lineage, not
    completion-derivation.
- **Open children must always surface** in "what to work on" views regardless of an
  ancestor's terminal status. This is a surfacing/filter requirement, not a modeling
  one — grouped children must never be hidden or lost behind a completed parent.
- **Consequences:**
  - `research → bugfix` as a child is legal and low-ceremony (research completes on
    findings; the fix is a grouped follow-up child that keeps surfacing). No epic
    wrapper required.
  - `bugfix → research(diagnosis)` child is also legal. Neither direction is
    mandated; ED-1514's prescription is subsumed by this general model (hence its
    rejection).
  - **Discriminator for "should this be an epic?":** does the parent have a
    deliverable of its own? Completion == sum of children with no parent-level
    deliverable → epic (container). Parent has its own standalone deliverable and
    merely has a subordinate child → legitimate non-epic-with-child.
- **Epic-ness is defined by container-ness, not size/duration.**

## Open (undecided)

- Exact surfacing/filter behavior for open descendants under a terminal-status
  parent — where it applies (session status, task next, list views) and how.
- Whether/how to add a promote-to-epic prompt/gate at `task add --parent` /
  `task move` when a child is added to a non-epic that has no deliverable of its own.
- Durable documentation home: epic + relationship semantics belong in `endless guide`
  (E-1545 covers the epic definition) — this outcome is interim capture, not the
  permanent home.
- Interaction with the decision-subsystem rework (E-1861): formalization rides that
  rework; until then this task-held capture is the working agreement.

payload.reason: Subsumed by the general task-relationship model captured in E-1863; ED-1514 over-prescribed (bugfix may have a diagnosis child, but that never precluded the inverse). Decisions moving to task content per E-1861.

payload.title: Add a way to revert a decision from accepted or rejected back to proposed
payload.description: There is currently no way to move a decision off a terminal status: 'decision update' has no --status flag, and there is no unaccept, unreject, or reopen command; 'decision reject' only works proposed to rejected. Add a way to revert accepted or rejected decisions back to proposed (e.g. a 'decision reopen' command, or a 'decision update --status' flag). Immediate need: ED-1517 was accidentally accepted and must be reverted so it can be rejected or superseded per E-1863. General need: an accidental accept or reject is otherwise irreversible.

fields.description: The working agreement on what task relationships mean by task type: an epic parent is containment (completion derives from its children), while a non-epic parent is grouping and provenance and may complete with open children that still surface for work. The outcome holds the decided model plus the open threads; supersedes proposed ED-1517 and ED-1514.

There is no way to move a decision off a terminal status: 'decision update' has no --status flag and there is no reopen command; 'decision reject' only works proposed to rejected. Add a 'decision reopen' command that reverts an accepted or rejected decision back to proposed, mirroring 'task reopen' and the existing dedicated-verb pattern for decision status changes (accept, reject). A 'decision update --status' flag was considered but rejected for consistency: status changes use dedicated verbs, not update. Immediate need: ED-1517 was accidentally accepted and must be reopened so it can then be rejected or superseded per E-1863. General: an accidental accept or reject is otherwise irreversible.

payload.title: Add `task unsettled` to explain why a worktree is unsettled (modified vs unlanded)
payload.description: The flat `session status` view marks a row unsettled with a bare ◆ but never says why, and the two sub-states need opposite fixes (modified means commit-or-discard, unlanded means land), so the user must run git by hand in the worktree to find out -- E-1537's worktree is the case that prompted this. Add `endless task unsettled [<id>]`, modeled on its inverse `task landed`: bare form lists every task whose worktree is unsettled with a one-line reason each; with an ID, print the full breakdown (which files are modified, auto-managed vs user work; how many commits ahead of main and which). Support --llm and --json. Named `unsettled` not `unlanded` because ED-1540 defines unsettled as the union (modified OR unlanded), so `unlanded` would name only one sub-state.
payload.analysis:
## Naming

`unsettled`, not `unlanded`. ED-1540 defines unsettled as the union (modified OR
unlanded); `unlanded` names only one of the two sub-states and would be actively
wrong for a worktree that is unsettled purely because of uncommitted changes.
Under `task` (4 chars) as requested, and it pairs with the existing `task landed`.

## The predicate already exists -- explain it, don't reimplement it

`taskWorktreeDirty` (internal/monitor/reap_worktrees.go:334) is what drives the ◆:

  1. `git -C <wt> status --porcelain` non-empty            -> modified
  2. else `git -C <wt> rev-list main..HEAD --count` > 0    -> unlanded
  3. no worktree, or any git error                         -> settled (fail-open)

It considers neither remote state nor the `task_landings` rows. The new command
must report these exact signals so the marker and its explanation cannot
disagree. Build it as a diagnostic over that predicate, not a second copy.

`AnnotateSessionStatusDirty` (reap_worktrees.go:316) is the fan-out; the reaper
inverts the same two signals at reap_worktrees.go:188-207 ("never reap unsettled").

## Reuse

- `internal/monitor/worktree_anomalies.go` -- finer-grained probes
  (`WorktreeAnomaliesAt`, line 91) already split user dirt from auto-managed via
  `AutoManagedStatusGlobs` (line 37). Read `.endless/plans/E-1758.md` before
  touching the anomaly core.
- `src/endless/worktree_cmd.py:637` `_git_status_partition` -- returns
  (auto_commit_files, user_work_files); the Python mirror of the same split.
- `src/endless/worktree_cmd.py:783` `_guard_dirty_worktree` -- land-time refusal
  with separate messages for auto-managed vs user dirt; same message shapes apply.

## Where the code goes

- Register in `src/endless/cli.py` immediately after `task_landed` (~line 1393),
  same decorator set (`item_id` optional TASK_ID, --project/--all/--limit/--llm/
  --json) and the same lazy `from endless.task_cmd import ...` inside the body.
- Implement `unsettled_list` / `unsettled_item` in `src/endless/task_cmd.py`
  alongside `landed_list` (line 1551) / `landed_item` (line 1635); mirror its
  three output modes (json / llm / human table).

## Sequencing risk

E-1825 ("Replace union-sense 'dirty' with 'unsettled'") is `unverified` and
renames exactly these identifiers across exactly these files. Either sequence
this after E-1825 lands or expect to touch the same symbols.

payload.title: Show creating session on task show Created: line, plus a Touched by: session list
payload.description: `task show` never reveals which session/active task created a task, nor which others touched it, so there is no path from a task back to the sessions that worked it -- and therefore no way to know what to pass to `session goto`. Add the creating session (and its active task) to the `Created:` line, and add a `Touched by:` section listing every session that touched the task, laid out like the existing `This task:` relations block so it reads as a peer. Each entry should carry enough identity (session id + its active task) to feed `session goto` directly. Surfacing these makes a task a navigational hub for jumping between the sessions that shaped it.

payload.title: Tasks can exist with an empty description; decide require-vs-backfill (found via E-1707)
payload.description: E-1707 has a complete plan in its Text field but a NULL/empty description, so `task show` renders no '— Description —' section at all and list views have only the title to work with. Since `task add` normally validates a description, some creation path (plan import, epic/child creation, or a direct DB write) is skipping it. Determine which path produces description-less tasks, then decide the fix: enforce a description at every creation path, backfill from the plan's opening section, or have `task show`/list views fall back to the plan's first meaningful line so the gap is invisible to readers. Audit for other affected rows while there -- E-1707 was found by chance, so the true count is unknown.

payload.title: Move decisions back onto tasks
payload.description: Reverts E-1511/E-1378 (decisions extracted into a dedicated decisions table). Returns decisions to being carried on tasks. The mechanism - storage shape, lifecycle, content model - is deliberately NOT locked here; a brainstorm child (E-1861) determines how, and implementation children emerge from it. Replaces E-1511.

fields.description: Maybe-phase tasks must not be children of EPICS. Rationale: an epic's status auto-derives from its children (E-1541); a maybe (uncommitted) child creates phantom scope - the epic can appear done while an uncommitted commitment lingers inside, and auto-derivation cannot safely treat a maybe child as part of the epic's outcome. NON-epic parents do NOT auto-derive and their open children always surface for work (per the E-1863 relationship model), so a maybe child under a non-epic parent creates no phantom scope and is allowed. Therefore phase=maybe with an EPIC parent must not coexist; maybe under a non-epic parent is permitted. Enforcement at the write path (task add/update). Supersedes the prior blanket 'maybe must be parentless' form. relates_to remains available. See E-1616 for validator + survey; enforcement-narrowing code tracked separately.

Make a settled decision reversible. Before this, 'decision accept' and 'decision reject' were one-way: 'decision update' has no --status flag and no reverse verb existed, so an accidental accept was permanent. Ships three verbs: 'decision unaccept' (accepted to proposed, guarded on 'accepted'), 'decision unreject' (rejected to proposed, guarded on 'rejected', and clears the stored rejection_reason), and 'decision reconsider' (dispatches to whichever applies, unguarded). Deliberately NOT named 'reopen': a decision is proposed and then accepted or rejected, so it is never 'open'. The guarded pair is the primary surface because each verb asserts the status you believe you are in, so aiming one at the wrong terminal status errors instead of silently performing the other reversal. Immediate need: ED-1517 was accidentally accepted and must be reverted so it can then be rejected or superseded per E-1863.

fields.title: Explore how decisions are carried on tasks and how they are arrived at
fields.description: Now that the direction is settled to move decisions back onto tasks (E-1868), this brainstorm determines HOW: the storage/content shape for decisions on tasks (candidate: a typed content item sibling to tasks.outcome, riding task_content E-1531), the decision lifecycle in that model, and how decisions are arrived at more organically than the current propose/accept flow.

payload.outcome: Direction reversed: decisions move back onto tasks (E-1868) rather than a dedicated table. E-1378/E-1507 shipped and remain under E-1511 as history; E-1389 rehomed and E-1383 relinked to E-1868. Superseded by E-1868.

payload.title: Decisions have no 'reopen' verb; each settled status is undone by its own inverse (unaccept / unreject)
payload.description: A decision is proposed and then accepted or rejected — it is never 'open', so 'reopen' (the task-tree verb) is a category error when applied to decisions. E-1864 ships 'decision unaccept' and 'decision unreject' as the primary surface: each names the status it undoes and refuses if the decision is not in that status, so aiming one at the wrong terminal status errors instead of silently performing the other reversal. 'decision reconsider' is the unguarded convenience for when you do not care which way the decision went. Reversing is for correcting the record (an accidental accept, a reject you want to re-argue); overturning a decision that was rightly settled is still better captured as a new decision linked with --type reverses.

payload.title: Change the maybe-phase parent enforcement to block only maybe children of epics
payload.description: Implements the revised ED-1510: maybe-phase tasks may now be children of NON-epic parents; only a maybe child of an EPIC is disallowed (epic auto-derivation would treat a maybe child as phantom scope). The write-path validation (task add and task update) currently blocks maybe with ANY parent - change it to check the parent's type and block only when the parent is an epic. Reconcile with E-1616 (validator plus survey of existing violations, e.g. E-1383's prior state).

payload.outcome: Duplicate — every aspect was already filed. Enforcement at the creation path: E-1820 (underway, event-emit choke point) and E-963 (CLI write-time). Display fallback for a NULL description: E-963 item (4). Backfill of existing description-less rows, which covers the audit: E-964 (unverified). E-1707 remains a live instance that E-964's backfill should catch. Filed without searching for prior art first.

payload.title: Guide never tells an agent to commit its work in the worktree before land
payload.description: docs/guide/orchestration.md walks a session from claim through 'Landing the work' with no step that says commit your work on the task branch. `worktree land` auto-commits only endless-managed files (verbs.jsonl, ledger entries), so an agent that follows the guide literally reaches land with its actual changes uncommitted and land moves nothing. This session did exactly that: it left E-1865 uncommitted because the behavior lived in a session memory rather than the product, and the guide gave it no directive. Add the commit step to the worktree walkthrough (before 'Landing the work'), and audit the guide for other conventions that currently survive only in agent memory rather than in `endless guide` -- each one is a rule that silently breaks for a fresh session.

fields.description: The ◆ unsettled marker and the dim-grey terminal-status styling contradict each other, and dim wins: a completed-but-unlanded row renders grey and reads as done, so the ◆ and the land it calls for are easily missed (hit live on E-1687). Change colorize() in internal/sessionstatuscmd/session_status.go to skip the dim styling when the row is Unsettled, so such rows render at normal weight and the marker stays visible.

payload.reason: This is a gratuitous filing because AI must feel like it accomplished a task rather than be good at reasoning about when a decision record is not needed.
This was written for all children when it should have been only for epic children. Rejected rather than reworded because we plan to file a revised decision later.

payload.title: session status renders a terminal-status row as ⁇ unknown when it is not landed/focal

fields.description: classify() in internal/sessionstatuscmd/session_status.go has no case for the terminal statuses (confirmed/assumed/declined/obsolete/completed), so such a row falls through to the default → actUnknown (⁇), and the legend then advertises '⁇ unknown' — the should-never-happen glyph — for an entirely ordinary row. Usually masked because a terminal task is also Landed → actLanded (⏚), but NOT when it is completed-but-unlanded, which is exactly the E-1707 shape: a non-focal 'completed' row with a diverged worktree renders '⁇ T◆E-NNN ✓ …'. Found while reproducing E-1707; scope-fenced out of it (E-1707 is color-only). Fix is likely a terminal case in classify() routing to its own action/glyph, or folding into actLanded — needs a call on which.

fields.title: Add the missing commit-your-work step to the guide's worktree walkthrough

payload.title: Document the commit-message convention (E-<id>: summary) in the guide
payload.description: Every task branch's commits ride into main via 'worktree land', and the de-facto convention in git history is 'E-<id>: <verb-first summary>' (e.g. b6dd933e 'E-1865: add `task unsettled` to explain the ◆ marker'). Nothing in `endless guide` states it, so a fresh session invents its own subject line. Found by the E-1870 guide audit.

payload.title: Document that a session must not land or drop without asking the user
payload.description: The handoff templates tell every spawned session "Don't run `endless worktree land`/`drop` without asking", but the guide's 'Landing the work' section says the opposite by omission: 'When the task is verified (or you're using assume): endless worktree land <id>'. The only trace of the rule in the guide is orchestration.md:284, a sentence *describing what the handoff template carries* — not a rule a session reading the Landing section would see. A session that re-reads the guide after a compaction will land unasked. Found by the E-1870 guide audit.

payload.title: Document the file-don't-fix convention for drive-by discoveries (--cleans-up)
payload.description: Handoffs tell sessions to file unrelated discoveries as new tasks with --cleans-up <id> and confirm before implementing, rather than fixing them inline. In the guide this exists only as orchestration.md:284 (describing the handoff's contents) and a bare flag mention in tasks.md:85's comment block. There is no prose rule, so a session working from the guide alone fixes drive-bys inline and inflates the diff. Found by the E-1870 guide audit.

payload.title: Document the FULL STATUS escape hatch in the guide
payload.description: The reporting contract's escape hatch — the user typing FULL STATUS licenses one unconstrained response, not a sticky mode — lives only in internal/templatecmd/templates/handoff/_close.tmpl. It appears nowhere in docs/guide/. A session whose context is compacted loses the keyword's meaning and either ignores it or treats it as a mode switch. Belongs alongside 'Reporting to your user' in the tasks section. Found by the E-1870 guide audit.

fields.description: Under `endless session status --all`, an ordinary done task renders with ⁇ — the renderer's should-never-happen glyph — and the legend then advertises '⁇ unknown', so a perfectly normal row reads as a bug in the tool. Cause: classify() (internal/sessionstatuscmd/session_status.go) has no case for the five terminal statuses (confirmed/assumed/declined/obsolete/completed), so any terminal row that is not focal/parent/from/in-flight and has never landed falls through to default → actUnknown. declined and obsolete tasks never land by definition, so they are ALWAYS ⁇. See the analysis for the reproduction, the classification decisions the fix needs, and an adjacent stale comment to fix with it.

fields.analysis:
## Symptom

In `endless session status --all`, an ordinary done task renders with the ⁇ glyph, and the
legend then advertises "⁇ unknown". ⁇ is the renderer's should-never-happen marker — the
comment on `actUnknown` says its appearance "flags an unhandled status slipping through" —
so it reads as a bug in the tool on a row that is in fact perfectly normal.

## Reproduce

Seed an epic with done children (one landed, one not) and render with `--all`:

```
● this  ⏚ landed  ⁇ unknown  ✓ done
● T E-900  1 the epic I am on
⏚ T E-905  ✓ child: confirmed AND landed
⏚ T E-907  1 child: ready AND landed
⁇ T E-901  ✓ child: confirmed, never landed
⁇ T E-902  ✓ child: declined
```

E-901 and E-902 are unremarkable — one confirmed, one declined — but both get the
"something is wrong here" glyph.

## Why

`classify()` (internal/sessionstatuscmd/session_status.go) switches on status and has NO
case for any of the five terminal statuses — `confirmed`, `assumed`, `declined`, `obsolete`,
`completed`. They fall through to `default:` → `actUnknown` (⁇).

A row hits this whenever ALL of these hold:
  - status is terminal, AND
  - it is not focal / parent / from / in-flight (those decorations are checked first and win), AND
  - it has no `task_landings` row (a landed task is caught one branch earlier → `actLanded` ⏚).

Terminal rows are filtered out of the view unless `--all` is passed, which is why this stays
hidden day to day. But under `--all` the affected set is not marginal:
  - `declined` and `obsolete` tasks never land by definition, so they are ALWAYS ⁇;
  - so is anything confirmed/assumed whose work never went through `worktree land`.

## Why it matters

⁇ is load-bearing as a diagnostic: it is supposed to mean "classify() met a status it does
not know about." Firing it on the most ordinary rows in the ledger destroys that signal —
a genuinely unhandled status would now be invisible in the noise.

## Decisions the fix needs

1. What should a terminal, non-landed row render as? Options: its own action + glyph
   (e.g. ✓/done, distinct from ⏚ landed), or fold into `actLanded` (wrong — "landed" and
   "done" are not the same claim, and ⏚ would then lie about a declined task), or a new
   `actDone`. Needs a call.
2. Whether `blocked` belongs in the same cleanup. `TestClassify` currently pins
   `Status: "blocked"` as the "unrecognized status is unknown" case, yet `blocked` is a
   documented status in the guide's status table — so the test encodes the same gap.
3. Sort rank: wherever the new action lands in the `action` enum determines where done rows
   sort under `--all` (`sortRows` ranks on the enum). Today they sort last, as ⁇.

## Adjacent (same change, trivial)

internal/monitor/session_status.go:36 still documents `Landed` as routing "a landed
non-terminal task to the catch-all ⁇ bucket". That has been wrong since E-1750 split ⁇ into
⏚ landed + ⁇ unknown; classify() returns `actLanded`. Fix the comment while in here.

## Provenance

Found while reproducing E-1707 (a non-focal `completed` + ◆ row rendered `⁇ T◆E-NNN ✓ …`),
and deliberately fenced out of it — E-1707 changed only dim/bold, never classification.
No test covers this: `TestClassify` has no terminal-status case, and `TestBuildLegend`'s
terminal case sets `IsFocal`, so it exits classify() at the first decoration and never
reaches the switch.

payload.title: Treat facts already enforced by a test, guard, or commit message as already reported
payload.description: Concrete rule for the E-1785 umbrella, drawn from a live violation in E-1865: the agent appended a 'two things worth your attention' section to a task report covering an invariant already guarded by a check in its verify script and a performance regression already fixed and covered by a test. Both facts were durably recorded where they belong; repeating them in prose made the user read the work twice. The rule: if a fact is enforced by a test, a guard, or the commit message, it is already reported and must not appear in user-facing output. Decide where this binds -- guide prose, the task report directive, or a check -- and how an agent distinguishes a discharged fact from a genuine open decision, which remains the one thing worth saying.

payload.title: Brainstorm how to keep session narration out of plans, descriptions, and titles
payload.description: Agent-authored durable content keeps carrying the session that produced it -- 'This session did exactly that', 'Found while auditing X during E-1834', titles that narrate a problem rather than state the work (E-1870 shipped as 'Guide never tells an agent...', which passed the title-verb gate only because 'Guide' collided with the allowlist as a noun). The artifacts are read later by people and sessions with no memory of the authoring session, so narration is noise at best and misleading at worst, while genuine provenance still has value and should not be blanket-banned. Brainstorm where the line sits, whether it differs by field (title vs description vs plan vs outcome), and what could enforce it -- a gate, a linter, a guide rule, or a rewrite pass -- including whether provenance belongs in a dedicated field instead of prose.

fields.description: docs/guide/orchestration.md walks a session from claim through 'Landing the work' with no step directing it to commit its work on the task branch. `worktree land` auto-commits only endless-managed files (verbs.jsonl, ledger entries), so a session that follows the guide literally reaches land with its actual changes uncommitted and land moves nothing. Add the commit step to the worktree walkthrough before 'Landing the work', and audit the guide for other conventions that currently survive only in agent memory rather than in `endless guide` -- each is a rule that silently stops holding for a session without that memory.

fields.text:
# Add the missing commit-your-work step to the guide's worktree walkthrough

## Problem

`docs/guide/orchestration.md` takes a session from `task claim` (§ Auto-creation
on claim) through `§ Landing the work` without ever saying **commit your work**.

`worktree land` auto-commits only endless-managed files:

> 1. Auto-commits endless-managed modifications (verbs.jsonl, ledger entries)

A session's own code, tests, and docs are not in that set. So a session that
follows the guide literally arrives at `worktree land` with its changes
uncommitted, and the land moves nothing — the rebase and fast-forward carry only
the ledger churn.

The step has been happening anyway because sessions carried it as a habit. When
that habit is absent, nothing in the product supplies it.

## Change

### 1. The commit step

Add a subsection to `docs/guide/orchestration.md` between `§ Inspecting` /
`§ Why a worktree is unsettled` and `§ Landing the work` — it must land *before*
the land instructions, since that is the order the reader executes.

Content requirements:

- **Commit on the task branch as you work.** Not a single commit at the end;
  the branch is the reviewable unit and lands as a group of commits.
- **`worktree land` does not commit your work for you** — state the asymmetry
  explicitly and point at the auto-commit list so the exception is legible.
- **Uncommitted work at land time is a no-op land**, which is the failure this
  section exists to prevent. Point at `endless task unsettled <id>` (E-1865),
  which reports `modified` precisely when this is about to happen.
- Do **not** restate the commit-to-main policy (`§ Commit-to-main policy`
  already owns it) — link to it instead.

### 2. The audit

Sweep the guide for other conventions that currently live only in agent memory.
Method: for each step a session performs between `claim` and `land`, ask "does
`endless guide` state this, or has it merely been habitual?" Known candidates to
check (not a closed list):

- committing (this task)
- when to run the project-wide regression vs the per-task verify suite
- whether to update the plan file as the work diverges from it
- what to do with drive-by findings mid-task (`--cleans-up`)

File a task per genuine gap found rather than expanding this one — the audit's
output is a list, and each entry is its own change.

## Verification

`tests/tasks/e-1870-verify.sh`:

1. The commit subsection exists in `orchestration.md` and appears **before** the
   `### Landing the work` heading (assert on line-number ordering, not just
   presence — placement is the point).
2. It names `worktree land`'s non-committing of user work.
3. `just guide-check` exits 0 (the map still resolves; add a `help/` entry only
   if a new section slug was introduced).
4. The audit's findings are filed as tasks, or the section records that none
   were found.

## Notes

- Guide-only change; no code, no schema.
- The related agent-output-discipline work (E-1785 and children) is about what a
  session *says*; this is about what the guide *tells it to do*. Distinct.

payload.title: Skip Go rebuild in endless worktree land when only .endless metadata files changed
payload.description: For epic-shaped worktrees whose commits are purely .endless/ metadata files (plans, analyses, ledger entries), the pre-land Go build in 'just land' (which calls 'just go') is dead weight — it doesn't verify anything that changed. Detect 'no non-.endless files touched between main and branch HEAD' and skip the rebuild step. Belongs on 'endless worktree land' since 'just land' is thin infra around it. Surfaced 2026-06-29 when 'just land E-1537' (epic-shaped) failed the rebuild step because 'just go-work-init' hadn't been re-run in the worktree; the build was unnecessary since the commits were all .endless/ metadata.

payload.title: Add task annotate as the agent's write-only observation sink, hidden by default
payload.description: Agents narrate discharged facts into chat partly because displaced observations have no destination. Project notes are not that destination -- they are project-scoped, have found no good use since being added, and are likely to be deprecated. Add `endless task annotate <id> "..."`: task-scoped, append-only, write-only by design, and hidden from the default `task show` -- surfaced only under `task show --annotations`, so the sink never relocates noise to where the user already reads. This is the CAPTURE half of a pair; E-1803 owns ENFORCEMENT (task report as the mandated channel plus a PostToolUse nudge). Neither half works alone: a sink without the gate yields annotate-and-narrate, giving the user a third place to read, while the gate without a sink forces the agent to either drop genuine observations or smuggle them into prose. E-1865 is the evidence that a destination alone is insufficient -- every fact narrated there already had a durable home.

fields.title: Document the guide's memory-only conventions in one pass
fields.description: Five conventions sessions are expected to follow that appear nowhere in `endless guide`: the commit-message form, don't-land-without-asking, file-don't-fix for drive-bys, the FULL STATUS escape hatch, and the lean-toward-fewer-tasks rule. Same class of gap as E-1870. All are docs/guide/ edits, so one review rather than five. Consolidates E-1873/1874/1875.
fields.text:
# E-1872 — Document the guide's memory-only conventions in one pass

Consolidates E-1873, E-1874, E-1875 (obsoleted into this task) and adds the
task-proliferation rule.

Each item below is a convention a session is expected to follow that appears
nowhere in `endless guide`, so it silently breaks for a fresh session — the same
class of gap E-1870 fixed for the commit step. All five are edits to
`docs/guide/`, so they are **one** review, not five.

## The gaps

### 1. Commit-message convention

Branch commits ride into `main` via `worktree land`, and git history's de-facto
form is `E-<id>: <verb-first summary>` (e.g. `b6dd933e`, `fd28a75d`). Nothing in
the guide states it, so every session invents its own subject line.

**Where:** `orchestration.md`, in the "Committing your work" section E-1870 added.

### 2. Do not land or drop without asking

Every handoff template carries "Don't run `endless worktree land`/`drop` without
asking." The guide's "Landing the work" section says the opposite by omission:
"When the task is verified (or you're using `assume`): `endless worktree land
<id>`." The only trace in the guide is `orchestration.md:284` — a sentence
*describing what the handoff template carries*, not a rule a session reading the
Landing section would ever see. A session that re-reads the guide after a context
compaction will land unasked.

**Where:** `orchestration.md`, "Landing the work" — as a rule, not a description
of a template.

### 3. File-don't-fix for drive-by discoveries (`--cleans-up`)

Exists only as `orchestration.md:284` and a bare flag mention in `tasks.md:85`'s
comment block. There is no prose rule, so a session working from the guide alone
fixes drive-bys inline and inflates the diff.

**Where:** `tasks.md`, alongside the relation flags.

### 4. `FULL STATUS` escape hatch

Lives only in `internal/templatecmd/templates/handoff/_close.tmpl`: the user
typing `FULL STATUS` licenses **one** unconstrained response, not a sticky mode.
Absent from `docs/guide/` entirely, so a session whose context is compacted
either ignores the keyword or misreads it as a mode switch.

**Where:** `tasks.md`, alongside "Reporting to your user".

### 5. Lean toward FEWER tasks — user directive, 2026-08-04

When filing discovered work, prefer **one** task over several whenever one is
reasonable.

Every filed task costs the user review, prioritization, and scheduling attention.
Five tasks cost roughly **3x** the attention of one task covering the same
ground. Endless exists to **save** the user time, not to manufacture busy work —
for this user or for any downstream Endless user.

Split into separate tasks only when the items genuinely need different reviewers,
different decisions, or different land timing. Same file + same kind of edit +
same reviewer = one task.

This session's own E-1872..E-1875 — four near-identical "document X in the guide"
items — is the anti-pattern. Folding them into this one task is the pattern.

**Where:** `tasks.md`, in the section covering `task add` / filing discovered
work. This one is load-bearing enough to state as a rule with the cost rationale
attached, not a passing aside — an agent that does not know *why* will re-split.

## Verification

`tests/tasks/e-1872-verify.sh` — for each of the five, assert the rule is present
in the rendered `endless guide <section>` output (not merely on disk), and that
the `land`-without-asking rule sits inside the "Landing the work" section rather
than in the handoff-template description. Fold in `tests/test_guide_map.py` and
`just guide-check` as the fail-fast first check.

fields.text:
# `endless task report` contradicts the handoff contract it serves

Observed live at the E-1870 handoff. Two defects, both in
`src/endless/report_cmd.py::_render_facts` (lines ~246-262).

## Defect 1 — the report emits what the handoff forbids

The handoff close (`internal/templatecmd/templates/handoff/_close.tmpl`) tells
every spawned session two things at once:

- "run `endless task report <id>` and relay its output **verbatim**"
- "Do NOT recap task **status**, phase, or **relationships**"

`_render_facts` unconditionally emits `Task: E-NNNN`, `Status: <status>`, and the
relationship rows (`Follow-ups you filed:`, `Children:`) — and the report's own
header says "add nothing else."

So the two contracts are in direct conflict and the session cannot satisfy both.
Whichever it picks, it is disobeying an instruction. On E-1870 the session obeyed
the tool and printed a status recap the user had explicitly asked not to receive.

This matters beyond one bad handoff: the whole point of routing reports through
the command is that the command is the authority on what is worth saying. Right
now the command's output *is* the noise the contract exists to suppress.

**Fix direction:** decide which surface is authoritative and make the other
agree. Most likely the command should stop emitting `Task:`/`Status:` (the user
already knows both — `session status` renders them, and the status flip *is* the
contract), leaving the report to carry only what the user could not already know:
notes, questions, anomalies, and genuinely new follow-ups.

## Defect 2 — the same IDs print twice under two labels

`successors` (the `cleans_up` relation) and `children` (the parent link) are
computed independently and rendered as separate lines. A task filed with both
`--parent E-N --cleans-up E-N` — the exact pattern every handoff instructs a
session to use for drive-by discoveries — lands in **both** lists.

Actual E-1870 output:

```
Follow-ups you filed: E-1872 [unplanned], E-1873 [unplanned], E-1874 [unplanned], E-1875 [unplanned]
Children: E-1872 [unplanned], E-1873 [unplanned], E-1874 [unplanned], E-1875 [unplanned]
```

Identical sets, twice, because the documented way to file a follow-up produces
both relations. This is not a usage error — it is the recommended usage.

**Fix direction:** dedupe across the two lists; when an item is both, render it
once under the more informative label (`Follow-ups you filed:`).

## Verification

`tests/tasks/e-1876-verify.sh`: build a task with children that are also
`cleans_up` successors, render the report, and assert (a) each ID appears exactly
once, and (b) whatever the resolved policy is for `Status:` holds. Fold in the
`report_cmd` unit tests as the fail-fast first check.

# Route closed tasks to ⇥ instead of ⁇

## Why

Under `endless session status --all`, an ordinary done task renders with `⁇` — the glyph
`classify()` reserves for "a status slipped through unhandled" — and the legend then
advertises `⁇ unknown` for a perfectly normal row. `declined` and `obsolete` tasks never
land, so they hit this **always**; so does anything confirmed/assumed whose work never went
through `worktree land`.

The cost is not cosmetic: `⁇` is load-bearing as a diagnostic. Firing it on the most ordinary
rows in the ledger means a genuinely unhandled status would be invisible in the noise.

See this task's `--analysis` for the reproduction and the full derivation.

## Design (settled — do not re-litigate)

**New action `actDone`, glyph `⇥` (U+21E5 RIGHTWARDS ARROW TO BAR), label `closed`.**
Measured at display width 1 with `go-runewidth`, same as every other glyph in the table, so
the fixed 13-column prefix and its alignment are unaffected. "Arrow to bar" reads as a
terminus, which is what a terminal status is, and it is visually distinct from `▶ do` and
`↩ from`.

**Column 1 stays a verb column.** `✓` was considered and rejected: the phase column (column 4)
already renders `✓` for every terminal status, so `✓` in column 1 would state the same fact
twice. Blank was also considered and rejected — a row with no glyph reads as a rendering
failure rather than a classification.

**`⏚` wins over `⇥`.** A row that is both landed and terminal renders `⏚ landed`. This needs
NO reordering: `classify()` already checks `r.Landed` before the status switch, so adding the
terminal case to the switch delivers this for free. `⇥` therefore appears only on a closed
task whose work never merged — which is the informative case. Pin it with a test so a future
refactor cannot silently swap the precedence.

**Decorations still win over both.** `IsFocal`/`IsParent`/`IsFrom`/`InFlight` are checked
first, so a done parent keeps `↑`. Unchanged; just make sure the new cases do not disturb it.

**Enum position: append `actDone` AFTER `actUnknown`.** Enum order is both legend order and
sort rank (`sortRows` ranks on the enum), so appending leaves every existing rank untouched —
the same trick E-1750 used when it added `actUnknown`. The resulting order is deliberate:
closed rows sort last under `--all`, below the `⁇` anomaly rows, which is right — an
unhandled status deserves more prominence than a finished task.

**Legend reads `⇥ closed` AND keeps `✓ done`.** They are not redundant: `✓` is the phase-column
marker and still appears on *decorated* done rows (a focal, parent, or landed task can be
terminal), where column 1 shows `●`/`↑`/`⏚` rather than `⇥`. Two entries, deliberately.

## Change

All of it is in `internal/sessionstatuscmd/session_status.go` (the action enum is not consumed
anywhere else — `tree.go` takes a separate render path):

1. Add `actDone` to the `action` const block, after `actUnknown`, with a comment explaining
   the append-don't-insert rule and the `⏚`-wins precedence.
2. Add `actDone: {"⇥", "closed"}` to `actionMeta`. `buildLegend` iterates `actionMeta` by
   index, so the legend picks it up with no further change.
3. In `classify()`'s status switch, route terminal statuses to `actDone` by calling the
   existing `isTerminal(r.Status)` helper — do NOT re-list the five statuses inline, or the
   list and `isTerminal` will drift. A `switch` case cannot call a function, so this goes in
   as an `if isTerminal(r.Status) { return actDone }` immediately before the `switch r.Status`
   (after the `r.Landed` check, which must keep winning).

Adjacent, trivial, same change: `internal/monitor/session_status.go:36` still documents
`Landed` as routing "a landed non-terminal task to the catch-all ⁇ bucket". That has been
wrong since E-1750 split `⁇` into `⏚ landed` + `⁇ unknown`; `classify()` returns `actLanded`.
Fix the comment.

## Explicitly out of scope

`TestClassify` pins `Status: "blocked"` as its "unrecognized status is unknown" case, while
the guide's status table documents `blocked` as a real status (and the lifecycle diagram says
blocking is a relation, not a state). That contradiction is a separate question about whether
the status exists at all — it is NOT a terminal status and does not belong in this change.
Leave the test case as-is. Captured in this task's `--analysis` under Decisions #2; do not
file a new task for it without asking.

## Verify

Add `tests/tasks/e-1871-verify.sh`, modeled on `tests/tasks/e-1707-verify.sh` (same harness:
build → the rule's own unit tests as a fail-fast gate → full suites → end-to-end against a
seeded temp DB). Fold this task's tests into that one script; hand the user exactly one
command.

Unit tests in `internal/sessionstatuscmd/session_status_test.go`:

- `TestClassify`: each of the five terminal statuses (`confirmed`, `assumed`, `declined`,
  `obsolete`, `completed`) → `actDone`.
- `TestClassify`: terminal + `Landed: true` → `actLanded` (⏚ wins — the precedence pin).
- `TestClassify`: terminal + `IsFocal` → `actThis`, terminal + `IsParent` → `actParent`
  (decorations still win).
- `TestClassify`: no terminal status yields `actUnknown` any more.
- `TestActionIcons`: `actDone` → `⇥`, and `displayWidth("⇥") == 1`.
- `TestBuildLegend`: an undecorated terminal, unlanded row yields BOTH `⇥ closed` and
  `✓ done`, and NOT `⁇ unknown`; a terminal *landed* row yields `⏚ landed` + `✓ done` and
  NOT `⇥ closed`.
- `TestSortRows`: a closed row sorts after an `actUnknown` row and after every open row.

End-to-end through the worktree binary, against a temp DB seeded from
`internal/schema/schema.sql` (see e-1707-verify.sh §4 for the exact fixture pattern —
an epic with children, rendered with `--task <epic> --all`, plus a `task_landings` row to
drive the landed case; note the column is `merge_commit_sha`, not `landed_sha`):

- a `confirmed` child with no landing renders `⇥`, and `⁇` appears nowhere in the output;
- a `confirmed` child WITH a `task_landings` row still renders `⏚`;
- a `declined` and an `obsolete` child both render `⇥`;
- the legend line contains `⇥ closed` and `✓ done` and not `⁇ unknown`;
- the id column does not shift (glyph is width 1).

Run the project-wide regression before handing off: `just build`, `just test-go`, `just test`,
`just guide-check`.

payload.title: Add continuous auto-merge job for endless-managed worktree commits into main on E-698 runner
payload.description: Prevent long-lived worktrees from drifting from main on endless-managed metadata files. A job (running on E-698's fire-once runner) periodically syncs endless-auto commits (touching only .endless/plans, .endless/analyses, .endless/db-ledger) from each live worktree branch to main. Strict scoping: never touches code, tests, or non-.endless files — those remain gated by the normal land workflow. Continuous invocation shrinks the concurrent-append window for ledger shards, so out-of-order ordering risk is small but non-zero. Complements E-NNNN (reconcile) — reconcile fixes drift after it happens; this prevents drift from accumulating. Surfaced 2026-06-29 during E-1537 land.

payload.title: Add endless worktree reconcile to resolve stale endless-managed commits
payload.description: Detects and resolves the scenario where a long-lived worktree accumulates endless-generated commits (plan/analysis/ledger updates) that overlap or are superseded by main's independent updates, causing 'just land' to hit rebase conflicts. Classifies each unlanded commit by files touched: (a) endless-managed metadata (.endless/plans, .endless/analyses, .endless/db-ledger) that match or are superseded on main → safe to drop, (b) endless-managed metadata with genuinely unique branch content → preserve with clear per-file explanation, (c) any non-endless-managed file → bail out (real work that needs land, not reconcile). Output should tell the operator exactly what would happen before doing anything destructive. Invocable standalone as 'endless worktree reconcile <id>' or as a --reconcile fallback flag on 'endless worktree land'. Surfaced 2026-06-29 during E-1537 land which took ~20min of manual investigation to arrive at 'reset --hard main is safe'.

fields.title: Define the discharged-fact test for what agent output may leave unsaid
fields.description: Sharpen one half of E-1803's acceptable-output test. E-1803 defines acceptable agent output functionally -- a computed fact the user cannot derive, or a genuine open decision, and nothing else -- and owns enforcement (task report as the mandated channel plus a PostToolUse nudge). What it does not pin down is when a fact counts as ALREADY reported. Proposed rule: a fact recorded in a test, a guard, a verify script, a commit message, or a task field is discharged and must not appear in user-facing output -- including when the agent introduced the problem and then fixed it, where the fix is the record and there is nothing left for the user to decide. Deliverable is a test an agent can actually apply, plus the boundary against a genuine open decision, which stays worth saying. Enforcement is out of scope: this defines the rule E-1803 enforces. Evidence from E-1865, where an invariant already guarded by its verify script and a regression already covered by a test were both narrated anyway.

payload.title: Decide how to scope Endless databases so a db-ledger rebuild is project-safe
payload.description: db-ledger is PROJECT-scoped (lives at <project>/.endless/db-ledger, designed so the DB can be rebuilt from it), but ~/.config/endless/endless.db is MACHINE-global across ALL registered projects. So rebuilding from one project's ledger loses every other project's data: the rebuild guarantee only holds on a single-project machine. Raised by Mike 2026-08-04 during E-698. Apparent direction is splitting into a machine DB plus one DB per project, but this is deliberately open — brainstorm options before locking anything in.
payload.analysis:
# Context

Raised by Mike on 2026-08-04 during E-698 (fire-once job runner), while
discussing why `session monitor` inside a self-dev worktree is pinned to the
real `~/.config/endless/endless.db`.

## The flaw

- `db-ledger` is **project-scoped**: it lives at `<project>/.endless/db-ledger`,
  is committed to that project's repo, and is designed so the Endless DB can be
  rebuilt from it.
- `~/.config/endless/endless.db` is **machine-global**: one SQLite file holding
  every registered project's tasks, decisions, events, landings — plus
  machine-local state (sessions, panes, worktree locks).

So the rebuild guarantee does not actually hold. Rebuilding the DB from project
A's ledger reconstructs A's rows and **loses every other project's data**. The
guarantee is only true on a single-project machine.

## Options to weigh (nothing decided)

1. **Split the databases.** One machine-local DB (sessions, panes, machine
   state) + one DB per project (tasks, decisions, events, landings). A project's
   ledger then rebuilds exactly its own DB and nothing else. Cleanest mapping of
   ledger scope to DB scope; biggest change (every query, the `--db` context
   machinery, cross-project views like `session status`).
2. **Project-scoped rebuild.** Keep one DB; make rebuild surgical — replace only
   the rows belonging to the project being rebuilt, inside a transaction.
   Smallest change; leaves the scope mismatch in place and every rebuild is a
   delicate partial write.
3. **Machine-global ledger alongside the per-project ones.** A second ledger for
   machine-scoped rows so the machine DB is itself rebuildable. Complements 1 or
   2 rather than replacing them.
4. **ATTACH per project.** One file per project, attached on demand, so
   cross-project queries still work with `project.tasks` qualification.
5. **Do nothing; document the limitation.** Rebuild is declared single-project
   only, and cross-project machines are told to back up instead.

## Constraints to respect

- The self-dev sandbox (E-1281) and the `--db main|sandbox` context threading
  (E-1429) both assume a single DB path resolved from `ConfigDir()`. Any split
  has to keep that seam coherent.
- `session status` / `session monitor` deliberately read machine-global session
  state regardless of cwd (`PinMainDB`, E-1450/E-1685). Splitting must not
  break that.
- Cross-project reads exist today (`endless project list/status`, the web
  dashboard).

## Not yet decided

Mike explicitly wants to brainstorm options before anything is locked in. Do not
implement from this text.

payload.title: Convert the 42 log.Printf call sites to the E-698 fault system
payload.description: Go code writes diagnostics with log.Printf to stderr: hookcmd 23, monitor 11, schema 5, channelcmd 3. Once session monitor fires the E-698 job runner in-process, any stderr write lands on top of the dashboard's stdout frame painting, and because monitorLoop only repaints when the frame content changes, the corruption persists until the next change rather than being cleaned up on the next tick. E-698 contains this at its own seam by swapping the standard logger to a sink while jobs run; this task routes the pre-existing call sites into the faults table so they get a code, a severity, and a clearable record instead of scribbling on the terminal.
