fields.text:
# E-1892 — `session monitor` re-resolves its focal task until one appears

## Scope

`internal/sessionstatuscmd` only. The monitor's resolution lifecycle — nothing
about rendering, sizing, or the layout E-1851 builds.

## Decision: re-anchor the WHOLE set, freeze on the first focal hit

Re-resolve `focal`, `parentSession` and `emittingSession` together on each tick
while `focal == 0`; stop re-resolving the moment `focal != 0`.

All three are read from the same not-yet-settled state and share one race:
`parentSession` comes from the `@endless_spawned_by` window option, which
`spawn-launch` writes immediately before its `syscall.Exec` — the same instant
the session row does not yet exist. `emittingSession` is consulted only while
`focal == 0`, so freezing it at a stale 0 would leave the no-goal view (E-1802)
permanently empty for exactly the sessions it exists to serve.

Freezing on `focal != 0` preserves E-1698's anchor-once contract unchanged: once
a task is anchored the view stays pinned to THIS window's task as other sessions
come and go. Nothing re-resolves after that point. A session that never claims
keeps re-resolving every 2s, which is correct — that is how the view recovers
when the user finally claims.

## Mechanism

`Run` currently resolves once and passes three values into `monitorLoop`. Change
it to pass an *anchor function* that returns the triple, and have `monitorLoop`
call it each tick until focal is non-zero:

    type anchor struct{ focal, parentSession, emittingSession int64; hint string }

    // seamed as a package var so tests drive the sequence, mirroring the
    // existing `worktreeAnomalies` seam in this same file
    var resolveAnchor = func(pane string) (anchor, error) { ... }

`Run`'s existing `--task` / `--session` headless branches keep their fixed
anchors (they name the focal directly, so there is nothing to wait for) — those
call `monitorLoop` with an anchor func that returns a constant.

### Required for testability: honor an explicit `--config-dir`

`sessionstatuscmd.Run` calls `monitor.PinMainDB()` unconditionally on the normal
(pane-resolved) path, so `--config-dir` cannot redirect it and the pane→session
resolution cannot be exercised against a seeded DB — which is precisely what
this task needs to test. Gate it the way `cmd/endless-go/main.go` already gates
the same pin for `hook`/`channel`/`tmux`:

    if !monitor.HasExplicitDBContext() && !monitor.InSelfDevWorktree() {
        monitor.PinMainDB()
    }

A per-invocation flag is trustworthy; the env-driven pin is the fallback
(E-1429). Production invokers pass no `--config-dir`, so real traffic still
pins main. This only widens what tests can reach.

## Tests — `tests/tasks/e-1892-verify.sh`

One suite, task's own checks fail-fast first, then project-wide regression.

**Layer A — unit, FAIL-FAST** (`internal/sessionstatuscmd`)
- Drive `resolveAnchor` through the seam with a scripted sequence — returns
  `focal=0` three times, then `focal=1851` — and assert `monitorLoop` picks up
  1851 and renders its rows.
- Assert it STOPS calling the resolver after the first hit: the seam counts
  calls; the count must not advance across subsequent ticks.
- Assert `parentSession`/`emittingSession` update on the same tick focal does,
  not one tick later.

fields.title: Add untriaged status upstream of unplanned and wire the lifecycle
fields.text:
# E-1845 — Add `untriaged` status upstream of `unplanned`

**Shipped.** Prerequisite for E-1859 (the description-sufficiency triager),
which unblocks the moment this lands.

`tasks.status` is plain TEXT validated in application code (schema.sql carries
no CHECK constraints and there is no status enum table), so this was a code +
docs change with **no migration and no backfill**. Existing rows keep their
current status; only newly filed tasks start at `untriaged`.

## Decisions settled during implementation

**1. Named `untriaged`, not `unevaluated`.** The docs had provisionally used
`unevaluated`; Mike renamed it at implementation time. "Triage" is the
better-known word for the gate where incoming work gets looked at before it
enters the real queue — a reader knows what `untriaged` means without being
told. The four doc files, this task, and E-1859's description were renamed to
match. The mermaid transition labels read "triage routes (…)", naming the act
rather than a component, so E-1859 is free to name its job whatever it likes.

**2. No shipping deadlock — the manual route is the duplicated slice.**
`untriaged` is in `_SUBMITTABLE_FROM`, so a human can route with
`endless task submit` before E-1859 exists. That overlap is deliberate and
permanent: it is the human override for a triage call you disagree with, not
scaffolding to remove. Section C of the verify script pins it.

**3. Description-edit reset fires from pre-work statuses only, on a material
change.**

| Fires from | Never fires from |
|---|---|
| `untriaged`, `unplanned`, `submitted`, `ready`, `revisit` | `underway`, `unverified`, `confirmed`, `assumed`, `completed`, `declined`, `obsolete` |

Guards mirror E-1762's auto-revisit: identical rewrites no-op, `--keep-status`
suppresses, an explicit `--status` wins. `ready` IS included (approval was
granted against the old description); `underway` is excluded so an edit cannot
yank work out from under a live session.

**Composition, discovered in test:** re-spec + plan-attach in the SAME call
lands `submitted`, not `untriaged` — a task carrying a full plan must not read
as "nobody has looked at this". This is resolved in Python, because the
executor's plan-attach auto-move only fires when the update does not set status
explicitly, and the reset does set it. A `ready` task still loses its approval
this way, landing `submitted` for re-approval — correct.

**4. `task next` OMITS it** (Mike's call). The original plan said "rank after
revisit", which contradicted its own verification check 6. `task next` has been
largely superseded by `session status` and may be deprecated later; omitting is
the simpler, consistent answer. The tree backlog and the web "next actions"
widget omit it for the same reason. An untriaged task still **blocks** its
dependents — unfinished work is unfinished whether or not it was looked at.

**5. Epic derivation gains its own rung** (below `unplanned`). Without it, an
epic whose children are all freshly filed matches no bucket and is left
unchanged — the common case now that `untriaged` is the default, not an edge
one.

**6. `schema.sql`'s column DEFAULT stays `'unplanned'`** (Mike's call). Changing
a SQLite column default requires a table rebuild, which the no-migration
constraint rules out. Every insert path supplies status explicitly, so the
default is dead code. Align it whenever `tasks` is next rebuilt.

## Sites changed

### Python
- `cli.py` — `TASK_STATUSES` (feeds five `click.Choice`/`MultiChoice` option
  types for free); `--status` help strings.
- `task_cmd.py` — `add_item` default; `_SUBMITTABLE_FROM`; `update_plan`'s
  `valid` tuple; `next_tasks` WHERE exclusion; tree glyph `◌`; tier-1
  auto-advance; `_CHILDREN_STATE_ORDER`; the new `_DESCRIPTION_RESET_FROM` +
  reset logic beside E-1762's auto-revisit.
- `session_status_cmd.py` — `_VALID_STATUSES`.

### Go — beyond the original plan's site list
Three sites the plan did not name would have broken:
- `events/executor.go` — the plan-attach auto-move was gated on `unplanned`, so
  `task add --text plan.md` would have filed a fully planned task as untriaged
  and stranded it. Extracted `isPreJudgmentStatus` for both call sites.
- `events/epic_derivation.go` — the new rung (decision 5).
- `monitor/session.go` — claim promotes `untriaged` → `underway`, else a
  claimed task reads untouched while someone is actively on it.

Also: `events/session_status.go` (Pending disposition), `monitor/task.go`
(`GetActiveTasks`), `web/handlers.go`, `web/queries.go`, both templ pages.

### Go — `sessionstatuscmd`
New `actTriage` **appended** to the enum (enum order is legend order and
`sortRows`' rank, so appending leaves every existing rank untouched), glyph `◌`
(single-width, asserted), label `triage`. `classify()` gains an explicit
`case "untriaged"` — load-bearing, since falling through to `actUnknown` would
paint `⁇` (the should-never-happen marker) on the most common row in the ledger.
It is deliberately NOT `actPlan`: "needs a plan" is a judgment nobody has made
yet, and that distinction is the entire reason the status exists.

### Docs
`docs/status-lifecycle.mmd` is canonical; the three embedded copies were
re-synced byte-identically. The prose status table in `docs/guide/index.md`
gained an `untriaged` row, and both it and `CLAUDE.md` now document the
description-edit reset and `--keep-status`.

## Adjacent pre-existing bugs found (filed, not fixed inline)
- **E-1888** — `submitted` missing from `_CHILDREN_STATE_ORDER`, so a submitted
  child is counted in the total but never rendered as a bucket.
- **E-1891** — `task update --status submitted` is rejected as invalid; the
  `valid` tuple duplicates `cli.TASK_STATUSES` and has drifted from it.
- **E-1894** — `tests/tasks/*-verify.sh` rot silently. `e-1648-verify.sh` was
  dead (called `endless register`, renamed to `project register`, so it exited 2
  at setup) and carried an assertion E-1765 superseded. Both fixed here because
  this task's rename touched the file.

## Verification
`tests/tasks/e-1845-verify.sh` — 63 checks, fail-fast (section A runs the Go +
Python unit tests first and aborts the run if they fail). Sections B–J cover the
add default, the no-deadlock guarantee, the description-edit reset and all three
guards, the `◌ triage` render on a non-focal row, `task next` omission with
blocking retained, epic derivation, doc sync + prose, cross-surface
registration, and a project-wide regression.

fields.description: New status untriaged, upstream of unplanned. task add defaults new tasks here unless a status is given explicitly; a material description edit resets a pre-work task to untriaged. Transitions: untriaged -> unplanned or untriaged -> submitted (set by triage). session status renders it as its own action (untriaged, never 'needs a plan'); task next omits it as not-actionable. Touches the canonical status lifecycle (ED-1529). Prerequisite for the triager job.

The bespoke job that registers with the E-698 fire-once runner. For each untriaged task it assembles the persisted-artifact context (description + parent + sibling titles + linked decisions — deliberately NOT the filing session's context) and calls a model via the shared run_internal_claude helper with a config-resolved model (standardize the config key so verb auto-registration and this job resolve their model the same way; do not hardcode 'claude -p'; see E-1849 for making the harness itself pluggable). It then sets status to submitted or unplanned and emits the transition as an event with triager attribution. Runs as belt (inline at file time) and suspenders (background sweep over the untriaged queue).

Container for the feature that removes the manual submit-vs-plan judgment: new tasks land in untriaged and triage routes each to submitted (description is a sufficient spec) or unplanned (needs a planning session), with status — not complexity/risk — routing the workflow. Completion derives from its children (the untriaged status wiring E-1845 and the triager job E-1859); the opt-out E-1847 is a related maybe. Rides the E-698 fire-once runner; orthogonal to auto-spawn (E-1812), which shares only that runner.

Optional per-task flag/field marking a task as hands-off for the description-sufficiency triager (E-1844), for the rare 'AI, don't touch this one' case. The untriaged status already handles the common exclusions (anything a human has moved is out of the queue by construction), so this is only the explicit exception. Deferred to maybe pending evidence it's needed.

# Analysis — `session monitor` never recovers a focal task

## Mechanism (confirmed by reading, E-1851 session)

`sessionstatuscmd.Run` resolves the focal task ONCE, before entering the loop:

    focal, kind, err = monitor.ResolveSessionStatusFocal(pane)
    ...
    monitorLoop(focal, parentSession, emittingSession, ...)

`monitorLoop` takes `focal` by value and never re-resolves it — grepping the
loop body for `ResolveSessionStatusFocal|GetPaneStatus` returns 0 matches. So a
monitor started before its session exists renders the claim/bind hint forever.

## Why E-1851 exposed it

Latent while a human started `session monitor` by hand — that always happened
well AFTER Claude had registered its session. E-1851 makes `task spawn` launch
the monitor automatically, milliseconds after the window is created and seconds
before Claude's SessionStart hook writes the session row. The spawned layout's
monitor pane is therefore blank in the common case, which is most of the value
of the 3-pane layout.

## Scope of the race

`parentSession` shares it exactly: it is read from the `@endless_spawned_by`
window option, which `spawn-launch` writes immediately before its
`syscall.Exec` — the same instant the session row does not yet exist.
`emittingSession` is consulted only while `focal == 0`, so a stale 0 there
leaves the no-goal view (E-1802) empty for exactly the sessions it serves.
All three therefore move together; the plan re-anchors the set and freezes it
on the first focal hit.

## Testability constraint found while planning

`sessionstatuscmd.Run` calls `monitor.PinMainDB()` unconditionally on the
normal pane-resolved path, so `--config-dir` cannot redirect it and pane→session
resolution cannot be exercised against a seeded throwaway DB — which is what
verifying this fix requires.

Resolved in the plan by adding a test-intended `--pane` flag on the precedent of
the existing `--task`/`--session` flags, NOT by gating the pin on
`HasExplicitDBContext()`. The gate was considered and rejected: it would turn a
stateless invariant into a caller-dependent convention whose failure mode is a
silently empty view, and unlike the `main.go` precedent it would be
production-reachable, since the Python CLI already translates `--db` into
`--config-dir` and is one refactor away from threading it here. Full rationale
is recorded in the plan so it is not relitigated.

## Explicitly NOT this task

The pane HEIGHT symptom is handled in E-1851: with no rows the pane holds
`monitorPaneEmptyHeight` instead of collapsing to a 2-row sliver, and it grows
to an exact fit as soon as rows resolve. This task is only about the rows
appearing at all.

Separately, a monitor whose cwd is a self_dev worktree reads the sandbox DB,
whose session rows carry no `active_task_id` — verified: the e-1851 sandbox has
1 session row, 0 with a task. That is E-698's documented cost (E-1883).
E-1851 works around it by starting the monitor pane in the project dir.

# E-1892 — `session monitor` re-resolves its focal task until one appears

## Scope

`internal/sessionstatuscmd` only. The monitor's resolution lifecycle — nothing
about rendering, sizing, or the layout E-1851 builds.

## Decision: re-anchor the WHOLE set, freeze on the first focal hit

Re-resolve `focal`, `parentSession` and `emittingSession` together on each tick
while `focal == 0`; stop re-resolving the moment `focal != 0`.

All three are read from the same not-yet-settled state and share one race:
`parentSession` comes from the `@endless_spawned_by` window option, which
`spawn-launch` writes immediately before its `syscall.Exec` — the same instant
the session row does not yet exist. `emittingSession` is consulted only while
`focal == 0`, so freezing it at a stale 0 would leave the no-goal view (E-1802)
permanently empty for exactly the sessions it exists to serve.

Freezing on `focal != 0` preserves E-1698's anchor-once contract unchanged: once
a task is anchored the view stays pinned to THIS window's task as other sessions
come and go. Nothing re-resolves after that point. A session that never claims
keeps re-resolving every 2s, which is correct — that is how the view recovers
when the user finally claims.

## Mechanism

`Run` currently resolves once and passes three values into `monitorLoop`. Change
it to pass an *anchor function* that returns the triple, and have `monitorLoop`
call it each tick until focal is non-zero:

    type anchor struct{ focal, parentSession, emittingSession int64; hint string }

    // seamed as a package var so tests drive the sequence, mirroring the
    // existing `worktreeAnomalies` seam in this same file
    var resolveAnchor = func(pane string) (anchor, error) { ... }

`Run`'s existing `--task` / `--session` headless branches keep their fixed
anchors (they name the focal directly, so there is nothing to wait for) — those
call `monitorLoop` with an anchor func that returns a constant.

### Decided: add a test-intended `--pane`, do NOT gate the pin on `--config-dir`

`sessionstatuscmd.Run` calls `monitor.PinMainDB()` unconditionally on the normal
(pane-resolved) path, so `--config-dir` cannot redirect it and pane→session
resolution cannot be exercised against a seeded DB — which is what this task
must test.

**Add `--pane <id>`** to `session-status`, on the exact precedent of the
existing `--task` / `--session` flags: documented *"intended for tests"*,
it supplies the pane id the live path would read from `$TMUX_PANE` and, like
those two, honors the resolved DB context instead of pinning main. It still
goes through the real `ResolveSessionStatusFocal` → `GetPaneStatus` path, so it
exercises the resolution this task changes rather than bypassing it.

**Rejected: `if !monitor.HasExplicitDBContext() { PinMainDB() }`.** Three
reasons, recorded so this is not relitigated:

1. It converts an invariant into a caller-dependent convention. "Session/pane
   state always comes from main" currently holds regardless of flags, matching
   the hook and the status line. Gated, it holds only when the caller stays
   quiet — and the failure is SILENT: the view renders the no-task hint, which
   is indistinguishable from "nothing claimed here."
2. It is production-reachable, unlike the `main.go` precedent it would borrow
   from. That rule is safe for `hook`/`channel`/`tmux` because production never
   passes `--config-dir` to those. `session-status` is invoked by a Python CLI
   that already translates `--db main|sandbox` into `--config-dir` and today
   deliberately does not thread it here — one natural refactor away from
   `endless session status --db sandbox` quietly emptying the view.
3. It adds a second orthogonal exception axis to a pin E-698 just narrowed to
   one deliberate rule ("one self_dev rule, not a per-command exception").

`--pane` has none of these properties: the Python CLI never passes it, so the
production path keeps the unconditional pin exactly as it is today.

## Tests — `tests/tasks/e-1892-verify.sh`

One suite, task's own checks fail-fast first, then project-wide regression.

**Layer A — unit, FAIL-FAST** (`internal/sessionstatuscmd`)
- Drive `resolveAnchor` through the seam with a scripted sequence — returns
  `focal=0` three times, then `focal=1851` — and assert `monitorLoop` picks up
  1851 and renders its rows.
- Assert it STOPS calling the resolver after the first hit: the seam counts
  calls; the count must not advance across subsequent ticks.
- Assert `parentSession`/`emittingSession` update on the same tick focal does,
  not one tick later.
- Assert a resolver ERROR while focal is still 0 is non-fatal — the monitor
  keeps its hint and retries; it must not exit the way a render error does.
- Assert `--pane` carries the same contract as `--task`/`--session`: it skips
  `PinMainDB` and reads the resolved DB context, while still routing through
  `ResolveSessionStatusFocal` rather than bypassing resolution.
- Assert the production path is UNCHANGED: with no `--pane`/`--task`/`--session`
  and no self_dev worktree, the pin still fires unconditionally — an explicit
  `--config-dir` must NOT redirect it (the rejected design above, pinned as a
  regression guard so it cannot creep back in).

**Layer B — integration (isolated tmux server + seeded throwaway DB)**
The recovery proof, and what `--pane` above exists to make reachable:
1. `tmux -L <socket>` private server; seed a throwaway `--config-dir` DB with a
   project + task but NO session row.
2. Split a pane running
   `endless-go --config-dir <tmp> session-status --monitor --pane <that pane id>`
   and assert it renders the no-task hint, and that E-1851's fit holds the pane
   at `monitorPaneEmptyHeight` (8 rows).
3. Mid-flight, `INSERT` the session row with `process = <that pane id>` and
   `active_task_id = <task>`.
4. Within ~3 ticks assert the pane now renders the task rows AND has resized to
   the exact fit (frame lines + 1) — proving recovery end-to-end and that it
   composes with E-1851's sizing.
5. Tear down the tmux server and temp dirs on exit.

**Layer C — project-wide regression**: `go test ./...` and `just test`.

Reuse the harness shape from `tests/tasks/e-1851-verify.sh` (private `-L`
socket, geometry-addressed panes never pane indexes, throwaway `--config-dir`,
trap-based teardown) — same author conventions, no shared file.

## Out of scope

- The pane HEIGHT symptom. E-1851 already holds `monitorPaneEmptyHeight` when
  there are no rows and grows to an exact fit as rows appear. This task is only
  about the rows appearing at all.
- A monitor whose cwd is a `self_dev` worktree reads that worktree's sandbox,
  whose session rows carry no `active_task_id` (verified: the e-1851 sandbox has
  1 session row, 0 with a task). That is E-698's documented cost, tracked at
  E-1883. E-1851 sidesteps it by starting the monitor pane in the project dir;
  do not re-litigate it here.

# E-1853 — Verb gate: stop-and-ask on a classifier error, enforced by a gate

## 1. Classify into three outcomes
Rework `_check_verb_via_haiku` (src/endless/task_cmd.py) to return a three-state result instead of `(bool, str|None)`:
- **VERB** (clean `YES: <definition>`) + the definition.
- **NOT_VERB** — the reply is an explicitly matched clean `NO`.
- **UNDETERMINED** + a short reason (`timeout` | `nonzero-exit` | `missing-binary` | `malformed`) for the human-facing message.

Rules:
- Match a clean `NO` explicitly. A reply that is neither a clean `YES:` nor a clean `NO` (hedged, prose, empty, markdown) is **UNDETERMINED (malformed)** — NOT `NOT_VERB`. (Today "not `YES:`" is misread as NO — the core bug.)
- Retry twice on a transient UNDETERMINED (`timeout` / `nonzero-exit` / `malformed`) before settling UNDETERMINED. `missing-binary` is not retried.

## 2. Behavior in `validate_title`
- **VERB** → register via `matchers.add_verb`, pass. (unchanged)
- **NOT_VERB** → raise the existing "title must start with an actionable verb" error; the agent rewrites the title. (unchanged)
- **UNDETERMINED** → do NOT reword, register, or guess. Enter the enforced stop-and-ask gate (§3).

## 3. Enforced gate (a message alone is ignorable — the agent will reword anyway)
On UNDETERMINED, `endless task add` / `task update`:
1. Makes NO change to the task.
2. Sets a lightweight per-session flag marking that a verb-classifier stop is pending (a column / state on the session row that hit the error, carrying the failure reason for the message — no new table). Unshipped software, so add the column directly; no migration.
3. Exits non-zero with a message that names the failure reason and says: STOP, tell the user what failed, do not reword.

Enforcement lives in the Claude hook (internal/hookcmd/claude.go), extending the existing gate (which already blocks Write/Edit until a task is claimed):
- **PreToolUse**: while the flag is set for the current session, BLOCK any `endless task add` / `task update` that carries a title, with the stop message. This closes the reword bypass — the agent cannot route around the stop by picking a different word. The block is title-scoped (not a full tool freeze), so the agent can still surface the situation to the user; it simply cannot create a mis-titled task.
- **UserPromptSubmit**: clear the flag. The gate lifts the moment the human replies, so resolution is the human answering in chat — not a special command.

## 4. Human resolution — in chat, no new command
The human's reply clears the flag (via UserPromptSubmit) and directs the agent:
- "it's a verb" → the agent registers it with the existing `endless verb add <word> --definition "<d>"`, then retries the title. It now passes with no classifier call (the word is registered).
- "rewrite it" → the agent rewrites the title with a real verb.
No `verb resolve` command and no pending-decision table: existing `verb add` covers approval; a chat reply covers the rest.

## 5. Tests — tests/tasks/e-1853-verify.sh
- **Classifier (unit):** VERB / NOT_VERB / UNDETERMINED for clean YES, clean NO, malformed-non-NO (→ UNDETERMINED, not NOT_VERB), timeout, nonzero-exit, missing-binary. Retry fires on transient UNDETERMINED, not on `missing-binary` or `NO`. (Fake the `claude` subprocess.)
- **Gate:** on UNDETERMINED, `task add` refuses, creates no task, sets the session flag; a subsequent titled `task add`/`update` is blocked by the PreToolUse hook while the flag is set; the block clears after a `UserPromptSubmit`.
- **Resolution:** once the flag is cleared, the existing `endless verb add <word>` registers the verb and the original title passes; the reword path is blocked only while the flag is set.
- **Regression:** clean YES still auto-registers + passes; clean NO still rejects with the verb error.

## Out of scope
Punctuation/dedup on the verb write path (E-1837). Optional apfel/local classifier as a Haiku alternative (E-1849) — a later swap behind the same three-state result.

# E-1892 — `session monitor` re-resolves its focal task until one appears

## Scope

about rendering, sizing, or the layout E-1851 builds.

## Decision: re-anchor the WHOLE set, freeze on the first focal hit

Re-resolve `focal`, `parentSession` and `emittingSession` together on each tick
while `focal == 0`; stop re-resolving the moment `focal != 0`.

All three are read from the same not-yet-settled state and share one race:
`parentSession` comes from the `@endless_spawned_by` window option, which
`spawn-launch` writes immediately before its `syscall.Exec` — the same instant
the session row does not yet exist. `emittingSession` is consulted only while
`focal == 0`, so freezing it at a stale 0 would leave the no-goal view (E-1802)
permanently empty for exactly the sessions it exists to serve.

Freezing on `focal != 0` preserves E-1698's anchor-once contract unchanged: once
a task is anchored the view stays pinned to THIS window's task as other sessions
come and go. Nothing re-resolves after that point. A session that never claims
keeps re-resolving every 2s, which is correct — that is how the view recovers
when the user finally claims.

`Run` currently resolves once and passes three values into `monitorLoop`. Change
it to pass an *anchor function* that returns the triple, and have `monitorLoop`
call it each tick until focal is non-zero:

    type anchor struct{ focal, parentSession, emittingSession int64; hint string }

    // seamed as a package var so tests drive the sequence, mirroring the
    // existing `worktreeAnomalies` seam in this same file
    var resolveAnchor = func(process string) (anchor, error) { ... }

`process` is the session's process handle (`sessions.process`), sourced from
`$TMUX_PANE` or `--process`. Keep the tmux-shaped name confined to the
`monitor` helpers that genuinely take a tmux pane.

`Run`'s existing `--task` / `--session` headless branches keep their fixed
anchors (they name the focal directly, so there is nothing to wait for) — those
call `monitorLoop` with an anchor func that returns a constant.

tmux vocabulary must not leak into its flag names — a tmux pane id is merely

multiplexer-driver seam (E-1085). `tmux status-line --pane` keeps its name

   the hook and the status line. Gated, it holds only when the caller stays
   quiet — and the failure is SILENT: the view renders the no-task hint, which

2. It is production-reachable, unlike the `main.go` precedent it would borrow
   from. That rule is safe for `hook`/`channel`/`tmux` because production never
   passes `--config-dir` to those. `session-status` is invoked by a Python CLI
   that already translates `--db main|sandbox` into `--config-dir` and today
   deliberately does not thread it here — one natural refactor away from
   `endless session status --db sandbox` quietly emptying the view.
3. It adds a second orthogonal exception axis to a pin E-698 just narrowed to
   one deliberate rule ("one self_dev rule, not a per-command exception").

the production path keeps the unconditional pin exactly as it is today.

socket, geometry-addressed panes never pane indexes, throwaway `--config-dir`,
trap-based teardown) — same author conventions, no shared file.

  1 session row, 0 with a task). That is E-698's documented cost, tracked at

  do not re-litigate it here.

on a premise that was already stale when this plan was written: that
`sessionstatuscmd.Run` calls `monitor.PinMainDB()` UNCONDITIONALLY, so
`--config-dir` cannot redirect it and process→session resolution cannot be
exercised against a seeded DB.

payload.title: Record a fault when the tmux status line cannot reach the database
payload.description: `runStatusLine` maps every `monitor.DB()` error to `placeholder()` and stays silent on stderr, so a blank status bar is byte-identical to 'this pane has no task' and leaves no trace — ~7 distinct fail-closed exits all render as the same dim dot. Record a fault instead (dedupes while open, so a bar blanking every 2s across 14 panes raises one incident). Keep the bar output and the stderr silence exactly as they are; this is observability only.
payload.analysis:
# Analysis — a blank status bar is indistinguishable from "no task here"

## The swallow

`internal/tmuxcmd/status_line.go` `runStatusLine` has three exits to
`placeholder()` (lines 27, 40, 52). The one at line 40 is the problem:

    status, err := monitor.GetPaneStatus(pane)
    if err != nil {
        // Real error (DB unreachable, etc.). Render placeholder; stay
        // silent on stderr to avoid log spam during interactive use.
        fmt.Print(placeholder())
        return
    }

`monitor.DB()` has ~7 fail-closed exits behind that single `err`: the
`schema.SQL` apply, five enum `VerifyIntegrity` gates (task_types,
session_kinds, gate_kinds, session_task_relations, nav_via_kinds), and
`guardWorktreeDBContext`. Every one of them renders as the same dim dot as
"this pane has no Endless context", and writes nothing anywhere.

The stderr silence is correct and should stay: the bar re-runs this binary once
per pane every `status-interval` (2s here, ~14 panes), so logging would be a
firehose landing on top of a live TUI.

## Evidence this matters

2026-08-05: the tmux status bar went fully blank twice, machine-wide. It could
not be diagnosed. Post-hoc the resolution path was healthy — 20/20 serial
samples of the exact bar invocation returned the task, and 60/60 under 13-way
concurrency — so the trigger was transient and is now unreproducible. A fault
record would have captured which of the seven exits fired, with its error text.

## Why the fault system fits

`faults.Record` dedupes an open incident in place, so a bar blanking every 2s
across every pane raises ONE incident rather than thousands of rows. That is
precisely the shape this call site needs, and it is why stderr was rejected.
`cmd/endless-go/main.go` already calls `faults.Bind` for every subcommand, so
the recorder is available here with no new wiring.

## Not in scope of the neighbours

- E-1884 converts 42 `log.Printf` sites (hookcmd 23, monitor 11, schema 5,
  channelcmd 3) — sites that write too NOISILY. This is the inverse: a site
  that writes nothing. `runStatusLine` is not among those 42.
- E-698 is `assumed` and landed twice. It did not introduce the swallow, which
  predates it; at most its +78 lines of schema widened the window.

payload.title: Repair 6 verify scripts still calling the renamed `endless register`
payload.description: tests/tasks/e-{1747,1754,1758,1766,1768,1771}-verify.sh set up their isolated env with `endless register <path> --infer ...`, which now exits 1 with "\`endless register\` moved to \`endless project register\`". Every one of those scripts therefore dies in setup() with "ERROR: registering temp project failed" and verifies nothing — they are silently dead, not passing. Fix is mechanical (`en register` -> `en project register`; the flags are unchanged, confirmed by running e-1771-verify.sh with the substitution applied: 21/21 pass). Discovered while updating e-1771-verify.sh for E-1880; the E-1880 assertions in it are correct but cannot execute until this lands.

payload.title: Isolate the log directory in Go tests, not just the database
payload.description: `go test ./...` writes into the REAL log dir under the user's config: hook.log entries at 2026-08-05 17:08:41-46 carry fixture data (`bound session uuid-real to dispatch row short_id feed1234`, and an `auto-registered project: 003` whose path is a Go test temp dir). The DB IS isolated — no fixture projects or sessions appear in the real ledger — so only the log path escapes. It corrupts the one artifact you reach for when diagnosing a live incident, since real and synthetic entries interleave with no marker distinguishing them.

fields.outcome: Filed on a false premise. A tests/tasks/e-NNNN-verify.sh is point-in-time proof for ONE pre-land verification; after that task lands its validity is undefined. Those 6 scripts dying on the renamed `endless register` is therefore not a defect and not work — they are historical artifacts, not a living regression suite.

  1 session row, 0 with a task). That is E-698's documented cost, tracked at
  E-1883. E-1851 sidesteps it by starting the monitor pane in the project dir;
  do not re-litigate it here.



## SUPERSEDED at implementation time — `--process` was not added

The `--process` decision above, and the regression guard paired with it, rested
on a premise that was already stale when this plan was written: that
`sessionstatuscmd.Run` calls `monitor.PinMainDB()` UNCONDITIONALLY, so
`--config-dir` cannot redirect it and process→session resolution cannot be
exercised against a seeded DB.

`c186df7d` (E-698, "restore session-status to main; move the job guard to the
trigger" — already on `main`) had changed that call to:

    if !monitor.HasExplicitDBContext() { monitor.PinMainDB() }

i.e. the E-1429/E-1700 contract that an explicit `--config-dir` beats the
env-driven main pin, pinned by `internal/monitor/db_gate_test.go`'s
`TestSelfDetectVsExplicit_MainPinRouting`.

Consequences, decided with Mike before implementing:

1. **`--process` was NOT added.** Its entire justification was the
   untestability the E-698 commit had already removed. Layer B drives the real
   `ResolveSessionStatusFocal` path with `--config-dir` and the monitor pane's
   own `$TMUX_PANE`, so no new production surface is needed.
2. **The "pin fires unconditionally / `--config-dir` must NOT redirect it"
   assertion was DROPPED.** Implementing it would mean reverting a deliberate,
   merged E-698 decision and breaking its test — out of scope for E-1892. The
   routing contract that actually holds is pinned in Layer A instead, by running
   `TestSelfDetectVsExplicit_MainPinRouting` as a must-not-regress check.

Everything else in this plan was implemented as written.

### One further deviation, test-placement only

- **Layer A tests `anchorTracker` and `monitorFrame`, not `monitorLoop`
  directly.** The tracker holds 100% of the lifecycle logic this task changed;
  `monitorFrame` is the resolve→render composition the loop repeats, split out
  so it is drivable without a terminal, a ticker, or a signal. `monitorLoop`
  itself keeps only paint/fit/tick machinery, and Layer B proves its wiring
  end-to-end against a real tmux pane — which is the recovery proof anyway.


### Rebase onto main (after the first land attempt)

`e1fa96f9` ("E-1851: start the observation panes in the project dir; floor the
empty monitor") landed on main after this branch was cut and reworked the same
functions, so `worktree land` hit a genuine content conflict. Resolved in place
by rebasing — no work duplicated or lost:

- `renderSnapshot` now returns `(rowCount, error)`. `monitorFrame` forwards that
  count, so the pane fit still distinguishes "no task rows" from "a short real
  frame". The count flipping 0 → non-zero on the tick a focal task resolves is
  exactly what regrows the pane in the same repaint the rows appear in — the two
  changes compose cleanly.
- `monitorPaneEmptyHeight = 8` DOES exist as of that commit (it did not when this
  plan was drafted, which is why an earlier revision of this section said so).
  Layer B now asserts the unresolved pane holds 8 and the recovered pane fits
  exactly at 7, so recovery is a shrink rather than a grow. Direction is
  incidental; both ends are pinned exactly.

Two sites are still broken: update_plan's 'valid' tuple (so 'task update --status submitted' fails today) and _CHILDREN_STATE_ORDER (so the epic handoff breakdown does not reconcile). fields.text:
# E-1891 — Consolidate the duplicated task status vocabulary

Absorbs E-1888. Both were filed as separate bugs during E-1845; they are two
surviving symptoms of one defect, and fixing them apart means writing the same
regression test twice.

## The defect

Six hand-maintained copies of the FULL status vocabulary must agree with
`cli.TASK_STATUSES`, across both languages, with nothing enforcing it:

| Site | State |
|---|---|
| `src/endless/cli.py:122` `TASK_STATUSES` | canonical |
| `src/endless/task_cmd.py` `update_plan`'s `valid` | **missing `submitted`** |
| `src/endless/task_cmd.py` `_CHILDREN_STATE_ORDER` | **missing `submitted`** |
| `src/endless/session_status_cmd.py` `_VALID_STATUSES` | in sync |
| `internal/web/handlers.go` valid map | in sync |
| `internal/events/session_status.go` `statusToDisposition` | in sync (safe `default:`) |

E-1648 added `submitted` and updated four of six. E-1845 added `untriaged` and
had to hand-edit all six — a miss would have shipped silently. The next status
added walks into the same trap.

## The two live symptoms

1. **`update_plan`'s `valid` tuple omits `submitted`**, so
   `endless task update <id> --status submitted` fails with "Invalid status"
   today, even though `submitted` is a real status reachable via `task submit`.
2. **`_CHILDREN_STATE_ORDER` omits `submitted`**, so a submitted child is
   counted in the epic handoff breakdown's `(N total)` suffix but renders no
   bucket. The breakdown does not reconcile — contradicting the tuple's own
   docstring, which promises exactly that it will.

## Fix

**Derive where derivable.** `update_plan`'s `valid` IS `cli.TASK_STATUSES`;
stop duplicating it.

**Assert coverage where it is not.** `_CHILDREN_STATE_ORDER` encodes lifecycle
progression and collapses terminals into one bucket, so it cannot simply BE the
list — but a test can require every status in `TASK_STATUSES` to map to some
bucket.

**Deliverable: one test** that fails the day a status is added and any site is
missed. That test, not the two one-line fixes, is the point of this task.

## Also in scope

- **The Go copies** need the same guarantee or they drift independently. There
  is no shared constant across the language boundary today, so this task has to
  pick a mechanism — generate one side from the other, or a cross-language
  fixture test. This is the harder half and the reason this is not a 10-minute
  task.
- **Collapse `_TERMINAL_STATUSES` and `_RELATION_TERMINAL_STATUSES`** in
  `task_cmd.py`: byte-identical five-status lists under two names. Not a bug
  yet; will be.

## Explicitly OUT of scope

Do NOT derive the policy subsets from the vocabulary — they are *supposed* to be
shorter, because they encode rules rather than copies:
`_SUBMITTABLE_FROM`, `_DESCRIPTION_RESET_FROM`, `_REOPENABLE_TERMINAL_STATUSES`,
`_REOPEN_TO_REVISIT`, `isPreJudgmentStatus`, and the epic-derivation buckets.
Collapsing any of these into the full list would be a behavior change, not a
cleanup.

payload.title: Stop the dead-pane reaper from nulling live pane bindings project-wide
payload.description: `ReapDeadTmuxPanes` decides liveness from `tmux list-panes -a` using an ambient $TMUX it never validates, so a caller running under a foreign or private tmux server sees none of the real panes and nulls `process` for every session row in the project. `TouchSession` then cannot heal it: an empty TMUX_PANE revives `state` but leaves `process` NULL via COALESCE, so the row reads alive and resolves to nothing forever. Observed 2026-08-05: 27 live Claude panes orphaned, 59 of 61 status lines blank.
payload.analysis:
# Analysis — the dead-pane reaper can destroy live pane bindings project-wide

## Two defects, both required for the damage

### 1. The reaper trusts an ambient tmux view it never validates

`monitor.ReapDeadTmuxPanes` (internal/monitor/reap.go) decides liveness with:

    exec.Command("tmux", "list-panes", "-a", "-F", "#{pane_id}")

It inherits whatever `$TMUX` the calling process has. Any caller running under a
DIFFERENT tmux server — a private `tmux -L <socket>` server started by a test or
a verify script — sees only that server's panes. Every real pane then looks dead
and the whole project is reaped. There is no check that the observed pane set is
plausible for the rows about to be ended.

The `len(alive) == 0` branch is the sharpest edge: it nulls `process` for EVERY
non-ended tmux-format row in the project in one statement. Its comment treats an
empty pane set as proof that everything is dead; it is equally consistent with
"I am looking at the wrong server."

`internal/tmuxcmd/reset.go` already guards its own entry point (refuses when
`$TMUX` is empty, calling it "a footgun"). The SessionStart caller in
`internal/hookcmd/claude.go` has no such guard, and that is the one that fires
constantly.

### 2. TouchSession cannot undo it

    process = COALESCE(NULLIF(?, ''), process)
    state   = CASE WHEN sessions.state = 'ended' THEN 'needs_input' ELSE state END

A later hook firing with an EMPTY `TMUX_PANE` flips the row back to
`needs_input` but leaves `process` NULL. The row now reads as alive and resolves
to nothing, permanently — pane lookup keys on `process`. Only a hook that fires
WITH a pane can heal it, which is why sessions actively running tools recovered
and idle ones did not.

## Observed damage (2026-08-05)

- 27 live Claude panes had their session row at `state='ended'`, `process` NULL,
  while the pane was demonstrably alive and working in that task's worktree.
- 59 of 61 tmux windows rendered a blank status line simultaneously.
- Only 3 sessions were intact — exactly the ones firing hooks with `TMUX_PANE`
  set at the time.
- Reap batches are visible in the ledger by minute, including one batch of 37.

The blank bar is invisible by construction: `runStatusLine` maps every failure
to the same placeholder (E-1895), so this destroyed state for hours with no
diagnostic anywhere.

## Directions (not locked — this needs a plan)

- Refuse to reap on an implausible pane set: if `alive` is empty, or disjoint
  from every stored `process` for the project, treat it as "wrong server" and
  no-op rather than reaping.
- Pin the server identity: record which tmux server a session belongs to
  (socket path) and only reap rows for that server.
- Make the damage recoverable: reviving `ended` to `needs_input` while leaving
  `process` NULL should not be possible — either restore both or neither.
- Consider whether SessionStart is the right trigger at all, given it fires from
  contexts whose `$TMUX` is not the user's server.

# E-1891 — Consolidate the task status vocabulary behind one accessor

Absorbs E-1888 (obsolete). Both were filed as separate bugs during E-1845; they
are two surviving symptoms of one defect.

## The defect

Status is the only vocabulary in the system that never got first-class
treatment. Task type, session kind, and session↔task relation each have a Go
package that owns the list. Status is bare string literals, scattered across
roughly fifteen sites in two languages, in three different shapes:

1. **Copies of the whole vocabulary** — must equal `cli.TASK_STATUSES`.
   `update_plan`'s `valid` tuple, `_VALID_STATUSES`, `web/handlers.go`'s valid
   map, `statusToDisposition`, `_CHILDREN_STATE_ORDER`.
2. **Policy subsets** — deliberately shorter, each encoding a rule.
   `_SUBMITTABLE_FROM`, `_DESCRIPTION_RESET_FROM`, `_REOPENABLE_TERMINAL_STATUSES`,
   `_REOPEN_TO_REVISIT`, `_TERMINAL_STATUSES`, `_RELATION_TERMINAL_STATUSES`,
   `isPreJudgmentStatus`.
3. **Lists embedded in SQL string literals** — the least visible and the most
   rot-prone, since nothing reads inside a SQL string. `next_tasks`'s
   `NOT IN (...)`, `GetActiveTasks`, the claim promotion in `monitor/session.go`,
   `web/queries.go`.

E-1648 added `submitted` and updated four of the category-1 sites out of six.
E-1845 added `untriaged` and had to hand-edit every site in all three
categories, with nothing to catch a miss.

## Two live symptoms (acceptance criteria)

1. `update_plan`'s `valid` tuple omits `submitted`, so
   `endless task update <id> --status submitted` fails with "Invalid status"
   today, even though `submitted` is real and reachable via `task submit`.
2. `_CHILDREN_STATE_ORDER` omits `submitted`, so a submitted child is counted in
   the epic handoff breakdown's `(N total)` but renders no bucket — the
   breakdown does not reconcile, contradicting the tuple's own docstring.

Both must be fixed, but neither is the point. The point is that the next status
added cannot reintroduce them.

## Design — one accessor, one owner

**Go owns the registry. Python delegates to it.** Not two mirrored registries:
that would leave two places that must agree, and a drift test to police them.
Python already shells out to `endless-go` for the event bridge, template
rendering (E-1565), and `session-status`, so this is the house pattern, not a
new dependency.

```go
package taskstatus

// Status is the machine slug. A plain string alias: every DB read/write and
// SQL literal is already a string, so this adds no conversions at boundaries.
type Status = string

const (
    Untriaged Status = "untriaged"
    Unplanned Status = "unplanned"
    Submitted Status = "submitted"
    // ...one per status
)

// Group names a curated set. Every grouping in the system is defined in the
// one map below, so a new status is reviewed against all of them at once.
type Group int

const (
    All Group = iota
    SubmittableFrom
    DescriptionResetFrom
    PreJudgment
    ReopenableTerminal
    ReopenToRevisit
    Terminal
    NotActionable
    ChildrenStateOrder
    // ...
)

var groups = map[Group][]Status{
    All:             {Untriaged, Unplanned, Submitted, Ready, /* ... */},
    SubmittableFrom: {Untriaged, Unplanned, Revisit},
    PreJudgment:     {Untriaged, Unplanned},
    // ...
}

func Get(g Group) []Status        // defensive copy — callers must not mutate the map
func Has(g Group, s Status) bool
func SQLList(g Group) string      // "'untriaged','unplanned'" for IN clauses
func Rank(g Group, s Status) int  // index within an ordered group
```

**Python side:** one command — `endless-go task-status groups --json` — emits
the whole map. Python loads it **once on first use and memoizes**; do NOT call
out per lookup, or every `update_plan` validation and `task add` pays a
subprocess spawn. Python re-exposes the same `get` / `has` / `sql_list` / `rank`
API over the cached payload, so call sites read the same in both languages.

Verify during implementation that no Python path needs status data when
`endless-go` cannot be resolved. If one exists, decide explicitly whether it
fails closed or falls back — do not let it fail by accident.

## What moves in

- All three categories above, including the SQL lists. `SQLList(NotActionable)`
  replacing a hardcoded `NOT IN (...)` is the highest-value single change here:
  those literals are invisible to every tool and are where drift hides longest.
- `_TERMINAL_STATUSES` and `_RELATION_TERMINAL_STATUSES` collapse into one
  group — they are byte-identical five-status lists under two names.

## What stays out, and why

- **Glyph and label maps.** These are status→presentation, and they legitimately
  differ per surface (the Python tree renders `○`; the Go monitor keys off
  actions, not statuses). Forcing them into `Get(Group)` would make the registry
  lie about what it holds.
- **Epic derivation.** A precedence ladder with fallthrough order — an
  algorithm, not a set.
- **The membership rules themselves.** Moving a subset into the registry must
  not change which statuses it contains. This is a pure relocation; any
  behavior change is a separate decision.

## Enforcement

Relocating the lists removes the copies. It does not stop a future author from
typing `"untriged"` in a fresh comparison — and no choice of Go type prevents
that, since an untyped string constant converts implicitly whether `Status` is
an alias or a defined type. If enforcement is wanted it has to be a lint rule or
a test that greps for bare status literals outside `taskstatus`. Decide whether
that is in scope; it is cheap and it is the only thing that actually holds the
line.

## Explicitly NOT in scope

A `task_statuses` lookup table. The code is the source of truth; a table would
only be a convenience copy so SQL can join and enforce a foreign key, and it
would need a migration and a backfill across every in-flight worktree. Deferred
deliberately — not filed as a task, tracked by Mike directly.

# E-1891 — Consolidate the task status vocabulary behind one accessor

Absorbs E-1888 (obsolete). Both were filed as separate bugs during E-1845; they
are two surviving symptoms of one defect.

## The defect

treatment. Task type, session kind, and session↔task relation each have a Go
package that owns the list — `tasktype` even carries `String()` and `Label()`
methods. Status is bare string literals scattered across roughly fifteen sites
in two languages, in four shapes:

1. **Copies of the whole vocabulary** — must equal `cli.TASK_STATUSES`.

   map, `statusToDisposition`, `_CHILDREN_STATE_ORDER`.
2. **Policy subsets** — deliberately shorter, each encoding a rule.
   `_SUBMITTABLE_FROM`, `_DESCRIPTION_RESET_FROM`, `_REOPENABLE_TERMINAL_STATUSES`,
   `_REOPEN_TO_REVISIT`, `_TERMINAL_STATUSES`, `_RELATION_TERMINAL_STATUSES`,
   `isPreJudgmentStatus`.
3. **Lists embedded in SQL string literals** — the least visible and most
   rot-prone, since nothing reads inside a SQL string. `next_tasks`'s
   `NOT IN (...)`, `GetActiveTasks`, the claim promotion in `monitor/session.go`,
   `web/queries.go`.
4. **Per-status presentation and ordering** — the glyph maps in `task_cmd.py`
   and `web/pages`, `statusLabel()`, and the epic-derivation precedence ladder.

The failure mode is **omission, not typos**: a status gets added and a site gets
missed. E-1648 added `submitted` and updated four of six category-1 sites.
E-1845 added `untriaged` and had to hand-edit every site in all four categories,
with nothing to catch a miss — and the category-4 miss in `epic_derivation.go`
would have silently stopped epics reacting to freshly filed children.

## Two live symptoms (acceptance criteria)

1. `update_plan`'s `valid` tuple omits `submitted`, so
   `endless task update <id> --status submitted` fails with "Invalid status"
   today, even though `submitted` is real and reachable via `task submit`.
2. `_CHILDREN_STATE_ORDER` omits `submitted`, so a submitted child is counted in
   the epic handoff breakdown's `(N total)` but renders no bucket — the
   breakdown does not reconcile, contradicting the tuple's own docstring.

added cannot reintroduce them.

## Design — Go owns everything; Python consumes answers, not inputs

Not two mirrored registries: that leaves two places that must agree. Python
already shells out to `endless-go` for the event bridge, template rendering
(E-1565), and `session-status`, so delegation is the house pattern.

```go
package taskstatus

// Status is the machine slug. A plain string alias: every DB read/write and
// SQL literal is already a string, so this adds no conversions at boundaries.
type Status = string

const (
    Untriaged Status = "untriaged"
    Unplanned Status = "unplanned"
    Submitted Status = "submitted"
    // ...one per status
)

// Group names a curated set. EVERY grouping in the system is defined in the one
// map below, so adding a status forces a decision about each of them.
type Group int

const (
    All Group = iota
    SubmittableFrom
    DescriptionResetFrom
    PreJudgment
    ReopenableTerminal
    ReopenToRevisit
    Terminal
    NotActionable
    ChildrenStateOrder
    DerivationPrecedence   // the epic ladder, as ordered data
    // ...
)

var groups = map[Group][]Status{
    All:                  {Untriaged, Unplanned, Submitted, Ready, /* ... */},
    SubmittableFrom:      {Untriaged, Unplanned, Revisit},
    PreJudgment:          {Untriaged, Unplanned},
    DerivationPrecedence: {Underway, Ready, Submitted, Unplanned, Untriaged},
    // ...
}

func Get(g Group) []Status        // defensive copy — callers must not mutate
func Has(g Group, s Status) bool
func SQLList(g Group) string      // "'untriaged','unplanned'" for IN clauses
func Rank(g Group, s Status) int  // index within an ordered group
func Label(s Status) string       // "Untriaged" — mirrors tasktype.Label()
func Glyph(s Status) string       // "◌" — semantic only, no color
```

**Python side:** one command — `endless-go task-status --json` — emits the
**derived output** of the accessors, not the raw sets: per group, the ordered
members, the pre-rendered SQL list, and the rank map; plus the label and glyph
tables. Python loads it **once on first use and memoizes**, then does pure
lookup. It must not reimplement `SQLList` quoting or `Rank` semantics — that
would single-source the data while duplicating the logic, which is this same
defect one layer up.

Do NOT call out per lookup, or every `update_plan` validation and `task add`
pays a subprocess spawn. Verify during implementation that no Python path needs
status data when `endless-go` cannot be resolved; if one exists, decide
explicitly whether it fails closed rather than letting it fail by accident.

## What moves in

- All four categories, including the SQL lists. `SQLList(NotActionable)`
  replacing a hardcoded `NOT IN (...)` is the highest-value single change:
  those literals are invisible to every tool and rot longest.
- `_TERMINAL_STATUSES` and `_RELATION_TERMINAL_STATUSES` collapse into one
  group — byte-identical five-status lists under two names.
- Glyph and label, as `Glyph()`/`Label()` methods, mirroring `tasktype`.
- The epic-derivation ladder as `DerivationPrecedence`, an ordered group. The
  algorithm stays in `epic_derivation.go` and walks the group, returning the
  first status present among the children; the *ordering data* — the part that
  must change when a status is added — lives with every other grouping.

## What stays out, and why

- **Medium-specific color values.** `click.style(fg="yellow")` and
  `bg-slate-400` are not shareable. The registry owns the semantic glyph; each
  surface maps its own palette.
- **Algorithms.** Only their ordering data moves in (see derivation above).
- **The membership rules themselves.** Relocating a subset must not change which
  statuses it contains. Any behavior change is a separate decision.

## Enforcement — none needed beyond the design

No lint rule, no bare-literal grep test. The user path is already input-validated
(`click.Choice`, the `valid` tuple). The code path has one author working under
review. And the failure that actually occurred twice was omission, not a typo —
which the one-map design fixes structurally, because a status cannot be added
without reading every grouping it might belong to.

## Sequencing — one task, two commits

Not split into separate tasks: the Go registry and the Python delegation are a
dependency chain, not independent pieces, so a second task could not start until
the first landed and would have no standalone value. The real concern is blast
radius while worktrees are in flight, which is a commit-sequencing matter:

1. Go package + subcommand + convert all Go call sites. Complete and useful
   alone; Python still duplicates at this point.
2. Python client + convert all Python call sites; delete the duplicates.

## Explicitly NOT in scope

A `task_statuses` lookup table. The code is the source of truth; a table would
only be a convenience copy so SQL can join and enforce a foreign key, and it
needs a migration and backfill across every in-flight worktree. Deferred
deliberately — not filed as a task, tracked by Mike directly.

payload.title: Document the tmux and config isolation rule for verification suites
payload.description: Nothing tells a verify-script author that a suite must isolate BOTH the tmux config (tmux -f /dev/null) and `XDG_CONFIG_HOME` before starting a private tmux server or running endless-go. Without the second, anything the suite spawns can decide liveness from a 3-pane fake server and reap the user's real database — 27 sessions orphaned and 59 of 61 status lines blanked on 2026-08-05. Add a short subsection to the guide's per-task verification suite section, pointing at tests/tasks/e-1851-verify.sh as the reference implementation.
payload.analysis:
# Rule to document

Add a short subsection to `docs/guide/orchestration.md`, under the per-task
verification suite guidance, stating the isolation contract a suite must meet.

## The rule

A verification suite may never start a tmux server, or run `endless-go`, without
isolating BOTH:

- **tmux config** — start private servers with `tmux -L <socket> -f /dev/null`,
  so the user's `~/.tmux.conf` (and any hook it installs, e.g. `session-created`
  -> `endless tmux init`) cannot fire against the throwaway server.
- **`XDG_CONFIG_HOME`** — point it at a throwaway directory for the server
  process, so every descendant (anything the suite spawns, and anything THOSE
  spawn) resolves its config dir, and therefore its database, away from
  `~/.config/endless/endless.db`.

Kill the server and remove the temp dirs in a trap on exit.

## Why the second one is load-bearing

Inside a private tmux server, `$TMUX` names a server with a handful of panes.
Any endless-go code path that decides liveness from `tmux list-panes -a` — most
importantly `monitor.ReapDeadTmuxPanes` — will conclude that every pane it does
not see is dead. Pointed at the user's real database, that nulls `process` for
every live session in the project and blanks every tmux status line on the
machine (observed 2026-08-05: 27 orphaned sessions, 59 of 61 windows blank).
Isolating the config dir means the worst such a path can do is damage a temp DB.

`-f /dev/null` alone is NOT sufficient: it only blocks config-file hooks, not
processes the suite launches itself.

## Reference implementation

`tests/tasks/e-1851-verify.sh` does both, with the reasoning inline at each

fields.outcome: Filed on a category error. The premise was that the per-task verify scripts 'rot silently' and need CI to catch it. But a per-task acceptance harness becoming invalid after its task lands is the EXPECTED end state, not a defect — its validity is defined as ending there. Both instances that prompted this task confirm it: e-1648-verify.sh asserted classify() maps 'submitted' into the actDo case, which E-1765 deliberately changed; and its fixture called 'endless register', which was deliberately renamed to 'project register'. Neither was decay — both were the codebase correctly evolving past a point-in-time script. Guarding against that would mean pinning behavior to superseded assertions, or maintaining historical harnesses indefinitely. Real regression coverage belongs in the go test and pytest suites, which these scripts already delegate to. E-1623 covers the legitimate adjacent work (retrofitting the scripts onto a shared harness) from a sounder premise.

fields.description: Agents reflexively file a new task for a bug they just introduced rather than reopening the task that introduced it, causing task proliferation. Three doc sources cause it: the spawn handoff tells sessions to file discoveries as new tasks without distinguishing a bug in their own work; docs/status-lifecycle.mmd has no edge from assumed/confirmed back to revisit even though the CLI accepts that transition today; and both revisit framings are about replanning, never about shipped work that turned out wrong. Fix the handoff wording, add the missing edges, broaden revisit's definition, and add a 'Fix a bug in your own landed work' guide pattern covering worktree reuse. fields.analysis:
# Scope extension — the "could this be done now?" test

Contributed from the E-1845 session, which reproduced this failure live: four
tasks filed during one task, two of which (E-1888, E-1891) turned out to be a
single defect and had to be merged afterward.

## The line

E-1889's description already names the spawn handoff as one of three doc
sources. This narrows that to the exact text. In the todo handoff template,
under `internal` templatecmd templates handoff todo.md.tmpl, step 4 reads:

> Stay focused on E-NNNN. File unrelated discoveries as new tasks
> (`--cleans-up E-NNNN`) and confirm before implementing them — **don't fix
> them inline.**

Two problems, beyond the own-work-bug distinction E-1889 already covers:

1. **Filing is the default action**, with no test for whether the finding
   merits a task at all.
2. **Inline fixing is explicitly forbidden.** So an agent that finds a
   one-word fix inside the blast radius of the work it is already doing is
   instructed to file it instead. That is not a misreading — it is the
   template working as written.

## The missing test

Mike's stated criterion: auto-filing helps, but not when the discovery could
*reasonably* be done in the current session, and not when several filings
should have been one. The handoff should carry both tests alongside the file
instruction:

- Could this reasonably be done now, inside the work already underway? If so,
  do it and report it — do not file it.
- Do the things I am about to file share a root cause? If so, file the cause,
  not the symptoms.

## Why this matters more than it looks

Backlog size is not free on this project — pending worktrees are what gate the
planned Python-to-Go port. Every reflexive filing lands on that critical path.
A useful third nudge would be surfacing backlog pressure at file time (the
count of open unplanned tasks), so the cost is visible at the moment the
decision is made.

## Relationship to sibling tasks

- **E-1890** (the tooling hint) is the enforcement counterpart, but it triggers
  on `--cleans-up X` where X was landed recently by this session. The
  could-this-be-done-now case is broader — it applies while the work is still
  underway, not after landing.
- **E-1739** (semantic-dup deny) catches *the same task filed twice*. It would
  NOT have caught E-1888 and E-1891: different tuples, different symptoms,
  different files, not semantically similar — yet one root cause. The
  same-session root-cause check is a distinct mechanism from backlog-wide
  similarity, and Endless already has the data for it in the session-to-task
  `surfaced` relations.

# Analysis — the dead-pane reaper can destroy live pane bindings project-wide

## Two defects, both required for the damage

### 1. The reaper trusts an ambient tmux view it never validates

`monitor.ReapDeadTmuxPanes` (internal/monitor/reap.go) decides liveness with:

    exec.Command("tmux", "list-panes", "-a", "-F", "#{pane_id}")

It inherits whatever `$TMUX` the calling process has. Any caller running under a
DIFFERENT tmux server — a private `tmux -L <socket>` server started by a test or
a verify script — sees only that server's panes. Every real pane then looks dead
and the whole project is reaped. There is no check that the observed pane set is
plausible for the rows about to be ended.

The `len(alive) == 0` branch is the sharpest edge: it nulls `process` for EVERY
non-ended tmux-format row in the project in one statement. Its comment treats an
empty pane set as proof that everything is dead; it is equally consistent with
"I am looking at the wrong server."

`internal/tmuxcmd/reset.go` already guards its own entry point (refuses when
`$TMUX` is empty, calling it "a footgun"). The SessionStart caller in
`internal/hookcmd/claude.go` has no such guard, and that is the one that fires
constantly.

### 2. TouchSession cannot undo it

    process = COALESCE(NULLIF(?, ''), process)
    state   = CASE WHEN sessions.state = 'ended' THEN 'needs_input' ELSE state END

A later hook firing with an EMPTY `TMUX_PANE` flips the row back to
`needs_input` but leaves `process` NULL. The row now reads as alive and resolves
to nothing, permanently — pane lookup keys on `process`. Only a hook that fires
WITH a pane can heal it, which is why sessions actively running tools recovered
and idle ones did not.

## Observed damage (2026-08-05)

- 27 live Claude panes had their session row at `state='ended'`, `process` NULL,
  while the pane was demonstrably alive and working in that task's worktree.
- 59 of 61 tmux windows rendered a blank status line simultaneously.
- Only 3 sessions were intact — exactly the ones firing hooks with `TMUX_PANE`
  set at the time.
- Reap batches are visible in the ledger by minute, including one batch of 37.

The blank bar is invisible by construction: `runStatusLine` maps every failure
to the same placeholder (E-1895), so this destroyed state for hours with no
diagnostic anywhere.

## Absorbed from E-1895: the failure was invisible by construction

`internal/tmuxcmd/status_line.go` `runStatusLine` maps EVERY error from
`monitor.GetPaneStatus` to `placeholder()` and stays silent on stderr:

    status, err := monitor.GetPaneStatus(pane)
    if err != nil {
        // Real error (DB unreachable, etc.). Render placeholder; stay
        // silent on stderr to avoid log spam during interactive use.
        fmt.Print(placeholder())
        return
    }

`monitor.DB()` alone has ~7 fail-closed exits behind that single `err` (the
schema apply, five enum VerifyIntegrity gates, guardWorktreeDBContext). All of
them render as the same dim dot as "this pane has no Endless context", and write
nothing anywhere. That is why the 2026-08-05 incident destroyed state for hours
with no diagnostic, and why three separate hypotheses had to be eliminated
experimentally before the cause was found.

The stderr silence is CORRECT and must stay: the bar re-execs this binary once
per pane every `status-interval` (2s across ~14 panes), so logging would be a
firehose painted over a live TUI. `faults.Record` is the right shape instead —
it dedupes an open incident in place, so a bar blanking every 2s across every
pane raises ONE incident. `cmd/endless-go/main.go` already calls `faults.Bind`
for every subcommand, so the recorder is available with no new wiring.

Scope note: this is NOT E-1884 (converting 42 `log.Printf` sites that write too
noisily). This is the inverse — a site that writes nothing when it should.

## Directions (not locked — this needs a plan)

- Refuse to reap on an implausible pane set: if `alive` is empty, or disjoint
  from every stored `process` for the project, treat it as "wrong server" and
  no-op rather than reaping.
- Pin the server identity: record which tmux server a session belongs to
  (socket path) and only reap rows for that server.
- Make the damage recoverable: reviving `ended` to `needs_input` while leaving
  `process` NULL should not be possible — either restore both or neither.
- Consider whether SessionStart is the right trigger at all, given it fires from
  contexts whose `$TMUX` is not the user's server.

# Analysis — a test or verify run must not touch the user's real machine state

One invariant, two gaps. E-1900 was folded in here: the leak and the rule that
prevents the next one are the same unit of work.

## Gap 1 — Go tests leak the log directory

`go test ./...` writes into the REAL log dir under the user's config. Observed
2026-08-05, hook.log carried fixture data mid-run: `bound session uuid-real to
dispatch row short_id feed1234`, and an `auto-registered project: 003` whose
path is a Go test temp dir. The DB IS isolated — no fixture projects or sessions
appear in the real database — so only the log path escapes.

It matters because it corrupts the one artifact you reach for when diagnosing a
live incident: real and synthetic entries interleave with nothing marking which
is which.

## Gap 2 — nothing tells a verify-script author the isolation rule

Add a short subsection to `docs/guide/orchestration.md`, under the per-task
verification suite guidance, stating the isolation contract a suite must meet.

## The rule

A verification suite may never start a tmux server, or run `endless-go`, without
isolating BOTH:

- **tmux config** — start private servers with `tmux -L <socket> -f /dev/null`,
  so the user's `~/.tmux.conf` (and any hook it installs, e.g. `session-created`
  -> `endless tmux init`) cannot fire against the throwaway server.
- **`XDG_CONFIG_HOME`** — point it at a throwaway directory for the server
  process, so every descendant (anything the suite spawns, and anything THOSE
  spawn) resolves its config dir, and therefore its database, away from
  `~/.config/endless/endless.db`.

Kill the server and remove the temp dirs in a trap on exit.

## Why the second one is load-bearing

Inside a private tmux server, `$TMUX` names a server with a handful of panes.
Any endless-go code path that decides liveness from `tmux list-panes -a` — most
importantly `monitor.ReapDeadTmuxPanes` — will conclude that every pane it does
not see is dead. Pointed at the user's real database, that nulls `process` for
every live session in the project and blanks every tmux status line on the
machine (observed 2026-08-05: 27 orphaned sessions, 59 of 61 windows blank).
Isolating the config dir means the worst such a path can do is damage a temp DB.

`-f /dev/null` alone is NOT sufficient: it only blocks config-file hooks, not
processes the suite launches itself.

## Reference implementation

`tests/tasks/e-1851-verify.sh` does both, with the reasoning inline at each
`new-session` call. Point the guide at it rather than restating the code.

## Related

- E-1898 is the product-side backstop (the reaper should refuse an implausible
  pane set instead of trusting an ambient `$TMUX`). This task is the authoring
  convention that keeps suites from tripping it in the first place.

# Absorbed tasks (E-1642, E-1468, E-1408)

This task became the umbrella for session<->pane binding integrity. Three
pre-existing tasks were folded in and marked obsolete; their content is
preserved below so nothing is re-derived.

## From E-1642 — close sessions on idle-timeout instead of mass-end sweeps

Original description: SessionEnd/EndSession rarely fires (the harness is killed,
not cleanly exited), so sessions linger until a later reaper/collision sweep
marks a batch 'ended' at one shared instant. last_activity is bumped far past
real life, durations span days, and duration stops being a usable "real session"
signal. End sessions on last_activity + idle-timeout rather than wall-clock
sweep time.

CORRECTION, from the 2026-08-05 incident: E-1642's plan opens with a "Recon
correction" asserting there is NO reaper and that clustered mass-end timestamps
come from bulk/collision events only. That is wrong. monitor.ReapDeadTmuxPanes
IS a reaper; it is not periodic but fires on EVERY SessionStart
(internal/hookcmd/claude.go:185) and mass-ends by design — the `len(alive) == 0`
branch ends every tmux-format row in the project in a single UPDATE. The batch
of 37 rows sharing one timestamp is that branch, not a bulk event. Any plan
carried forward from E-1642 must be re-read against this.

E-1642's plan as filed, preserved verbatim:

# E-1642 — Close sessions on idle-timeout (there is no reaper today)

**Independent.** · **Layer:** Go (`internal/monitor/session.go`) + a trigger

## Recon correction
There is **NO periodic reaper**. Sessions reach `ended` only via `EndSession` on `SessionEnd`
(`session.go:511-523`, rarely fires — harness is killed, not cleanly exited) or collision-
invalidation (`session.go:280-292`, inert when `process` is empty). So real dead sessions linger
`working`/`idle` indefinitely; the clustered "mass-end" timestamps come from bulk/collision
events, not a reaper. The fix is to **add** truthful idle-timeout ending.

## Why it matters
`duration` is currently a lie (a real session can span days), so it can't signal "the real
session." E-1645's resolver and the dashboard both want reliable `state` + `last_activity`.

## Approach
1. **Idle-timeout sweep:** any session in `working`/`idle`/`needs_input` whose `last_activity` is
   older than a configurable window (e.g. 60-90 min; align with the ~1h bg idle) → mark `ended`
   with end == **`last_activity`, not `now()`** (don't bump the timestamp). `EndSession` today
   updates `last_activity` (511-523) — the idle path must NOT.
2. **Trigger** (no daemon exists): BOTH (a) a cheap project-scoped stale-sweep piggybacked inside
   `TouchSession` (runs every hook event → self-heals during activity), and (b) an explicit
   `endless session sweep [--dry-run]` for manual/cron/tmux use.
3. **Config:** idle window in `.endless/config.json` (go-cfgstore) with a sane default.

## Risks
- Don't end a session legitimately parked on `needs_input` — longer timeout/exemption for it.
- Harness resumes on wake (v2.1.142+); base the decision on `last_activity` heartbeats, not
  wall-clock since spawn, so a machine-sleep gap doesn't end a live session.

## Verification — create a per-task verify script
Create `tests/tasks/e-1642-verify.sh` in the `e-1624-verify.sh` shape (bash, `set -u`, the
`section`/`report_*`/`summary` helpers, `cd` repo root, ensure `go.work`, exit 0/1/2). Drive the
REAL code path via Go tests in `internal/monitor` plus the `endless session sweep` CLI.

The script asserts (named checks):
- `internal/monitor` compiles.
- A Go test drives a `working`/`idle` session whose `last_activity` is older than the timeout and
  asserts it flips to `ended` with end == the **historical** `last_activity` (NOT `now()`).
- A recent (within-timeout) session is left untouched.
- A `needs_input` session honors its longer leniency (not ended at the short timeout).
- `endless session sweep --dry-run` lists **exactly** the stale sessions it would end (seed via
  fresh ids); `internal/monitor` full suite stays green.

Re-runnability (sandbox NOT wiped between runs):
- Derive seeded ids/`session_id`/`short_id` from freshly-allocated ids each run; set
  `last_activity` relative to a computed "now minus N" each run, never a fixed timestamp.
- Capture seeding output; `exit 2` loudly on any setup/seed error (never /dev/null).
- Run the script at least TWICE before declaring it done.

**Verify-handoff — tell the user to verify with (only) this:**
```
esu && ./tests/tasks/e-1642-verify.sh
```




## From E-1468 — collision invalidation ends rows with no liveness check

internal/monitor/session.go collision invalidation sets state='ended' for every
other sessions row sharing the incoming process (pane) string, with no liveness
check. When two Claude session identities share one physical tmux pane (e.g. a
worktree-keyed session and a main-checkout-keyed session during a land run from
main), the live session is falsely marked ended. Repro: E-1459 land run from the
main checkout spawned queue-operation session a27e5710 on pane %203, flipping
live session 510 to ended. Proposed fix: verify the prior occupant is actually
stale (tmux list-panes / last_activity recency / project-dir match) before
invalidating.

Note its description is partly stale: it says "TouchSession upserts never
restore state", but E-1686 has since added the ended -> needs_input revive. The
liveness-check principle still stands, and is the SAME principle the reaper
needs — which is why these belong together.

## From E-1408 — SessionStart must not silently capture an empty TMUX_PANE

The SessionStart hook reads TMUX_PANE via os.Getenv and writes it to the
companion file; PaneID has json:omitempty so an empty value drops out of the
JSON entirely. Downstream, sibling detection never matches and `endless task
bind` fails. Mike's directive on that task: silent degradation is unacceptable —
the hook MUST fail when it cannot capture pane_id, and subsequent hooks should
keep failing until resolved. Evidence then: TMUX_PANE='' in both the Claude env
and the parent shell env despite TMUX being set.

This is the upstream cause of the incident's unrecoverability: TouchSession
writes `process = COALESCE(NULLIF(excluded.process,''), sessions.process)`, so a
hook firing with an empty TMUX_PANE revives `state` while leaving `process`
NULL — the row then reads alive and resolves to nothing, permanently.

## Related, NOT absorbed

E-1395 (unverified) fixed the Python `_tmux_window_pane_ids` running `tmux
list-panes` without `-t`. Same bug class as the reaper's ambient view; precedent
for the fix, no action needed here.
