# E-1889 — Make reopening your own landed work the documented, tooled norm

Absorbs E-1890 (tooling counterpart). Every decision below is settled; there are
no open questions. Where a choice had a plausible alternative, the rejected one
is recorded so it is not relitigated.

## Problem

Agents reflexively file a new task for a bug they just introduced rather than
reopening the task that introduced it. The result is backlog growth, which on
this project is not free — pending worktrees gate the planned Python-to-Go port,
so every reflexive filing lands on the critical path.

Reproduced live in the E-1845 session: four tasks filed during one task, two of
which (E-1888, E-1891) turned out to be a single defect and had to be merged
afterward, and one of which (E-1894) rested on a category error and was retired.

The cause is not agent carelessness. The handoff template instructs exactly this
behavior.

## Settled decisions

| # | Decision | Rejected alternative |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | `task reopen` is aligned to land `revisit`, like the other two reopen paths. Code change, not just docs. | Documenting the three paths' divergence as intentional. |
| 2 | Five templates get the full rewording; `brainstorm` keeps "file as new tasks" (that IS its deliverable) and gains only the root-cause test. | One wording across all six. |
| 3 | Mermaid gains `confirmed`/`assumed`/`completed` → `revisit`. `declined`/`obsolete` stay terminal in the diagram. | Drawing all five reopenable statuses. |
| 4 | Tooling folds into E-1889; E-1890 is absorbed and marked obsolete. | Keeping E-1890 for the recently-landed hint. |
| 5 | Claim promotion gains `revisit`. | Routing `spawn --reopen` through re-approval. |
| 6 | `_REOPEN_TO_REVISIT` narrows to E-1555's set; `declined`/`obsolete` are no longer implicitly revived. | Broadening `task reopen` to accept them. |
| 7 | Handoff uses the four-case bulleted form. | Compact prose; minimal edit. |
| 8 | `revisit` definition broadens to a two-case sentence. | Terse form; form with explicit pointer. |
| 9 | Guide pattern lives in `orchestration.md`, cross-referenced from `tasks.md`. | `tasks.md` only; `orchestration.md` with no pointer. |
| 10 | Verification splits by durability: behavior into the real suites, acceptance into the verify script. | Everything in one verify script. |
| 11 | `session resume --reopen` on `declined`/`obsolete` refuses loudly and names the explicit route. | Silently skipping the flip; a `--force` override. |

## A. Handoff templates

Under `internal` templatecmd templates handoff. Five files carry byte-identical
text at the noted lines: `todo.md.tmpl:12`, `bugfix.md.tmpl:14`,
`epic.md.tmpl:25`, `research.md.tmpl:14`, `respawn.md.tmpl:45`. Replace with:


# Scope extension — the "could this be done now?" test

Contributed from the E-1845 session, which reproduced this failure live: four
tasks filed during one task, two of which (E-1888, E-1891) turned out to be a
single defect and had to be merged afterward.

## The line

E-1889's description already names the spawn handoff as one of three doc
sources. This narrows that to the exact text. In the todo handoff template,
under `internal` templatecmd templates handoff todo.md.tmpl, step 4 reads:

> Stay focused on E-NNNN. File unrelated discoveries as new tasks
> (`--cleans-up E-NNNN`) and confirm before implementing them — **don't fix
> them inline.**

Two problems, beyond the own-work-bug distinction E-1889 already covers:

1. **Filing is the default action**, with no test for whether the finding
   merits a task at all.
2. **Inline fixing is explicitly forbidden.** So an agent that finds a
   one-word fix inside the blast radius of the work it is already doing is
   instructed to file it instead. That is not a misreading — it is the
   template working as written.

## The missing test

Mike's stated criterion: auto-filing helps, but not when the discovery could
*reasonably* be done in the current session, and not when several filings
should have been one. The handoff should carry both tests alongside the file
instruction:

- Could this reasonably be done now, inside the work already underway? If so,
  do it and report it — do not file it.
- Do the things I am about to file share a root cause? If so, file the cause,
  not the symptoms.

## Why this matters more than it looks

A backlog is never free, on any project. Every filed task is a standing claim on
future attention: it must be read, re-read, and triaged past on every pass,
whether or not it is ever worked. A task filed reflexively does not defer the
cost of the discovery — it converts a small immediate cost into a recurring one.

On Endless itself that cost is currently visible as pending worktrees gating a
planned Python-to-Go port, but that is one instance of the cost, not the reason
for it.
A useful third nudge would be surfacing backlog pressure at file time (the
count of open unplanned tasks), so the cost is visible at the moment the
decision is made.

## Relationship to sibling tasks

- **E-1890** (the tooling hint) is the enforcement counterpart, but it triggers
  on `--cleans-up X` where X was landed recently by this session. The
  could-this-be-done-now case is broader — it applies while the work is still
  underway, not after landing.
- **E-1739** (semantic-dup deny) catches *the same task filed twice*. It would
  NOT have caught E-1888 and E-1891: different tuples, different symptoms,
  different files, not semantically similar — yet one root cause. The
  same-session root-cause check is a distinct mechanism from backlog-wide
  similarity, and Endless already has the data for it in the session-to-task
  `surfaced` relations.

fields.description: One root cause, one visibility gap. ROOT: `ReapDeadTmuxPanes` NULLs `process` for panes it cannot see, deciding that from an ambient $TMUX it never validates — so a caller under a foreign tmux server nulls every session row in the project, and TouchSession's COALESCE (correct, added by E-1426) is left with nothing to protect; rows then read alive with no pane, forever. Observed 2026-08-05: 27 orphaned panes, 59 of 61 status lines blank. VISIBILITY: the status line collapses every failure into one placeholder, so it ran for hours untraced, and a not-ended row with no process is incoherent and must fail loudly. Umbrella: absorbs E-1895, E-1468, E-1408 (stale) and E-1642 (idle-timeout must fill the gap that guarding the reaper opens).

correct — `--reason` is `task decline`'s flag, stored as outcome. Do not
"fix" it.

## D. Guide pattern — "Fix a bug in your own landed work"

New section in `docs/guide/orchestration.md`, near the existing `--reopen`
material (currently around the `task spawn --reopen` line). It must cover:

1. **The judgment.** A bug in work you just landed is not new work. Reopen the
   task that introduced it rather than filing a peer.
2. **The mechanics.** `task update <id> --status revisit`, then reuse the
   task's existing worktree rather than creating a second one for the same work.
3. **Re-verification.** The task's verify script still exists and still applies;
   re-run it rather than authoring a second one.
4. **The boundary.** When a genuinely separate task IS right — the discovery is
   new work the conversation surfaced, not a defect in what shipped.

One-line cross-reference from `tasks.md` under the status material, pointing
here.

## E. Code — reopen alignment

1. **`_reopen_task_core`** (`src/endless/task_cmd.py`, around the
   `new_status = "ready" if text_present else "unplanned"` line): always
   `revisit`. Keep returning `text_present` — callers use it for the message
   suffix — but stop branching status on it. Update the `reopen_item` docstring,
   which currently says "back to `ready` or `unplanned`".

2. **Five stale help/comment sites** assert the old target and must be updated
   in the same change: `task_cmd.py` at the spawn-reopen docstring, the
   `--reopen` help string, and the two reopen pre-step comments; plus the
   matching `--reopen` help text in `cli.py`.

3. **`_REOPEN_TO_REVISIT`** (`src/endless/session_cmd.py`): narrow to
   `{confirmed, assumed, completed}`, matching `_REOPENABLE_TERMINAL_STATUSES`.
   In `_resolve_resume`, refuse when `--reopen` targets a `declined`/`obsolete`
   task:

   ```
   Error: E-123 is 'declined' — a deliberate decision, not dormant work.
   Reviving it is an explicit act:
       endless task update E-123 --status revisit
   Then resume without --reopen.
   ```

   Follows the loud-failure-on-invalid-state convention used by the verb,
   maybe-parent, and db gates.

4. **Claim promotion** (`internal/monitor/session.go`): add `revisit` to the
   `status IN (...)` set. Without it, `task spawn --reopen` would bind a session
   and leave the task reading as not-started. The background-session gate is a
   separate check and is unchanged — background sessions remain restricted to
   `ready`.

## F. Code — three file-time hints

All three fire from `task add`. **Hints, never refusals** — sometimes a
genuinely separate task IS right, and the distinction needs human judgment.
Follow the existing gate/hint conventions.

1. **Recently landed.** When `--cleans-up X` names a task that the CURRENT
   session landed within 24h (join `task_landings` on `task_id` + `session_id`,
   filter `landed_at`), print: *"E-X was landed by this session Nh ago —
   consider `task update E-X --status revisit` and fixing it there."*

2. **Backlog pressure.** Print the count of open (`untriaged`/`unplanned`)
   tasks in the project, so the cost of adding one is visible at the moment the
   decision is made.

3. **Same-session root cause.** When this session has already filed at least one
   task (its `surfaced` rows in `session_tasks`), list them and ask whether the
   new one shares a root cause with any — *"file the cause, not the symptoms."*

   This is the mechanism that would have caught E-1888/E-1891. E-1739's
   semantic-dup gate provably would NOT have: those two were different files,
   different tuples, different symptoms, not semantically similar — yet one
   defect. Backlog-wide *similarity* and same-session *common cause* are
   different checks; E-1739 stays independent and is not superseded.

## Verification

**Real suites — permanent invariants:**

- pytest: `task reopen` lands `revisit` from each of the three reopenable
  statuses; `session resume --reopen` refuses on `declined`/`obsolete` and still
  works on the three; each hint fires when its condition holds and stays silent
  otherwise; no hint ever blocks the add.
- go test: claim promotion moves `revisit` → `underway`; the background-session
  gate still refuses non-`ready`.
- Mermaid byte-identity across the three copies belongs here too — it is a
  permanent invariant currently asserted in three separate verify scripts
  (e-1648, e-1832, e-1845). Promote it to a real test as part of this task and
  the copies stop multiplying.

**`tests/tasks/e-1889-verify.sh` — point-in-time acceptance only:**

- the four-case wording is present in all five templates;
- `brainstorm.md.tmpl` retains its own sentence and gained the root-cause line;
- the guide pattern section exists in `orchestration.md` with the cross-reference
  from `tasks.md`;
- the `revisit` table row reads as specified.

## Absorbed / superseded

- **E-1890** — absorbed. Mark obsolete with an outcome naming this task. Its
  recently-landed hint is section F.1 verbatim, including the 24h window and the
  hint-never-refusal constraint.
- **E-1739** — NOT superseded. Different check (see F.3).
- **E-1623** — unaffected, but note that promoting the mermaid assertion into a
  real test removes one of the duplicated blocks it would otherwise retrofit.
fields.analysis:
# Provenance — what was observed in the E-1845 session

Kept deliberately short: this field records only how the scope extension was
discovered. The specification, decisions, and deliverables live in the plan, and
are not restated here.

During a single task (E-1845, adding the `untriaged` status), the session filed
four new tasks:

- **E-1888** and **E-1891** — filed as separate bugs, both about a status list
  that had drifted from `cli.TASK_STATUSES`. Mike identified them as two
  symptoms of one defect; E-1888 was later absorbed into E-1891, which was
  re-scoped to the root cause.
- **E-1894** — filed to add CI so per-task verify scripts could not "rot
  silently". Retired as a category error: a per-task acceptance harness becoming
  invalid after its task lands is its expected end state, not a defect.
- **E-1899** — remove `task list --tree`, filed at Mike's explicit invitation.

So of four filings, one was sound, one was over-fragmentation the user had to
clean up, one rested on a false premise, and one was requested.

The agent's behavior was not a misreading of its instructions. The handoff
template told it to file discoveries and explicitly forbade fixing them inline.
That line is deliverable A of this task.

fields.text:
# E-1898 — the reaper must observe, never infer

## What this task is

`monitor.ReapDeadTmuxPanes` closes session rows whose tmux pane it believes is
gone. It decides that from `tmux list-panes -a` against an ambient `$TMUX` it
never validates, so a caller attached to a different tmux server concludes every
real pane is dead and NULLs `process` for the whole project. Rows then read
alive with no pane, permanently, and every tmux status line goes blank.

Observed 2026-08-05: 27 orphaned panes, 59 of 61 windows blank, unresolvable for
hours because the status line renders every failure as the same dim dot.

## Terminology (fix this first — it caused real confusion)

"Reaping" here is a **database write only**. The reaper's entire effect is:

    UPDATE sessions SET state='ended', process=NULL, last_activity=? WHERE ...

It never kills a pane, never touches tmux state. `ReapDeadTmuxPanes` reads as
"kill dead tmux panes"; it means "close rows whose pane is gone." **Rename it**
— proposed `CloseSessionsForDeadPanes` — and fix the doc comment to lead with
"writes only to `sessions`; never mutates tmux."

## Root cause, singular

The reaper destroys the value that `TouchSession`'s COALESCE exists to protect.

`process = COALESCE(NULLIF(excluded.process,''), sessions.process)` is correct
and stays: it means "use the pane I was handed, else keep the one on the row."
It was added by E-1426 specifically to fix E-1408 and it still does that job.
But once the reaper has NULLed `process`, there is no known-good value left to
protect, and a later hook with an empty `TMUX_PANE` revives `state` to
`needs_input` while `process` stays NULL. That row — not ended, no pane — is
incoherent, reads as alive, and resolves to nothing forever.

**No change to TouchSession's COALESCE.** Fix the reaper and the trap closes.

## Locked decisions

### D1 — `@server_uuid` is a GATE, not a stored column

No schema change. The reaper reads `@server_uuid` from the server `$TMUX` points
at. Empty means this server was never initialized by Endless — a private
`tmux -L` server, or a fresh one mid-init — so **refuse and record a fault**.

Rejected: adding `sessions.server_uuid`. It would couple the sessions table more
tightly to tmux and store a value identical across every live row.

Rejected: encoding `<server_uuid>:<pane>` into `process`. Twelve-plus call sites
compare `process` to a raw pane id (`tmux_lookup.go` x3, `session.go` collision
invalidation, `session_nav.go`, `events/session_status.go`, both reapers' GLOB),
the `channels` table keys on the same string, and `process` already holds
non-tmux values like `pid:1234`. Every missed site would fail **silently** by
simply not matching — the exact failure class this task exists to remove.

### D2 — guards run cheapest-first, expensive only when damage is imminent

    1. cheap   own server has @server_uuid?            no  -> refuse + fault
    2. cheap   any rows actually about to be closed?   none -> done
    3. costly  enumerate peer servers; another live one has a uuid?
                                                       yes -> refuse + fault

Step 3 costs nothing in the common case (nothing to close) and is bounded when
it matters. Enumeration is proven reliable: list sockets in
`dirname $(tmux display-message -p '#{socket_path}')`, query each for
`@server_uuid`, skip your own. Live-and-initialized returns the uuid with rc=0;
live-but-uninitialized and stale sockets both return empty with rc=1, cleanly
distinguishable.

Accepted limitation, documented in the code: servers started with `tmux -S
<path>` outside that directory, or under a relocated `TMUX_TMPDIR`, are not
enumerable. Neither is common; the failure mode is the status quo, not worse.

Two coexisting initialized servers are **guarded, not forbidden** — the reaper
declines while the ambiguity exists rather than `tmux apply` refusing to run.
Self-correcting: kill the second server and reaping resumes.

### D3 — the death test becomes an observation, not an inference

Today: "pane absent from `list-panes`". That is sufficient for death but not
necessary — a Claude session whose harness was killed leaves its pane alive
running a shell, and the reaper never notices.

New test: **pane absent OR the pane is running a known shell**
(`zsh`/`bash`/`sh`/`fish`).

This requires fixing a live bug next door. `monitor.paneIsRunningClaude` matches
`cmd == "claude" || cmd == "claude-code"`, but Claude Code sets its process title
to its version — every real Claude pane reports `pane_current_command` =
`2.1.212`. The helper therefore returns false for every live Claude pane, so
`GetPaneStatus`'s `PaneStatusClaudeNoSession` branch never fires correctly.

Fix by **inverting the test**: detect the shell, not the Claude. Shell names are
stable; a version string changes every release. Keep a positively-named helper
(`paneIsRunningShell`) and have the status-line path consume it.

### D4 — idle-timeout is NOT in scope; E-1642 stays obsolete

D3 replaces it. Positive detection covers "Claude died, pane lives" without
inferring death from silence, and therefore cannot close a session that is
merely idle — the failure mode E-1642's plan had to add a longer `needs_input`
window to mitigate. No config knob, no land-path sweep, no new CLI verb.

Consequently the earlier decision to trigger a sweep on `worktree land` is moot:
there is no sweep.

### D5 — a `process`-less live row raises a fault; it is NEVER auto-corrected

A row that is not `ended` and has no `process` is incoherent by construction.
Sweeping such rows would destroy the evidence that diagnosed this incident.
Record a fault naming the row; leave it exactly as it is.

### D6 — `endless tmux reset --force` bypasses the guards

The explicit operator verb keeps an escape hatch. Without `--force` it obeys D2
identically to the hook path. `--force` must print what it is overriding.

### D7 — `runInit` no longer calls `runReset(nil)`

Under D1 that call can never do anything: `runInit` stamps `@server_uuid` LAST
(deliberately, so a crash mid-init leaves the gate open for retry), so at reset
time the gate always refuses. Remove the call rather than leave a
destructive-looking no-op for someone to later "fix" by removing the gate.

This is also the trigger for the 37-row batch in the ledger: a fresh tmux server
firing `session-created -> endless tmux init` reaped the whole project against a
one-pane view. After a genuine restart, the next SessionStart still closes the
old rows correctly, once the uuid is stamped.

### D8 — the status line records a fault instead of swallowing (absorbed E-1895)

`runStatusLine` maps every `GetPaneStatus` error to `placeholder()` and stays
silent. `monitor.DB()` alone has ~7 fail-closed exits behind that one `err`.

Keep the bar output unchanged and keep stderr silent — the bar re-execs once per
pane every 2s, so logging would be a firehose over a live TUI. Use
`faults.Record`, which dedupes an open incident in place, so a bar blanking
across every pane raises ONE incident. `main.go` already calls `faults.Bind` for
every subcommand.

### D9 — collision invalidation must prove staleness (absorbed E-1468)

`TouchSession`'s collision path ends every other row sharing the incoming pane
string with no liveness check. It is the second write path that destroys a
binding on an unproven assumption. Apply the same principle: confirm the prior
occupant is actually stale before invalidating.

## Implementation order

1. Rename + doc comment (D-terminology). Mechanical, lands alone.
2. D1 + D2 guards, D5 fault, D7 removal — the urgent data-loss fix.
3. D3 death test + `paneIsRunningShell`, and repoint the status-line consumer.
4. D8 status-line fault.
5. D9 collision staleness.
6. D6 `--force`.

Steps 1-2 are independently landable and are the part that stops the bleeding.

## Tests — `tests/tasks/e-1898-verify.sh`

Task checks fail-fast first, then project-wide regression. The suite must itself
obey the isolation rule (private `tmux -L` servers started with `-f /dev/null`
under a throwaway `XDG_CONFIG_HOME`, sockets removed in the trap) — see
`tests/tasks/e-1851-verify.sh` for the reference implementation.

**Layer A — unit, FAIL-FAST**
- Gate: with `@server_uuid` absent, the reaper closes nothing and records a
  fault. With it present, it proceeds.
- Peer check: with a second live initialized server present, the reaper closes
  nothing and records a fault; with only stale sockets around, it proceeds.
- Ordering: with nothing to close, no peer enumeration happens at all (assert
  via a seam counter — this is the cost guarantee).
- Death test: a row whose pane is absent closes; a row whose pane runs a shell
  closes; a row whose pane runs Claude does NOT.
- `paneIsRunningShell` returns true for zsh/bash/sh/fish and false for a
  version-string command such as `2.1.212` — the exact value the old helper got
  wrong.
- D5: a not-ended row with NULL `process` is never modified, and raises a fault.
- D9: collision invalidation leaves a demonstrably live prior occupant alone.

**Layer B — E2E against a private tmux server**
1. Seed a throwaway DB with sessions bound to panes on a private server.
2. Confirm the reaper closes rows for panes killed on that server.
3. Point it at a SECOND private server and confirm it closes NOTHING and
   records a fault — the regression test for this incident.
4. Confirm `endless tmux reset` refuses there, and `--force` proceeds and says
   what it overrode.

**Layer C — project-wide regression**: `go test ./...` and `just test`.

**Ledger-safety assertion (mandatory).** Count non-ended sessions holding a
`process` in the REAL database before and after the whole suite; they must be
equal. This suite exercises a destructive code path, and that count is the
thing this task exists to protect.

## Out of scope

- Idle-timeout / session-duration truthfulness (D4).
- Non-tmux session lifecycle (`pid:1234` rows) — needs its own mechanism.
- E-1884's 42 `log.Printf` conversions. D8 is the inverse defect (a site that
  writes nothing when it should) and does not pull that sweep in.
- Repairing rows already damaged. A one-off reconstruction was applied by hand on
  2026-08-05 (window name -> task id -> most recent session row for that task).
  If a supported repair verb is wanted later, file it then.

fields.description: Remove the unused indented-tree rendering behind 'endless task list --tree' and 'endless epic list --tree'. Both flags forward to one renderer (epic_cmd.list_epics wraps task_cmd.show_plan), so there is a single branch and a single glyph map to delete. The flat-list tree seemed useful when added but has gone unused; what is wanted instead is an interactive TUI tree, which is much larger scope and deliberately unfiled. Do NOT touch 'session status --tree' or 'session monitor --tree' — those are Go-backed, are the trees actually in use, and share only the flag name. See the plan for the exact site list and the second, unrelated glyph map that must survive.
fields.text:
# E-1899 — Remove the unused list tree

A removal checklist, not a design. The only risk in this task is deleting the
wrong `--tree`: there are four flags by that name and two identically-named
glyph maps, and the two flags you must NOT touch are the ones actually in use.

## One renderer, two flags

`epic_cmd.list_epics` is a thin wrapper that forwards `tree=tree` into
`task_cmd.show_plan` with `type_filter="epic"`. So `task list --tree` and
`epic list --tree` share a single implementation — there is ONE branch and ONE
glyph map to delete, not two.

## Remove

| Site | What |
|---|---|
| `cli.py:1225` | the `--tree/as_tree` option on `task list` |
| `cli.py:2521` | the `--tree/as_tree` option on `epic list` |
| `cli.py` (both bodies) | the `tree=as_tree` argument passed onward |
| `epic_cmd.list_epics` | the `tree` parameter and its pass-through to `show_plan` |
| `task_cmd.show_plan` | the `tree` parameter |
| `task_cmd.show_plan` | the `else: # Tree output` branch — the `by_id` / `children_of` / `_render` block, ending at the `_render(None, 1)` call |
| `task_cmd.py` ~:1100 | the `status_indicators` map that opens that branch |

After removal, `show_plan`'s `if not tree: _render_flat_table(rows)` collapses
to an unconditional `_render_flat_table(rows)`; the trailing `click.echo()` and
the `N item(s)` summary below the branch stay.

## Do NOT touch

- **The second `status_indicators` map** further down `task_cmd.py` (around
  :1243). Same name, different map — it serves `next_tasks` and is unrelated.
- **`session status --tree`** (`cli.py:815`) and **`session monitor --tree`**
  (`cli.py:839`). These are the trees actually in use. They are Go-backed
  (`internal/sessionstatuscmd`), reach the renderer through
  `session_status_resolve`, and share nothing with the list tree but the flag
  name.

## Verify

- `endless task list` and `endless epic list` still render the flat table, with
  filters, sorting, `--llm`, and `--json` unaffected.
- `--tree` is rejected as an unknown option on both.
- `endless session status --tree` and `endless session monitor --tree` still
  render their trees.
- Existing pytest suites pass; add a case only if one asserted the removed
  output.

## Not in scope

An interactive TUI tree — what is actually wanted instead of this — is a much
larger piece of work and is deliberately unfiled.

## Note for E-1891

The deleted glyph map is the per-row lookup cited in E-1891's plan as the one
place worth measuring for subprocess cost. Landing this first dissolves that
concern rather than answering it.

payload.title: Enforce verbatim task report relay with a Stop-hook detector that blocks appended agent prose
payload.description: E-1803 adds a compose-time nudge at task report checkpoints and explicitly disclaims enforcement ("a strong nudge, not a hard gate"). Agents override the nudge because the override disguises itself as thoroughness. This task adds the missing teeth: a Stop-hook detector that blocks the turn until the final message exactly matches the sanctioned report output, and names the violation where both agent and user see it.
payload.text:
Mechanism (three parts):

1. Invert the default. The task report output IS the sanctioned user-facing message (already shown to the user as tool output). Move the two legitimate exceptions INTO the report so no prose outside it is ever justified:
   - the task's single verify command becomes a report field;
   - genuine open decisions/blockers go through the report's --json notes/questions channel (already E-1803's model).

2. Record the checkpoint. The report command marks the session turn as a verbatim-relay checkpoint and stores the exact sanctioned text.

3. Gate at Stop. A Stop hook compares the agent's actual final message to the sanctioned text; anything beyond it returns decision:block with a reason the user also sees ("appended N lines beyond the report; resend verbatim"). Compliant = empty or exactly-sanctioned; prose becomes the caught exception, not a discretionary default.

Keystone: routing the verify command and open decisions through the report as FIELDS is what collapses the Stop-hook check from an intractable 'is this prose a legitimate question or a banned recap' judgment into a hard equality check. Without it the gate has false positives; with it, prose-outside-the-report is always a violation.
payload.analysis:
WHY A DETECTOR, NOT A LOUDER REMINDER. The override survives every instruction because it disguises itself as thoroughness — the agent does not experience appending as defiance but as diligence, so a reminder (however forceful) gets reinterpreted rather than obeyed. You cannot fix a disguise with another instruction; the lever must be a detector that catches the act and NAMES it deterministically, stripping the 'I am just being thorough' cover.

WHY IT CREATES DISCOMFORT (the design goal Mike stated). The anticipated catch is deterministic and public: appending stops being 'thorough' and becomes 'get bounced and labelled a rule-break, every time.' The consequence — not the reminder — is what suppresses the urge.

HONEST CEILING (do not oversell). Claude Code cannot force tool output to literally BE the agent's message, and a re-prompted model can comply-then-drift on a later turn. This is a hard gate on the specific checkpoint (block until clean), not a guarantee the urge never fires. It raises the override's cost from zero to 'publicly caught and bounced,' the strongest in-harness lever short of a full regenerate loop. Scope is the report-gated checkpoints E-1803 defines; broadening to every agent message is a separate, larger question.

PROVENANCE. Surfaced when the E-1818 handoff agent overrode task report's explicit 'relay these lines, add nothing' instruction and appended ~4 paragraphs of reproduction/fix/regression recap — the exact E-1785 failure, and the exact enforcement gap E-1803 disclaims.

fields.text:
# Enforce non-empty task description at the event-emit choke point

## Goal
Block the AI agent from creating a task with an empty `description`, while leaving
human/manual creation free to omit it. Enforcement sits at the single
`endless-go event emit` seam, ahead of the JSONL WAL append, so it covers every
path that reaches the ledger.

## Scope (finalized): AI-only
The rule fires only when the `task.created` event is attributed to a live Claude
session — i.e. the event's actor carries a `session_id`. Manual/human creation
(`--no-session` -> `actor.kind=system`, no `session_id`) is exempt by design:
humans may file a bare title, and a background process augments the description
later (separate follow-up, below).

Note the discriminator is *"actor is session-attributed"*, NOT `actor.kind ==
"session"`. A `endless task add` run by the agent emits `actor.kind="cli"` WITH a
`session_id` bound (see `internal/events/event.go` `Actor{Kind, ID, SessionID}`).
Key the gate on `Actor.SessionID` being present.

## Change
1. In `endless-go event emit`, at the validation step that runs BEFORE the JSONL
   append, add a rule:
   - event type == `task.created`, AND
   - actor is session-attributed (`Actor.SessionID` present), AND
   - payload `description` is empty / whitespace-only
   -> reject with a non-zero exit and an agent-optimized stderr message.
2. Message: crafted for an agent reader — name the exact fix (`--description`
   with a short one-line spec) and clarify `--text` is the long-form plan, not a
   substitute. Actionable, no internal jargon.
3. Confirm the Python `task add` surfaces the Go stderr verbatim into the agent's
   tool output (it shells out to `endless-go event emit`). If it wraps or swallows
   the message, fix propagation so the crafted string reaches the agent.

## Must-verify during implementation
- Exact location of the JSONL append vs validation in the emit path — the check
  MUST precede the append (JSONL = WAL invariant; a rejected event must never land
  in the log).
- The precise actor field that marks "live session" (`Actor.SessionID`) and that a
  session-run `endless task add` actually carries it.
- That web / any other frontend also routes `task.created` through
  `endless-go event emit`. If so they inherit the rule automatically; the
  session-attribution condition leaves non-session creators unaffected.

## Out of scope — linked follow-ups (to file)
- Stop-hook sweep tripwire (defensive backstop): at session Stop, detect any
  session-created empty-description task and block/flag. Guards against this gate
  being bypassed or buggy; it is a tripwire on the invariant, not a second
  enforcement of it. Link `relates_to`.
- Background augmentation: a background process that detects human-created
  description-less tasks and has the AI write the description. Separate mechanism
  (worker/cron + AI call). Link `relates_to`.
- Description *quality* / placeholder linting — explicitly deferred.

## Dropped
- Python-CLI-layer pre-check ("approach A"): redundant with the Go choke point —
  same rule, same before-append timing, one layer up. Two copies would drift. Not
  implemented.

payload.title: Make worktrees disposable without risking in-flight work
payload.description: Worktree lifecycle leaks on three axes: 113 worktrees holding 180k files (47% derived), 184 orphaned sandboxes, and all of it backed up by Time Machine and Spotlight-indexed — driving fseventsd to ~20% of a core continuously. Blocker to reaping/excluding is that a worktree dir is the only home for uncommitted and untracked work. Verified fix: snapshot WIP into the main checkout's shared object store under refs/wip/*, which survives worktree removal and aggressive GC. Once WIP is durable, worktree dirs become genuinely disposable.
payload.analysis:
# Findings — dev-machine resource investigation, 2026-08-06

Triggered by `kernel_task` at 156% and `fseventsd` saturating CPU on the M4 mini
(24 GB RAM, 10 cores, 99-day uptime).

## Measured state

| Metric | Value |
|---|---|
| Swap | **49.2 GB used of 50.2 GB (98%)** |
| Free pages | 3,412 x 16 KB = 55 MB |
| CPU split | 65% sys / 20% user / 15% idle |
| Load average | 44-57 on 10 cores |
| Processes | 841, of which 43 are `claude` |
| tmux panes | 408 across 6 sessions |
| fseventsd CPU | 29,098 min in 100 days (~20% of a core, continuously) |

`pmset -g therm` recorded no thermal warnings, so `kernel_task` is the VM
compressor thrashing, not throttling.

## Worktree / sandbox footprint

- 113 worktrees, 180,117 files, 5.4 GB under `.endless/worktrees`
- **84,303 files (47%) are pure derived output:**
  `.venv` 67,289 - `__pycache__` 15,596 - `bin/` 1,159 - caches 259
- By bytes `bin/` dominates: 70 MB of a 76 MB worktree
- 267 sandboxes, of which **184 are orphaned** (no matching worktree), 228 MB,
  oldest dating to 2026-06-17
- Time Machine backs up all of it (`tmutil isexcluded` reports `[Included]` for
  `~/Projects`, `.endless/worktrees`, `~/.cache`) to a **network SMB share**
  (Synology, 708 GB / 3,846,305 files). Spotlight indexes the same churn
  (`spotlightknowledged.updater` 11.8%, `mds` 5.5%).

## Why we cannot just exclude and reap

A worktree dir is the only home for uncommitted + untracked work. That is
precisely what must survive removal.

## Verified mechanism for making WIP durable

A worktree's `.git` is an 84-byte pointer file; its object database is the
**main checkout's** `.git/objects`. Snapshot without mutating the working tree:

```sh
export GIT_INDEX_FILE=$(mktemp -u)
git add -A                      # honors .gitignore -> skips bin/, .venv/, __pycache__
TREE=$(git write-tree)
COMMIT=$(git commit-tree "$TREE" -p HEAD -m "wip: <name>")
unset GIT_INDEX_FILE
git update-ref refs/wip/<name> "$COMMIT"
```

Three properties, all verified end-to-end in a scratch repo:

1. Objects land in the main checkout's shared store, not the worktree.
2. `refs/wip/*` is outside git's per-worktree ref namespace (only `HEAD`,
   `refs/bisect/*`, `refs/worktree/*` are per-worktree), so the ref is written
   to `<main>/.git/refs/wip/` and survives worktree removal.
3. A ref pins its objects against GC.

Destructive test — after `git worktree remove --force`, `git branch -D`,
`git reflog expire --expire=now --all`, `git gc --prune=now --aggressive`:

```
$ git show refs/wip/e-999:scratch-notes.md
PRECIOUS untracked
```

Both the modified tracked file and the untracked file were recovered.
`git add -A` honoring `.gitignore` was confirmed against this repo's
`.gitignore` (`/bin/` :13, `.venv/` :10, `__pycache__/` :8), so snapshots
capture only the precious source and are kilobytes.

## Time Machine exclusion mechanics (verified)

Two mechanisms with opposite lifetimes:

| Form | Storage | Survives dir deletion | Root |
|---|---|---|---|
| `tmutil addexclusion <path>` | xattr `com.apple.metadata:com_apple_backup_excludeItem` on the dir | **No — dies with the inode** | no |
| `tmutil addexclusion -p <path>` | `SkipPaths` in `com.apple.TimeMachine.plist` | **Yes — accumulates forever** | yes |

Confirmed the sticky (non-`-p`) form leaves `SkipPaths` nonexistent before and
after. `-p` requires root, so it cannot be triggered accidentally. `tmutil` has
**no glob/pattern support**; the only pattern list is `StdExclusions.plist`
inside the SIP-protected `backupd.bundle`. The per-worktree creation hook is
therefore the correct place to apply exclusions.

## Sandbox leak — two independent defects

1. `internal/monitor/reap_worktrees.go` contains **zero** occurrences of
   "sandbox". `Sandbox.Destroy()` is called only from `sandboxcmd/run.go:50`
   (ephemeral teardown) and the manual `endless-sandbox destroy` CLI.
2. `internal/sandboxcmd/list.go:83` `classify()` returns `stateInUse` for any
   sandbox whose mode is `keep` or `persistent` — **unconditionally**, with no
   worktree-existence or PID check. All 267 sandboxes report `persistent` /
   `in-use`, and `prune` only removes `stateOrphaned`, so `sandbox prune` is
   structurally incapable of reclaiming any worktree sandbox. Its own message
   ("no orphaned ephemeral sandboxes") shows it was only ever built for
   ephemeral ones.

## Platform scope

The repo currently has **no** `runtime.GOOS` usage and no `_darwin.go` files —
no precedent for platform-conditional behavior. Anything built on `tmutil` or
`.metadata_never_index` would be the first, and needs an explicit no-op path on
other platforms rather than an assumed-macOS shell-out.

# Worktree teardown leaves three kinds of dependent behind

Found 2026-08-06 while investigating fseventsd/kernel_task saturation.
Measured: 267 sandboxes against 113 worktrees — **184 orphaned**, 228 MB,
oldest dating to 2026-06-17.

## Defect 1 — `classify()` can never report a worktree sandbox as orphaned

`internal/sandboxcmd/list.go:83`:

```go
func classify(meta SandboxMeta) sandboxState {
    if meta.Mode == modeKeep || meta.Mode == modePersistent {
        return stateInUse    // unconditional: no worktree check, no PID check
    }
    if isAlive(meta.CreatorPID) {
        return stateLive
    }
    return stateOrphaned
}
```

Every worktree sandbox is `persistent`, so all 268 classified `in-use`.
`prune.go:33` only removes `stateOrphaned`. **`endless-sandbox prune` was
structurally incapable of reclaiming a single worktree sandbox** — its own
message ("no orphaned *ephemeral* sandboxes") shows it was built only for
ephemeral ones. A persistent sandbox whose worktree no longer exists should
classify as orphaned.

## Defect 2 — the reaper never destroys the sandbox

`internal/monitor/reap_worktrees.go` contains **zero** occurrences of
"sandbox". `Sandbox.Destroy()` is reachable only from
`internal/sandboxcmd/run.go:50` (ephemeral teardown) and the manual
`endless-sandbox destroy` CLI. Nothing in the drop/land/reap path calls it.
`CLAUDE.md` documents the gap ("Sandbox cleanup on worktree drop/land is not
yet automatic") but the reaper shipped without closing it.

## Defect 3 — `endless-go channel` processes outlive their worktree

Four processes aged **18–24 days** still hold open the sandbox DBs of
worktrees that are gone:

| PID | age | sandbox | worktree dir |
|---|---|---|---|
| 73345 | 18d18h | e-1533 | GONE |
| 93453 | 23d21h | e-1603 | GONE |
| 1973  | 23d21h | e-1774 | GONE |
| 79957 | 18d21h | e-1789 | GONE |

They were the only 4 of 183 orphans that `sandbox destroy` refused (correctly,
without `--force`) during the 2026-08-06 manual cleanup that removed the other
179. Each is a live process plus a pinned SQLite handle on a directory nobody
will read again. Teardown should terminate the channel process, or the channel
process should exit when its worktree disappears.

## Manual cleanup already performed

179 of 183 orphans destroyed by hand (288 MB → 68 MB, 268 → 89 sandboxes).
Backup at `orphaned-sandboxes-backup.tgz` in the session scratchpad. This task
is about making that automatic, not about re-doing it.
