# Reap safety predicate (learned the hard way, 2026-08-06)

The manual cleanup used "worktree dir exists OR git tracks a worktree of that
name" as its protection rule. **That rule is insufficient.** It destroyed 10
sandboxes it should not have; all were restored from the pre-delete backup.

A sandbox may be reaped ONLY when every one of these is false:

| # | Condition | How to check | Missed by the manual run? |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | Worktree dir exists | `[ -d .endless/worktrees/<n> ]` | no |
| 2 | Git still tracks a worktree of that name | `git worktree list --porcelain` | no |
| 3 | **A live tmux window references the task ID** | window names carry `[E-NNNN]` | **YES — 8 destroyed** |
| 4 | **The task branch is unmerged to main** | `git branch --no-merged main` | **YES — 2 destroyed** |
| 5 | Worktree is unsettled (dirty working tree) | existing `worktree_unsettled.go` | n/a — implies (1) |
| 6 | A live process holds files in the sandbox | already enforced by `destroy` | no — correctly refused 4 |

## Why (3) matters

A tmux window is the user's own record that a task is still in play, and it
outlives the worktree. Of 57 task IDs with a live window in the `active`
session, 12 had no worktree directory at all — the window is the only surviving
handle on that work. Destroyed in error: `e-1202 e-1368 e-1552 e-1621 e-1664
e-1687 e-1702 e-1714` (the other 4 — `e-1533 e-1603 e-1774 e-1789` — survived
only because condition 6 blocked them).

Window names follow `endless_<slug>[E-NNNN]`; parse the bracketed ID. Note the
`active` session is grouped with `active-6`, so enumerate windows rather than
panes to avoid double-counting.

## Why (4) matters

A removed worktree whose branch never merged still holds the only copy of that
work. `git branch --no-merged main` currently lists **64** task branches.
Destroyed in error: `e-1036 e-1669`.

Condition (5) is subsumed by (1) for live worktrees, but must be checked
explicitly if reaping is ever extended to prune worktree dirs themselves.

## Implementation note

Conditions 3 and 4 are the two that survive worktree deletion, which is exactly
why a dir-existence check cannot stand alone. Both belong in the same predicate
the reaper consults, not as ad-hoc guards at the call site.

fields.text:
# E-1898 — the reaper must observe, never infer

## What this task is

`monitor.ReapDeadTmuxPanes` closes session rows whose tmux pane it believes is
gone. It decides that from `tmux list-panes -a` against an ambient `$TMUX` it
never validates, so a caller attached to a different tmux server concludes every
real pane is dead and NULLs `process` for the whole project. Rows then read
alive with no pane, permanently, and every tmux status line goes blank.

Observed 2026-08-05: 27 orphaned panes, 59 of 61 windows blank, unresolvable for
hours because the status line renders every failure as the same dim dot.

## Terminology (fix this first — it caused real confusion)

"Reaping" here is a **database write only**. The reaper's entire effect is:

    UPDATE sessions SET state='ended', process=NULL, last_activity=? WHERE ...

It never kills a pane, never touches tmux state. `ReapDeadTmuxPanes` reads as
"kill dead tmux panes"; it means "close rows whose pane is gone." **Rename it**
— proposed `CloseSessionsForDeadPanes` — and fix the doc comment to lead with
"writes only to `sessions`; never mutates tmux."

## Root cause, singular

The reaper destroys the value that `TouchSession`'s COALESCE exists to protect.

`process = COALESCE(NULLIF(excluded.process,''), sessions.process)` is correct
and stays: it means "use the pane I was handed, else keep the one on the row."
It was added by E-1426 specifically to fix E-1408 and it still does that job.
But once the reaper has NULLed `process`, there is no known-good value left to
protect, and a later hook with an empty `TMUX_PANE` revives `state` to
`needs_input` while `process` stays NULL. That row — not ended, no pane — is
incoherent, reads as alive, and resolves to nothing forever.

**No change to TouchSession's COALESCE.** Fix the reaper and the trap closes.

## Locked decisions

### D1 — `@server_uuid` is a GATE, not a stored column

No schema change. The reaper reads `@server_uuid` from the server `$TMUX` points
at. Empty means this server was never initialized by Endless — a private
`tmux -L` server, or a fresh one mid-init — so **refuse and record a fault**.

Rejected: adding `sessions.server_uuid`. It would couple the sessions table more
tightly to tmux and store a value identical across every live row.

Rejected: encoding `<server_uuid>:<pane>` into `process`. Twelve-plus call sites
compare `process` to a raw pane id (`tmux_lookup.go` x3, `session.go` collision
invalidation, `session_nav.go`, `events/session_status.go`, both reapers' GLOB),
the `channels` table keys on the same string, and `process` already holds
non-tmux values like `pid:1234`. Every missed site would fail **silently** by
simply not matching — the exact failure class this task exists to remove.

### D2 — guards run cheapest-first, expensive only when damage is imminent

    1. cheap   own server has @server_uuid?            no  -> refuse + fault
    2. cheap   any rows actually about to be closed?   none -> done
    3. costly  enumerate peer servers; another live one has a uuid?
                                                       yes -> refuse + fault

Step 3 costs nothing in the common case (nothing to close) and is bounded when
it matters. Enumeration is proven reliable: list sockets in
`dirname $(tmux display-message -p '#{socket_path}')`, query each for
`@server_uuid`, skip your own. Live-and-initialized returns the uuid with rc=0;
live-but-uninitialized and stale sockets both return empty with rc=1, cleanly
distinguishable.

Accepted limitation, documented in the code: servers started with `tmux -S
<path>` outside that directory, or under a relocated `TMUX_TMPDIR`, are not
enumerable. Neither is common; the failure mode is the status quo, not worse.

Two coexisting initialized servers are **guarded, not forbidden** — the reaper
declines while the ambiguity exists rather than `tmux apply` refusing to run.
Self-correcting: kill the second server and reaping resumes.

### D3 — the death test becomes an observation, not an inference

Today: "pane absent from `list-panes`". That is sufficient for death but not
necessary — a Claude session whose harness was killed leaves its pane alive
running a shell, and the reaper never notices.

New test: **pane absent OR the pane is running a known shell**
(`zsh`/`bash`/`sh`/`fish`).

This requires fixing a live bug next door. `monitor.paneIsRunningClaude` matches
`cmd == "claude" || cmd == "claude-code"`, but Claude Code sets its process title
to its version — every real Claude pane reports `pane_current_command` =
`2.1.212`. The helper therefore returns false for every live Claude pane, so
`GetPaneStatus`'s `PaneStatusClaudeNoSession` branch never fires correctly.

Fix by **inverting the test**: detect the shell, not the Claude. Shell names are
stable; a version string changes every release. Add a positively-named helper
`paneIsRunningShell`.

#### D3a — the reaper consumes the new helper; the STATUS LINE does not

`paneIsRunningShell` is introduced for the death test only. `GetPaneStatus`
(internal/monitor/tmux_lookup.go:218) keeps calling `paneIsRunningClaude`
unchanged.

Repointing it would silently change what the bar renders. The
`PaneStatusClaudeNoSession` branch would then fire for ANY pane not running a
known shell, so a pane running vim, less, git or a long `go test` in a window
with no Endless session would stop showing the dim placeholder and start
showing `no Endless session ▸ endless setup claude-hook`. On a machine with 60+
windows, most of them not Endless windows, that is a lot of surface telling the
user to install a hook they already have.

That is not a change to make as a side effect of a reaper fix. Deciding it
properly means deciding what the branch MEANS once "is Claude running here" is
not answerable — a hint-semantics question, and E-1698 requires the bar and
`session status` to agree on it. Out of scope here.

Recorded so it is not lost: `paneIsRunningClaude` is broken today and this task
does not fix it. It matches `cmd == "claude" || cmd == "claude-code"` while real
Claude panes report their version (`2.1.212`), so `PaneStatusClaudeNoSession`
effectively never fires. Pre-existing, orthogonal to the data loss, and left
exactly as found.

### D4 — idle-timeout is NOT in scope; E-1642 stays obsolete

D3 replaces it. Positive detection covers "Claude died, pane lives" without
inferring death from silence, and therefore cannot close a session that is
merely idle — the failure mode E-1642's plan had to add a longer `needs_input`
window to mitigate. No config knob, no land-path sweep, no new CLI verb.

Consequently the earlier decision to trigger a sweep on `worktree land` is moot:
there is no sweep.

### D5 — a `process`-less FOREGROUND row raises one fault; never auto-corrected

My original predicate — "not `ended` and no `process`" — was wrong. Two normal,
intended row shapes match it:

- **Background agents.** `RecordBgAgentSession` inserts `state='working'`,
  `process` NULL, `kind_id = background` by design ("bg agents have no tmux
  pane", session.go:442), and session.go:66-77 already carves that class out of
  the E-1640 dedup for the same reason. The literal predicate would raise a
  fault for every live background agent and light the errors badge permanently
  during normal operation — destroying the loudness D5 exists to create.
- **Claude started outside tmux.** `TouchSession` writes
  `process = NULLIF(os.Getenv("TMUX_PANE"), '')`, so a foreground session with
  no `$TMUX_PANE` legitimately lands `needs_input` with `process` NULL.

**Locked predicate:** `state != 'ended' AND process IS NULL AND kind_id = tmux`.

Background rows are EXCLUDED — they are a different lifecycle with its own
carve-out already in the code.

The non-tmux foreground case is **accepted noise**, and deliberately so: it is
indistinguishable on the row from reaper damage, and no condition available on
the row separates them (schema per
internal/schema/changes/e-1568-sessions-short-id-and-nullable-session-id.go:55).
It should be near-zero in this project's workflow, where sessions are spawned
into tmux windows. If it proves noisy in practice the answer is to narrow
further — a `platform`/kind refinement — never to widen the predicate back.

**Fingerprinting: ONE incident, not one per row.** Faults dedupe by fingerprint,
so putting row ids in the Summary would split the incident N ways and bury it.
Use a FIXED fingerprint (`sessions-live-without-pane`); carry the offending row
ids in Detail/Fields. One incident that grows a longer id list is the signal;
forty incidents is noise.

The rows themselves are never modified. Sweeping them would have destroyed the
evidence that diagnosed this incident.

### D6 — `endless tmux reset --force` bypasses the guards

The explicit operator verb keeps an escape hatch. Without `--force` it obeys D2
identically to the hook path. `--force` must print what it is overriding.

### D7 — `runInit` no longer calls `runReset(nil)`

Under D1 that call can never do anything: `runInit` stamps `@server_uuid` LAST
(deliberately, so a crash mid-init leaves the gate open for retry), so at reset
time the gate always refuses. Remove the call rather than leave a
destructive-looking no-op for someone to later "fix" by removing the gate.

This is also the trigger for the 37-row batch in the ledger: a fresh tmux server
firing `session-created -> endless tmux init` reaped the whole project against a
one-pane view. After a genuine restart, the next SessionStart still closes the
old rows correctly, once the uuid is stamped.

### D8 — the status line records a fault instead of swallowing (absorbed E-1895)

`runStatusLine` maps every `GetPaneStatus` error to `placeholder()` and stays
silent. `monitor.DB()` alone has ~7 fail-closed exits behind that one `err`.

Keep the bar output unchanged and keep stderr silent — the bar re-execs once per
pane every 2s, so logging would be a firehose over a live TUI. Use
`faults.Record`, which dedupes an open incident in place, so a bar blanking
across every pane raises ONE incident. `main.go` already calls `faults.Bind` for
every subcommand.

**Coverage is partial, and the plan should not imply otherwise.** `faults.Bind`
is wired as `faults.Bind(monitor.DB, ...)` (cmd/endless-go/main.go:144), so the
recorder's own DB accessor IS the thing that failed when `monitor.DB()` is the
cause — and `faults.Record` swallows its own DB failure by contract. D8
therefore covers the fail-closed exits that are NOT `monitor.DB()` itself. A DB
that cannot be opened at all still renders a silent placeholder. Recording that
case needs a sink that does not depend on the DB, which is out of scope here.

### D9 — collision invalidation gates on RECENCY + STATE, not on D3's test

`TouchSession`'s collision path (session.go:385-397) ends every other row sharing
the incoming pane string with no liveness check. It is the second write path that
destroys a binding on an unproven assumption.

**D3's observation cannot be reused here.** The collision path fires *because* a
hook just arrived carrying `process = <pane>`. The pane is therefore provably
present, and it is running the incoming Claude session, so it is not a shell.
D3's test would return "alive" 100% of the time, collision invalidation would
become a permanent no-op, and E-1530's pane-reuse ghosts would come straight
back: after a server restart, pane `%203` is reissued, the old row still claims
it, and nothing ever clears it.

**`server_uuid` does not settle it either**, which also resolves the tension with
D1. A stored uuid separates "row from a previous server lifetime" from "row on
this server" — but E-1468's actual case is two identities in ONE pane on the SAME
live server seconds apart (a land run from main, where a nested `claude -p`
inherits `$TMUX_PANE` from its parent and registers its own row). Same server,
same uuid, so the uuid cannot discriminate the case D9 exists for. D1's rejection
stands unmodified.

**Locked discriminator — invalidate only when BOTH hold:**

    prior.state != 'working'                    AND
    prior.last_activity older than 5 minutes

`state='working'` means mid-tool-call and is never invalidated at any age. This
is the load-bearing half: a long-running tool call (a 10-minute `go test`) fires
PreToolUse at the start and PostToolUse at the end, so a genuinely working
session can carry a `last_activity` ten minutes stale. Recency alone would kill
it — which is exactly E-1468's bug in a new costume.

**Why 5 minutes, and why the asymmetry is safe.** A parent session that spawns a
nested hook-firing subprocess wrote `last_activity` seconds earlier, so 5 minutes
is two orders of magnitude of headroom against E-1468's case. The cost at the
other end is unusually cheap: `queryActiveTaskForPanes` resolves with
`ORDER BY s.last_activity DESC LIMIT 1` (tmux_lookup.go:106), so a ghost that
lingers never wins pane resolution — the newer row always does. A too-large N
therefore costs a stale row visible in `session list`, not a wrong status line;
a too-small N costs a falsely-ended live session. The error budget is
overwhelmingly on the conservative side, so bias N large.

A named constant, not config — consistent with D4's no-knobs stance.

**Accepted residue:** a session that crashed while `state='working'` is never
invalidated by this path. If its pane died, D3's death test closes it. If its
pane was reused by a new Claude, the row lingers as a duplicate — cosmetic, since
resolution prefers the newer row. Fixing that needs process liveness, which is
not available on the row.

## Implementation order

1. Rename + doc comment (D-terminology). Mechanical, lands alone.
2. D1 + D2 guards, D5 fault, D7 removal — the urgent data-loss fix.
3. D3 death test + `paneIsRunningShell`, and repoint the status-line consumer.
4. D8 status-line fault.
5. D9 collision staleness.
6. D6 `--force`.

Steps 1-2 are independently landable and are the part that stops the bleeding.

Mechanical notes (verified during review, no design consequence):

- The reaper has **three** call sites, not two: `internal/hookcmd/claude.go:185`,
  `internal/sessionquerycmd/session_query.go:532`, `internal/tmuxcmd/reset.go:49`.
  The D1/D2 guards live inside the shared function, so all three inherit them.
- `monitor` cannot import `tmuxcmd` (`tmuxcmd` imports `monitor`), so
  `tmuxcmd/init.go`'s `readServerOption` moves into `monitor` for D1.
- D3 adds no per-pane subprocess cost: one
  `tmux list-panes -a -F '#{pane_id} #{pane_current_command}'` yields both fields
  for every pane, so D2's cost guarantee is unaffected.
- Every new fault code needs a matching `docs/errors.md` section;
  `faults_test.go:414 TestCatalog_EveryCodeIsDocumented` enforces the sync in
  both directions.

## Tests — `tests/tasks/e-1898-verify.sh`

Task checks fail-fast first, then project-wide regression. The suite must itself
obey the isolation rule (private `tmux -L` servers started with `-f /dev/null`
under a throwaway `XDG_CONFIG_HOME`, sockets removed in the trap) — see
`tests/tasks/e-1851-verify.sh` for the reference implementation.

**Layer A — unit, FAIL-FAST**
- Gate: with `@server_uuid` absent, the reaper closes nothing and records a
  fault. With it present, it proceeds.
- Peer check: with a second live initialized server present, the reaper closes
  nothing and records a fault; with only stale sockets around, it proceeds.
- Ordering: with nothing to close, no peer enumeration happens at all (assert
  via a seam counter — this is the cost guarantee).
- Death test: a row whose pane is absent closes; a row whose pane runs a shell
  closes; a row whose pane runs Claude does NOT.
- `paneIsRunningShell` returns true for zsh/bash/sh/fish and false for a
  version-string command such as `2.1.212` — the exact value the old helper got
  wrong.
- D5: a not-ended `kind_id = tmux` row with NULL `process` is never modified and
  raises a fault; a BACKGROUND row with NULL `process` raises none. Two damaged
  rows produce ONE incident carrying both ids, not two incidents.
- D3a: `GetPaneStatus` classification is UNCHANGED — a pane running a non-shell,
  non-Claude command (e.g. `vim`) in a window with no session still resolves to
  `PaneStatusNone`, not `PaneStatusClaudeNoSession`. This pins that the status
  line was not repointed.
- D9 recency gate: a prior occupant with `state='working'` and `last_activity`
  one hour old is NOT invalidated (the long-tool-call case). A prior occupant
  with `state='idle'` and `last_activity` ten seconds old is NOT invalidated
  (inside N). A prior occupant with `state='idle'` and `last_activity` one hour
  old IS invalidated (the pane-reuse ghost).
- D9 residue is harmless: with two non-ended rows claiming one pane, pane
  resolution returns the one with the newer `last_activity`.

**Layer B — E2E against a private tmux server**
1. Seed a throwaway DB with sessions bound to panes on a private server.
2. Confirm the reaper closes rows for panes killed on that server.
3. Point it at a SECOND private server and confirm it closes NOTHING and
   records a fault — the regression test for this incident.
4. Confirm `endless tmux reset` refuses there, and `--force` proceeds and says
   what it overrode.

**Layer C — project-wide regression**: `go test ./...` and `just test`.

**Ledger-safety assertion (mandatory).** Count non-ended sessions holding a
`process` in the REAL database before and after the whole suite; they must be
equal. This suite exercises a destructive code path, and that count is the
thing this task exists to protect.

## Out of scope

- Idle-timeout / session-duration truthfulness (D4).
- Non-tmux session lifecycle (`pid:1234` rows) — needs its own mechanism.
- E-1884's 42 `log.Printf` conversions. D8 is the inverse defect (a site that
  writes nothing when it should) and does not pull that sweep in.
- Repairing rows already damaged. A one-off reconstruction was applied by hand on
  2026-08-05 (window name -> task id -> most recent session row for that task).
  If a supported repair verb is wanted later, file it then.

Mechanism (three parts):

1. Invert the default. The task report output IS the sanctioned user-facing message (already shown to the user as tool output). Move the two legitimate exceptions INTO the report so no prose outside it is ever justified:
   - the task's single verify command becomes a report field;
   - genuine open decisions/blockers go through the report's --json notes/questions channel (already E-1803's model).

2. Record the checkpoint. The report command marks the session turn as a verbatim-relay checkpoint and stores the exact sanctioned text.

3. Gate at Stop. A Stop hook compares the agent's actual final message to the sanctioned text; anything beyond it returns decision:block with a reason the user also sees ("appended N lines beyond the report; resend verbatim"). Compliant = empty or exactly-sanctioned; prose becomes the caught exception, not a discretionary default.

Keystone: routing the verify command and open decisions through the report as FIELDS is what collapses the Stop-hook check from an intractable 'is this prose a legitimate question or a banned recap' judgment into a hard equality check. Without it the gate has false positives; with it, prose-outside-the-report is always a violation.


---

## Integration with E-1803

E-1803 ships the compose-time half of this feature (a relay nudge + the
coverage rule) and is landing now; once it lands you rebase onto it. Reuse what
it built rather than reinventing or colliding with it:

- **Detection already exists.** `internal/hookcmd/claude.go` has `taskReportRe`
  — it matches a Bash command that actually RUNS `endless task report`, anchored
  to a command position so the phrase appearing as an argument (a commit
  message, `echo`, `grep`) does not misfire. It drives a `PostToolUse` branch
  that emits the relay-verbatim nudge. Reuse `taskReportRe` for step 2's "record
  the checkpoint"; do NOT add a second, drifting matcher. (You will also edit
  `claude.go`, so you rebase onto these additions.)
- **The Stop gate layers on the nudge, it does not replace it.** Arm 1's
  `PostToolUse` additionalContext ("relay verbatim, add nothing") stays as the
  compose-time reminder that helps the agent comply on the first try and avoid
  the bounce; this task's Stop-hook block is the enforcement layer at turn end.
- **Sanctioned text = the fact block, not the steer prompt.** `task report`
  prints a *steering prompt* ("Report the following… add nothing") that the
  agent must NOT relay. Step 2 must store the facts-to-relay, separate from that
  wrapper — otherwise the Stop equality check compares against the wrong string.
- **The empty-report case is now the common one (E-1880).** Post-E-1880 a clean
  session's report fact block is empty and steers the agent to say nothing. Your
  equality gate needs a defined sanctioned message for that case (e.g. the
  deliverable one-liner + the verify command) or it has nothing to match. This
  is the sharpest open design point for the keystone.

# Plan — E-1822: deliver the type-handoff on claim-into-a-live-session

Design captured in the analysis; this is the implementation. Two axes, both now
unblocked (E-1803 landed — its `PostToolUse` `additionalContext` mechanism is the
delivery lever, and it is proven reliable for context *delivery*, which is all
this task needs; the "strong nudge, not a hard gate" caveat was about enforcing
behavior, not delivering context).

## Axis 1 — Content: a shared type-mechanics partial + a claim wrapper

The claim wrapper is the *second* consumer of each type's handoff mechanics
(spawn is the first). Per the analysis's discipline, this second consumer is what
justifies extracting the seam — extract ONLY the lines whose drift between the
spawn and claim renderings would be a bug; do not pre-factor the rest.

1. New shared partial `internal/templatecmd/templates/handoff/_mechanics.tmpl`,
   parsed into every handoff set exactly as `_close` is:
   - In `template.go`, mirror `closePartialName`/`mechanicsPartialName` and the
     `strings.HasPrefix(name, "handoff/")` block that parses the partial so
     `{{template "handoff_mechanics" .}}` resolves.
   - Content = only the genuinely invariant, drift-sensitive mechanics: worktree-
     bound; `--db main` routing inside the worktree; one-session-one-task; and the
     per-type terminal-status/artifact rule. Where a type differs (e.g. research/
     brainstorm end `completed` with a landable ledger artifact; todo/bugfix end
     `unverified`), branch on `.task_type` inside the partial rather than forking
     into five near-identical partials.
2. Wire the existing per-type spawn templates
   (`handoff/{todo,bugfix,epic,research,brainstorm}.md.tmpl`) to include
   `{{template "handoff_mechanics" .}}` in place of the mechanics lines they carry
   inline today. Spawn output must not change in meaning — only its source of the
   invariant lines moves, so spawn and claim can no longer drift on them.
3. New claim wrapper `internal/templatecmd/templates/handoff/claim.md.tmpl` — the
   claim-only arrival framing, then the mechanics partial, then the `_close` tail.
   Arrival block (from the analysis — focused, not thin):
   - you are NOT freshly spawned — you have been running and just claimed this; no
     blank-slate assumption;
   - relocate: `/cd` your working directory into the task's worktree (a spawned
     session is born there; a claimed-in one is not) — backstopped by the existing
     cwd gate that already refuses tools when cwd drifts outside the claimed
     worktree (E-1586);
   - routing: the worktree routes DB access to the sandbox, so real-ledger updates
     need `--db main`;
   - fold the planning you already did into the task's `text` field, not chat.

## Axis 2 — Delivery: `PostToolUse` additionalContext on the live-session claim

4. In `internal/hookcmd/claude.go`, the claim action is already detected in
   `handlePostToolUseSession` (`actionStart`/`scopeTask` → `StartWorkSession`).
   Extend that branch: after `StartWorkSession` succeeds, render the claim handoff
   and return it as `additionalContext` via the `postToolUseResponse` struct
   E-1803 added.
   - Retrofit vs spawn needs no flag: `endless task spawn` pre-claims the task
     BEFORE the target session starts, so its claim never runs as a `PostToolUse`
     inside that session; a `PostToolUse` `endless task claim` is definitionally
     the live-session retrofit. Confirm against `trySpawnBind` (spawn sets
     `@endless_spawned_by` + pre-flips status) that spawn cannot also emit this
     event in the spawned session — guard on the spawn marker if it can.
   - Render in-process: the hook IS the `endless-go` binary, so call the
     `templatecmd` render path (or a thin `monitor` helper) directly rather than
     shelling. Build the same vars the spawn path assembles in
     `render_handoff` (id, title, `task_type`, `worktree_path`, `branch`,
     `children_state`) with `template_name = handoff/claim`.
   - Reuse E-1803's response shape:
     `postToolUseResponse{HookSpecificOutput:{HookEventName:"PostToolUse",
     AdditionalContext: <rendered claim handoff>}}`.

## Verification — tests/tasks/e-1822-verify.sh (fully scripted)

- Go template: `template render handoff/claim` yields the arrival block +
  mechanics + close; `handoff_mechanics` resolves in BOTH a spawn per-type render
  and the claim render (the anti-drift guarantee).
- Go hook unit: a `PostToolUse` payload for `endless task claim <id>` returns
  `additionalContext` carrying the claim handoff; a spawn-marked session does not
  double-deliver.
- Script: build + the two Go suites (fail-fast) + a claim-into-a-live-session
  e2e against the sandbox asserting the handoff text is emitted, plus a guard that
  spawn output is unchanged in meaning.

## Boundary

- Content: extract ONLY drift-sensitive invariants into `_mechanics`; not a
  wholesale template rewrite.
- Delivery does not alter spawn (spawn still renders per-type templates; they now
  include the shared partial).
- Enforcing that the agent actually relocates/uses `--db main` is not this task's
  job — the cwd gate (E-1586) already backstops relocation; this task delivers the
  context so the agent knows to.

payload.title: Remove vestigial transcript_path column and session reimport

fields.description: Remove two vestigial pieces of session transcript tracking. The transcript_path column is recorded once at SessionStart from Claude's payload, goes stale when a session changes cwd (the file moves, the column does not), and has no live consumer — the session monitor's session_messages is kept current by the live Go parser using the payload path, not this column. session reimport is a manual-only CLI escape hatch with a duplicate Python parser that nothing automatic needs. Remove both (option A: delete reimport, do not keep a discovery-based form); keep transcript_offset (the live parser's resume cursor).
fields.text:
# Plan — E-1905: remove vestigial `transcript_path` + `session reimport`

Both are vestigial. `session_messages` is kept current by the LIVE Go parser
(`ParseTranscript`, `transcript.go:304`) on every event using Claude's payload
path; the stored `transcript_path` column feeds essentially nothing and goes
stale when a session changes cwd after start (recorded once at SessionStart,
never re-recorded). `session reimport` is a manual-only CLI escape hatch with a
duplicate Python parser; nothing automatic needs it. Decision (this session):
remove `session reimport` as well (option A), not keep a discovery-based form.

KEEP `transcript_offset` — it is the live parser's resume cursor
(`transcript.go:241/252`), unrelated to `transcript_path`.

## 1. Remove `session reimport` (command + Python parser)

- `src/endless/cli.py:1060-1065` — delete the `reimport` command + wiring.
- `src/endless/session_cmd.py` — delete `reimport_sessions` (~849), the duplicate
  `_parse_transcript_py` (~1202) and its helpers, and `_find_jsonl` (~857 — used
  ONLY by reimport). Remove any now-dead imports.
- Drop reimport-specific tests.

## 2. Drop the `transcript_path` column

- Schema: remove `transcript_path TEXT` from `internal/schema/schema.sql:137` and
  the mirrored DDL/backfill in `src/endless/db.py` (~361).
- Add a schema change under `internal/schema/changes/` that drops the column,
  following the `e-1568` sessions-rebuild pattern (SQLite `ALTER TABLE ... DROP
  COLUMN`, or table rebuild if the version in use needs it). The `sessions` table
  is machine-local (not journaled to the shared ledger), so this is a local
  schema change — no ledger upcast needed.

## 3. Remove writers/readers of the column

- `internal/hookcmd/claude.go:194-197` — delete the SessionStart
  `SetTranscriptPath(payload.SessionID, payload.TranscriptPath)` block (and the
  "Store transcript path for reimport" comment). `payload.TranscriptPath` is still
  used live by the `ParseTranscript` calls (232/252/262/265) — leave those.
- `internal/monitor/transcript.go` — delete `SetTranscriptPath` (~319) and
  `GetTranscriptPath` (~331, already caller-free) plus their round-trip tests
  (`transcript_test.go:397-419`).
- `internal/events/reopen_context.go` — in `inheritedSessionID`'s ORDER BY, drop
  the `OR transcript_path IS NOT NULL` evidence clause (leave `process IS NOT NULL`
  and the `>= 10`s span). Update the doc comment (~41) that names transcript_path
  as an evidence signal. Minor, intended behavior change: transcript_path is no
  longer a tiebreak signal.
- `src/endless/session_cmd.py:69/81/91` — remove `transcript_path` from the SELECT
  column lists; drop the `:854` read (goes with reimport).

## Verification — tests/tasks/e-1905-verify.sh (fully scripted)

- Build + `go test ./...` + `just test` green.
- `endless session reimport` is gone (command not found / not registered).
- `session list`, `session search`, and recaps still work — `session_messages` is
  unaffected (still populated by the live Go parser); assert a live-parsed session
  still yields messages/search hits against the sandbox.
- No remaining references to `transcript_path` in `internal/` or `src/` (grep guard).

## Boundary

- Does NOT touch `transcript_offset` or the live `ParseTranscript` path.
- Not a plan-file/plan-reimport change — that is a separate, already-abandoned
  concept; this is only session transcript tracking.

# Plan — E-1901: enforce verbatim report relay with a Stop-hook gate

Rebased onto main (E-1803 landed as `5dcdc2bf`), so `taskReportRe`, the
PostToolUse relay nudge, and `reportChannelRule` are all present and are reused,
not reinvented.

## Decisions taken (were open in the plan)

1. **Verify command enters via the `--json` payload** as a `verify` key —
   symmetric with `notes`/`questions`, no schema change on `tasks`, agent-supplied
   at report time. NOT Haiku-gated: a command is a command, not prose.
2. **Empty report renders a fixed sanctioned line, `Nothing to report.`** — not
   silence. Silence is indistinguishable from a stalled agent; one fixed line
   proves the turn ended deliberately and states the null result. Checkpoint-
   neutral (reads correctly mid-session and at session end).
3. **The comparison input is `last_assistant_message`**, the Stop-specific
   payload field. The Claude Code hooks reference explicitly says hooks needing
   the final assistant text must use it rather than reading the transcript,
   which lags. This removes the transcript-parse race entirely.

## Mechanism

### Part 1 — invert the default (Python)

`src/endless/report_cmd.py`, `report_prompts.py`, `cli.py`:

- `--json` accepts a third key, `verify`: a single non-empty command string.
  Rejected like the others on the wrong type; no Haiku call.
- Split today's single `_render_facts` into two:
  - `_render_sanctioned` — the user-facing block: `Verify:` (leads; it is the
    most actionable line), follow-ups, epic children, notes, questions.
  - `_render_agent_notes` — the worktree-anomaly advisory. This CANNOT be in
    the sanctioned block: it is explicitly labelled "for you — surface only if
    unexpected", so forcing its relay is wrong and excluding it from the block
    while leaving it inside would bounce any agent that obeys it. It renders
    OUTSIDE the markers, and the steer tells the agent that an unexpected
    anomaly is re-run material (`--json` note), never appended prose.
- Empty sanctioned block → substitute the `nothing-to-report` prompt text.
  Because the empty case now has a sanctioned string, the two rendering paths
  collapse into one: one steer, one comparison, no special case.
- Rename the `steer-empty` prompt to `nothing-to-report`. Its role changed from
  *steering the agent* to *being the sanctioned message*, so the old name would
  misdescribe it. Safe: no override file exists at either the machine or project
  layer, so nothing depends on the old name.
- `STEER` gains explicit `----- BEGIN REPORT -----` / `----- END REPORT -----`
  markers around `{facts}` so "verbatim" has an unambiguous extent, and names
  the gate so the agent knows the bounce is coming.

### Part 2 — record the checkpoint

- `internal/gatekind`: add `GateKindRelay = 2` (slug `relay`).
- `internal/schema/schema.sql`: seed the `gate_kinds` row; add
  `session_gates.sanctioned_text TEXT` and `session_gates.bounces INTEGER NOT
  NULL DEFAULT 0`. Plus `internal/schema/changes/e-1901-relay-gate.sql` for the
  populated real DB at land time.
  `session_gates` is the right home rather than a new table — it is already "a
  pending interception for a session" with a `kind_id` discriminator and named
  per-kind subject columns. Its doc comment (which says gates block at
  PreToolUse) is broadened to cover a Stop-blocking kind.
- `internal/monitor/session_gate.go`: `SetRelayCheckpoint`,
  `PendingRelayCheckpoint`, `ClearRelayCheckpoint`, `BumpRelayBounce` —
  mirroring the revisit helpers, including supersede-on-insert.
- `internal/sessionquerycmd`: `relay-checkpoint --session-id N`, sanctioned text
  on **stdin** (not argv — a report block is unbounded and would hit quoting and
  argv-length limits).
- `report_cmd.report_item` resolves the session via the existing
  `_current_endless_session_id()` and records. Best-effort: an unresolved session
  means no checkpoint and no gate, never a failed report.

### Part 3 — gate at Stop

- `claudePayload` gains `LastAssistantMessage` and `StopHookActive`.
- New `internal/hookcmd/relay_gate.go` holding the pure, DB-free comparison so
  it is unit-testable without infrastructure.
- Normalization before comparison, applied to both sides: trim trailing
  whitespace per line, drop blank lines at both ends, collapse blank runs, drop
  marker lines, drop lines that are only a code fence. Fence-dropping is
  deliberate: an agent wrapping the verify command in ``` is formatting, not
  prose, and bouncing it would be a false positive that teaches the agent the
  gate is noise.
- Compliant = normalized-empty OR normalized-equal. Otherwise emit
  `{"decision":"block","reason":…,"systemMessage":…}`. Both fields carry the
  violation because they go to different audiences — `reason` to Claude,
  `systemMessage` to the user — which is what "names the violation where both
  agent and user see it" requires.
- Loop guard: `bounces` is incremented per block and capped at 2, after which
  the gate clears and lets the turn end. `stop_hook_active` is undocumented, so
  it is a secondary signal only; the counter is the primary guard and is
  deterministic.
- Cleared on `UserPromptSubmit` — a new user turn supersedes an unconsumed
  checkpoint, so a checkpoint can never leak into a later turn (this is also
  what keeps `FULL STATUS` unblocked).

### Part 4 — Stop must be synchronous

`Stop` currently sits outside `SYNC_EVENTS` in `src/endless/setup.py`, so it is
installed `async: true` — and an async hook cannot block. Two changes:

- Move `Stop` into `SYNC_EVENTS`.
- `setup_claude_hook` currently early-returns when a hook is already installed,
  so no existing install would ever get the fix. Add an idempotent repair that
  corrects `async` flags that disagree with `SYNC_EVENTS` and reports what it
  changed.

The worktree's `.claude/settings.json` mirrors the user's global file, so it
picks the flag up once the global is repaired and `just claude-settings-init`
re-runs.

## Verification — `tests/tasks/e-1901-verify.sh`

Fully scripted, fail-fast on the unit contract, single entry point:

- Go unit tests: the normalization/verdict matrix (verbatim passes; appended
  prose bounces with the right count; empty passes; fences and markers tolerated),
  the block-response shape (both `reason` and `systemMessage` present), and the
  bounce cap.
- Python tests: `verify` payload accepted and rendered leading the block;
  anomalies rendered outside the markers; empty report renders `Nothing to
  report.`; the renamed prompt resolves.
- `setup.py`: `Stop` is in `SYNC_EVENTS`, and the repair flips a stale async
  entry.
- End-to-end through the real CLI → worktree endless-go → sandbox DB: run
  `endless task report` and assert a relay checkpoint row lands with the exact
  sanctioned text.

## Honest ceiling (carried from the analysis, not softened)

This is a hard gate on the report checkpoint, not a guarantee the urge never
fires: a re-prompted model can comply now and drift on a later turn, and the
bounce cap means a determined violation eventually lands. What changes is the
cost — appending stops being free and becomes "publicly named and bounced,
every time."

payload.title: Remove the vestigial session-recap flag now that one session maps to one task
payload.description: FlagNeedsRecap dates from open-ended multi-task sessions; one session now maps to one task and 'endless task report' covers the handoff, so the flag and its consumers should be audited and removed.
payload.text:
`FlagNeedsRecap` fires on both `Stop` and `SessionEnd` in
`internal/hookcmd/claude.go`, flagging a session as owing a recap. It dates from
the era when a Claude session was open-ended and covered many tasks, so a recap
was the only way to reconstruct what a session had done.

That premise no longer holds: one session now corresponds to roughly one task,
and `endless task report` covers the handoff for that task directly. The recap
flag, its consumers (`internal/hookcmd/recap.go`), and any surfacing of
"needs_recap" state should be audited and removed if nothing else depends on
them.

Scope: find every reader of the flag before deleting the writer — session
monitor / status rendering may still display it, and the sessions column (if any)
needs a schema change to drop.

Surfaced by Mike during E-1901, which added the Stop-hook relay gate alongside
the existing Stop-branch `FlagNeedsRecap` call.

payload.title: Distinguish retired event kinds from unknown ones instead of silently discarding both
payload.description: The replayEvent default branch silently skips any event kind it does not recognize, so an intentionally-skipped session kind and a typo'd or genuinely-unknown one are indistinguishable — data loss with no signal on rebuild-db and validate-db. A retired kind needs somewhere to live so it is recognized-then-discarded rather than falling into that path.

fields.analysis:
# Why this is a real hazard, and why it is not folded into E-1906

## What replay does today

`rebuild-db` and `validate-db` both go through
`events.ProjectToTempDB` -> `ReadAllEvents` -> `replayEvent`.

- `ReadAllEvents` does a plain `json.Unmarshal` per ledger line. It never
  calls `Event.Validate()`.
- `replayEvent` is a `switch evt.Kind` over the task and decision kinds. Its
  `default:` branch is commented "Skip non-task events silently (sessions,
  notes, etc.)" and returns nil.

So every `session.*`, `note.*`, `message.*` and `conversation.*` kind lands in
`default:` and is dropped without a trace — and so does a kind that is
misspelled, emitted by a newer binary, or removed from the vocabulary. The two
cases are indistinguishable at replay time.

## Where ValidKinds actually applies

`ValidKinds` is consulted in exactly one place: `Event.Validate()`
(`internal/events/event.go`), which is called only on the four EMIT paths in
`internal/eventcmd/event.go`. It is a write-side gate, not a read-side one.

Consequence: removing a kind from the closed set cannot fail a rebuild today.
That is not because retirement is handled — it is because replay checks
nothing. The safety is accidental.

## Proposal

1. `events.RetiredKinds` — a set a removed kind moves into rather than
   vanishing. `Validate()` consults it and rejects an emit with a distinct
   "retired" message, so a stale binary still emitting one gets a diagnosis
   rather than a generic "unknown kind".
2. Split `replayEvent`'s `default:` into two branches: a known-and-
   intentionally-skipped set (silent, as today) and everything else (appended
   to `ProjectResult.Errors`, which `rebuild-db` and `validate-db` already
   print as warnings).

Step 2 is the bulk of the work: it requires enumerating every kind that is
legitimately skipped at replay, which is currently implicit in the absence of
a case arm. That enumeration is why this is a separate task.

## Relation to E-1906

E-1906 removed `KindSessionRecapped` and `SessionRecappedPayload`. That removal
is safe under today's behavior and was verified as such:

- no emitter exists anywhere in the tree — the kind was introduced by
  `f99b9ab0` (E-804) as vocabulary and never wired up;
- `grep 'session\.recapped' .endless/db-ledger/*.jsonl` returns zero hits, so
  no ledger line references it;
- replay would skip it silently even if one did.

The hazard above predates E-1906 and is independent of it.

fields.title: Define the agent output-discipline contract and deliver its remaining surfaces
fields.description: Close out the prose-discipline arm of E-1785 in one task: (1) the discharged-fact test for what agent output may leave unsaid, (2) a veracity requirement that any surfaced fact be verified against live state at the moment of surfacing, never recalled, (3) `endless task annotate` as a task-scoped, write-only observation sink hidden from the default `task show`, (4) a do-not-recap stdout reminder on `task update --text` — E-1772's existing mechanism applied at the plan-write trigger, and (5) per-session last-checkpoint and bounce count in `session monitor`, reading the rows E-1901 records. E-1803 defined acceptable output functionally and E-1901 adds the Stop-hook teeth; these five are what the gate still does not define or reach. Merged from E-1823 (veracity), E-1879 (sink), E-1787 (plan-write trigger) and E-1826 (monitor surface) per user direction: review cost is per-task attention, not per-task size, so fewer tasks beats smaller ones. Part 5 is blocked by E-1901, which creates the rows it reads.
fields.analysis:
# Why these five are one task

## The gap E-1803 and E-1901 leave

E-1803 defined acceptable agent output functionally — a computed fact the user
cannot derive XOR a genuine open decision, else nothing — and owns the
compose-time PostToolUse nudge. E-1901 adds the teeth: a Stop-hook detector that
blocks the turn unless the final message matches the sanctioned report block.

Between them they establish *that* output is gated and *where* the gate fires.
Neither establishes *what the test actually is*, whether what survives the test
is *true*, where a suppressed-but-genuine observation *goes*, or covers the
plan-write moment and after-the-fact observability. That is this task.

## Part-by-part

1. **Discharged-fact test.** A fact recorded in a test, a guard, a verify
   script, a commit message, or a task field is discharged and must not appear
   in user-facing output — including when the agent introduced the problem and
   then fixed it, where the fix IS the record and nothing is left to decide.
   Deliverable is a test an agent can apply in the moment, plus the boundary
   against a genuine open decision, which stays worth saying.

2. **Veracity.** Any fact that IS surfaced must be verified against live state
   (git, the ledger, the file) at the moment of surfacing, never inferred or
   recalled from earlier context. A wrong fact must clear a HIGHER bar than an
   omitted one: a confidently-wrong fact the user must track down to disprove
   costs more than ceremony does. Some classes are mechanically catchable and
   worth a lightweight check — an agent-authored task-ID citation whose target
   does not resolve or is topically unrelated, or a state claim git contradicts.

   Parts 1 and 2 are the two clauses of one test. Part 1 governs output VOLUME;
   part 2 governs output VERACITY. An agent applies both at the same instant,
   composing the same sentence.

3. **Sink.** `endless task annotate <id> "..."` — task-scoped, append-only,
   write-only by design, hidden from the default `task show`, surfaced only
   under `task show --annotations`. Deliberately NOT project notes: those are
   project-scoped, have found no good use since being added, and are likely to
   be deprecated. The sink must not relocate noise to where the user already
   reads, or it has solved nothing.

4. **Plan-write trigger.** After an agent writes a plan (`task update --text`,
   or a plan-mode save) the chat re-narrates the plan, forcing the user to
   review the same material twice — the plan AND the recap. Same disease as
   end-of-session ceremony: restating a reviewable artifact. Rides E-1772's
   existing mechanism (nudge in the reminder, gate in the command, no hook —
   a CLI command can do it), with wording tunable via the report-prompts surface.

5. **Monitor surface.** E-1901's Part 2 records a relay checkpoint per
   `task report` call into `session_gates`, carrying sanctioned text and a bounce
   count, with accessors already written. Surfacing per-session last-checkpoint
   and bounces in `session monitor` is a read on rows that will already exist.

## Why merged rather than five tasks

Behavioral coupling, not just topical adjacency:

- A **rule without a sink** makes the agent drop genuine observations or smuggle
  them into prose — the failure E-1865 demonstrates.
- A **sink without the rule** yields annotate-and-narrate: the agent writes the
  observation down AND says it, giving the user a third place to read.
- The **volume clause without the veracity clause** governs how much the agent
  says while leaving the costlier failure — wrong content — ungoverned.
- The **gate without parts 4 and 5** leaves the plan-write moment uncovered and
  leaves compliance unobservable.

Economic coupling as well, and it is decisive here: the user's review cost is
per-task attention, not per-task size. Five small tasks cost five shepherd
cycles — triage, approval, spawn, review, land — for changes that individually
move little. One task costs one. Shrinking a task does not reduce that cost;
only removing a task does.

## Evidence

E-1865: an invariant already guarded by its verify script, and a regression
already covered by a test, were both narrated to the user anyway. Every fact
narrated in that session already had a durable home. That is simultaneously the
case for part 1 (the facts were discharged), part 3 (the agent had nowhere
else to put what it felt compelled to record), and the reason a nudge alone
was known to be insufficient.

## Sequencing

Parts 1–4 are independent of anything in flight. Part 5 is blocked by E-1901:
it reads the `session_gates` relay rows E-1901 creates. If E-1901 changes shape
during implementation, part 5 follows it rather than the other way round.

## Merge provenance

Merged from E-1823 (veracity), E-1879 (sink), E-1787 (plan-write trigger), and
E-1826 (monitor surface). E-1826 additionally lost scope before the merge:
its item (1), recording a checkpoint per `task report` call, is delivered by
E-1901 Part 2; its item (3), a record-only Stop hook designed to sidestep the
blocking approach E-1803 rejected, is superseded outright — E-1901 un-rejects
blocking. Only its item (2), the monitor surface, survives as part 5 here.

payload.outcome: Merged into E-1876 as part 2 (veracity). The volume clause and the veracity clause are two halves of one test an agent applies at the same instant; splitting them cost a second shepherd cycle for no separation of concern.
Merged into E-1876 as part 3 (the annotate sink). Its own description declared it half of a pair that does not work alone; E-1876 now carries both halves.
Merged into E-1876 as part 4 (plan-write trigger). A one-trigger extension of E-1772's existing reminder mechanism did not justify a full shepherd cycle of its own.

Merged into E-1876 as part 5, reduced to the monitor surface only. Item (1), recording a checkpoint per task report call, is delivered by E-1901 Part 2; item (3), a record-only Stop hook designed to sidestep blocking, is superseded because E-1901 blocks by design.

fields.text:
# Plan — E-1876: the output-discipline contract and its remaining surfaces

Five parts, one land. Parts 1–4 are independent of anything in flight; part 5
reads rows E-1901 creates and must be implemented after E-1901 lands (this task
is `blocked_by E-1901`).

## Framing decision that makes parts 1–2 buildable

The merged-away tasks described parts 1 and 2 as *definitions* — "a test an
agent can actually apply". A definition with no delivery surface is a document
nobody reads at the moment of composing. So **the rule is delivered as prompt
text on surfaces that already fire**, not as prose in a guide page:

- `report_prompts.NOTE_CHECK` / `QUESTION_CHECK` — the Haiku classifiers that
  already KEEP/DROP each entry at `task report --json` time. This is where the
  discharged-fact test does mechanical work.
- `report_prompts.STEER` (and E-1901's renamed `nothing-to-report`) — the
  compose-time framing.
- The guide gets the human-readable statement so the rule is citable, but the
  guide is the *documentation* of the rule, not its enforcement point.

Consequence: parts 1–2 are largely prompt-text work plus one mechanical check,
which is why they fit in the same task as parts 3–5 rather than dwarfing them.

## Part 1 — the discharged-fact test

**Rule.** A fact is *discharged* — and must not appear in user-facing output —
when it is already recorded somewhere durable the user can reach: a test, a
guard, a verify script, a commit message, or a task field (`outcome`,
`analysis`, `text`, an annotation). The agent introducing a problem and then
fixing it is the paradigm case: the fix is the record, and nothing is left for
the user to decide.

**Boundary against a genuine open decision.** A fact stays sayable when the user
must *act* on it and no artifact will prompt that action: an unresolved choice
blocking the work, or an out-of-band condition (a service down, a credential
expired) with no durable home. The test is *actionability by the user*, not
*importance to the agent*.

**Delivery.** Rewrite `NOTE_CHECK` in `src/endless/report_prompts.py` to make
dischargedness an explicit DROP criterion — today it drops "restates something
already visible in git/task state", which misses the recorded-in-a-test and
fixed-it-myself cases. Add the self-inflicted-and-fixed case by name; it is the
one agents rationalize past.

## Part 2 — veracity

**Rule.** Any fact that *is* surfaced must be verified against live state (git,
the ledger, the file) at the moment of surfacing — never inferred, never
recalled from earlier context. A wrong fact clears a higher bar than an omitted
one: the user must spend effort to disprove it.

**Delivery — prompt.** Both check prompts gain a veracity clause: an entry
asserting state the agent has not just verified is DROP, not KEEP.

**Delivery — mechanical check.** In `report_cmd.py`, before the Haiku pass,
extract `E-\d+` / `ED-\d+` citations from each `--json` note and question and
resolve them against the DB. An unresolvable ID is rejected with the offending
citation named. This catches the cheapest and most common wrong fact — a
hallucinated task reference — without a model call.

Topical-relatedness of a citation and git-contradiction checks are explicitly
**out of scope**: both need judgment, and a false positive here would teach the
agent the check is noise. The rule covers them; only ID-resolution is mechanized.

## Part 3 — `endless task annotate` (the sink)

**Storage.** New table, not the unused `tasks.notes` column — annotations are
append-only rows with their own timestamps and authorship:

```sql
CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS task_annotations (
    id         INTEGER PRIMARY KEY,
    task_id    INTEGER NOT NULL,
    session_id INTEGER,
    body       TEXT NOT NULL,
    created_at TEXT NOT NULL DEFAULT (strftime('%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%S','now')),
    FOREIGN KEY (task_id)    REFERENCES tasks(id)    ON DELETE CASCADE,
    FOREIGN KEY (session_id) REFERENCES sessions(id) ON DELETE SET NULL
);
```

Plus `internal/schema/changes/e-1876-task-annotations.sql` for the populated
real DB, matching the E-1901 change-file pattern.

**Command.** `endless task annotate <id> "..."` — append only. No edit, no
delete: an observation sink that can be curated is a second inbox.
`session_id` resolves via the existing `_current_endless_session_id()`,
best-effort.

**Display.** `task show --annotations` only. Decisions taken:

- **`--all-fields` does NOT include annotations.** It reads as "show me
  everything", which is exactly the reading path the sink must stay out of;
  including it would relocate noise to where the user already looks. The flag's
  help text is amended to say so explicitly, since the exclusion is otherwise
  surprising.
- **`--json` DOES include them.** Machine consumers are not the audience being
  protected, and excluding them would make the rows unqueryable in practice.

**Ordering.** Oldest first, each line stamped and attributed to its session.

## Part 4 — the plan-write trigger

Mirror E-1772 exactly. In `src/endless/task_cmd.py`, alongside
`_is_report_wind_down` / `_maybe_emit_report_reminder` (≈ lines 2477–2525), add
`_maybe_emit_plan_written_reminder`, fired when `task update` writes a non-empty
`--text` / `--text-file`.

Reuses E-1772's gate verbatim: fires only under `_running_under_agent()` or
`agent_view_requested()`, so a human editing a plan never sees it.

Wording (a fifth entry, `plan-written`, on the report-prompts surface so it is
tunable without touching source): the plan is saved and the user will read it —
do not recap it, do not summarize what you just wrote. Reply with a genuine open
decision or blocker that must be answered before implementing, or say nothing.

**Fires on `--text` only** — not `--description`, not `--analysis`. The recap
pathology is specific to writing a reviewable plan the user is about to read.

**Plan-mode saves** route through the same `task update --text` path, so they
are covered without a separate hook.

## Part 5 — the monitor surface (after E-1901)

E-1901 Part 2 lands `session_gates.sanctioned_text` + `bounces`, the
`GateKindRelay` kind, and `SetRelayCheckpoint` / `PendingRelayCheckpoint` /
`ClearRelayCheckpoint` / `BumpRelayBounce` in
`internal/monitor/session_gate.go`. Part 5 is a read on those rows.

Add a `LastRelayCheckpoint(sessionID)` accessor returning timestamp and bounce
count, and render it in `internal/sessionstatuscmd/session_status.go` — the
renderer `session monitor` loops over. One line per session:
`last checkpoint: 2m ago` , with the bounce count shown only when non-zero,
since a zero is the expected case and printing it is itself ceremony.

Detection logic lives in Go, not `settings.json`.

**Explicitly dropped from the merged E-1826**: recording the checkpoint (E-1901
Part 2 does it) and a record-only Stop hook (E-1901 blocks by design, so the
sidestep it was built around no longer applies).

## Verification — `tests/tasks/e-1876-verify.sh`

Single entry point, fail-fast:

- **Python.** `task annotate` appends a row; `task show` omits annotations by
  default AND under `--all-fields`; `--annotations` shows them oldest-first;
  `--json` includes them. The `plan-written` reminder fires on `--text` under
  `CLAUDECODE=1`, and does **not** fire on `--description`, on `--analysis`, or
  for a human invoker. An unresolvable `E-` citation in a `--json` note is
  rejected and names the citation; a resolvable one passes.
- **Go.** `LastRelayCheckpoint` returns the most recent row per session; the
  status renderer omits a zero bounce count and shows a non-zero one.
- **Schema.** The change-file applies cleanly to a populated DB and is
  idempotent.
- **Prompt-surface.** `plan-written` resolves through the project > machine >
  embedded precedence like the existing four.

## Sequencing for the implementing session

Parts 1–4 first, in one pass — they share the `report_prompts` and `task_cmd`
surfaces. Part 5 last, after confirming E-1901 has landed and its column and
accessor names match what this plan assumes; if E-1901 shifted, part 5 follows
it rather than the reverse.

## Open decisions for the user

1. **`task annotate` argument form.** Plan assumes an explicit task ID. The
   alternative — defaulting to the session's claimed task — is fewer keystrokes
   at the cost of an annotation landing on the wrong task when a session is
   bound to something unexpected. Explicit is the safer default; say if you want
   the implicit form.
2. **Whether the guide gets a prose statement of the rule at all.** The plan
   delivers the rule as prompt text and adds a short guide statement for
   citability. If you would rather the rule live *only* where it fires, drop the
   guide edit and the task shrinks.

payload.title: Repair the e-1771 verify script's failing project-register setup step
payload.description: tests/tasks/e-1771-verify.sh exits 2 in setup() with 'registering temp project failed' before any assertion runs; reproduces identically on main, so it predates E-1901.
payload.text:
`./tests/tasks/e-1771-verify.sh` exits 2 during `setup()` with
"ERROR: registering temp project failed", before running a single assertion.

Confirmed pre-existing and NOT caused by E-1901: the identical failure with the
identical message reproduces from the main checkout at the same commit.

The script builds a fully isolated env (temp XDG_CONFIG_HOME + XDG_CACHE_HOME,
a fresh temp git project) and then runs:

    en project register "${PROJ}" --infer --name verify1771 --status active

which fails. The sibling script `tests/tasks/e-1880-verify.sh` performs a
near-identical setup and succeeds, so the divergence between the two setups is
the place to start.

Note: E-1901 edited two assertions in this script (the steer header moved to the
BEGIN REPORT marker, and a stale `Status: unplanned` assertion was dropped —
E-1880 had already removed `Status:` from the report output, so that assertion
was asserting the opposite of the current contract). Those edits are correct but
cannot be exercised until this setup failure is fixed.

fields.text:
# Plan — E-1901: enforce verbatim report relay with a Stop-hook gate

**Status: implemented.** Rebased onto main (E-1803 landed), so `taskReportRe`,
the PostToolUse relay nudge, and `reportChannelRule` are reused, not reinvented.

## Decisions taken (were open in the plan)

1. **Verify command enters via the `--json` payload** as a `verify` key —
   symmetric with `notes`/`questions`, no `tasks` schema change, agent-supplied
   at report time. NOT Haiku-gated: a command is not prose, and asking a model
   whether a shell command "reads as ceremony" would invent a failure mode
   rather than catch one. Multi-line values are rejected — a checklist wearing a
   field's clothes is the ceremony this replaces.
2. **Empty report renders a fixed sanctioned line, `Nothing to report.`** — not
   silence. Silence is indistinguishable from a stalled agent; one fixed line
   proves the turn ended deliberately and states the null result, and reads
   correctly at a mid-session checkpoint as well as at session end.
3. **The comparison input is `last_assistant_message`**, the Stop-specific
   payload field. The hooks reference explicitly says hooks needing the final
   assistant text must use it rather than reading the transcript, which lags.
   This removed the transcript-parse race entirely.

## What shipped

### Part 1 — invert the default (Python)

- `--json` accepts `verify`; `_parse_verify` validates it.
- `_render_facts` split into `_render_sanctioned` (the user-facing block the
  gate enforces byte-for-byte) and `_render_agent_notes` (the worktree-anomaly
  advisory). The split is forced, not cosmetic: anomalies are conditional
  ("surface only if unexpected") while the sanctioned block is unconditional, so
  including them would compel the relay of noise, and leaving them inside while
  excluding them from the sanctioned text would bounce any agent that correctly
  acted on one. They render outside the markers with the escape route named.
- Verify leads the block (it is the one line the user acts on) and is
  backticked, so an agent copying verbatim reproduces the formatting rather than
  adding it and tripping the gate.
- Empty block → the `nothing-to-report` prompt text. Both cases now render,
  print, and arm identically — one steer, one comparison, no special case.
- `steer-empty` renamed `nothing-to-report`: its role changed from steering the
  agent to BEING the sanctioned message. No override file existed at either the
  machine or project layer, so nothing depended on the old name.
- `STEER` gained `----- BEGIN REPORT -----` / `----- END REPORT -----` markers
  and now names the gate, so the agent knows the bounce is coming.

### Part 2 — record the checkpoint

- `gatekind.GateKindRelay = 2` (slug `relay`), seeded in `schema.sql`, plus
  `internal/schema/changes/e-1901-relay-gate.sql` for the populated real DB.
- `session_gates` gained `sanctioned_text` and `bounces`. Reused rather than
  adding a table: it is already "a pending interception for a session" with a
  kind_id discriminator and named per-kind subject columns. It differs from
  `revisit` only in which hook consumes it (Stop vs PreToolUse); the table
  comment was broadened to say so.
- `monitor`: `SetRelayCheckpoint` / `PendingRelayCheckpoint` /
  `ClearRelayCheckpoint` / `BumpRelayBounce`, mirroring the revisit helpers
  including supersede-on-insert.
- `session-query relay-checkpoint --session-id N`, sanctioned text on **stdin** —
  a report block is unbounded, and a truncated sanctioned text would gate
  against the wrong string forever.
- `report_item` records via `_current_endless_session_id()`. Best-effort: an
  unresolved session means no checkpoint and no gate, never a failed report.

### Part 3 — gate at Stop

- `internal/hookcmd/relay_gate.go`. The comparison is pure and DB-free so the
  part that must be exactly right is testable without infrastructure.
- Normalization strips only meaningless variation — whitespace, blank lines,
  code fences, block markers — and never a line containing words. Fences and
  markers are tolerated deliberately: a false positive teaches the agent the
  gate is noise, and the deterrent dies with the trust.
- Compliant = normalized-equal OR normalized-empty. Silence is not what the
  report asked for, but the offense being caught is APPENDING; bouncing silence
  would punish an agent for under-speaking while trying to obey.
- Violation emits `decision:"block"` + `reason` (to Claude) + `systemMessage`
  (to the user). Both, because a violation only the agent sees is one it can
  privately reinterpret — the exact failure that made E-1803's nudge insufficient.
- Loop guard: `bounces` capped at 2, then the gate clears and **announces** that
  it gave up. `stop_hook_active` is undocumented, so the counter is the primary
  guard.
- Subagents exempt (their final message returns to the parent, not the user).
- Cleared on `UserPromptSubmit`, which is also what keeps `FULL STATUS` working.

### Part 4 — Stop made synchronous

`Stop` moved into `SYNC_EVENTS`; an async hook cannot block and would have
disabled the gate invisibly. `setup_claude_hook` early-returns once a hook is
installed, so `_repair_hook_async_flags` was added — otherwise no existing
install would ever receive the fix.

## Incidental fix, in scope because the feature depended on it

`_ensure_claude_session_id` shelled to the bare PATH `endless-go` instead of
`_resolve_endless_go()` — an instance of the exact bug E-1510's routing exists to
prevent. Under `--db sandbox` the global binary's embedded enums are a different
baseline from the sandbox DB's, the fail-closed integrity check turns that into a
hard error, and this function swallowed it as "no session". That is why the relay
checkpoint could never arm in a self-dev worktree.

## Verification

`tests/tasks/e-1901-verify.sh` — 34 checks, fully scripted, single entry point.
Fail-fast on the comparison matrix, then schema, report shape, checkpoint
arming, and the whole mechanism driven through the real hook binary (compliant
allowed, violation blocked with both audiences named, cosmetic formatting not
bounced, bounce cap terminating, new prompt retiring the checkpoint).

Adjacent suites brought forward to the superseded contract: e-1880 (27 pass),
e-1772 (14), e-1782 (10), e-1803 (9), and e-1771's steer anchor.

## Landing notes

- Run `endless db apply-change internal/schema/changes/e-1901-relay-gate.sql`
  against the real DB, then `just install`. Order matters: the change seeds the
  `relay` gate_kinds row, and any older endless-go binary opening that DB will
  fail closed on the enum drift until the new binary is installed. This is the
  standard ED-1506 contract, not new to this task.
- Existing dev sandboxes need recreating (`sandbox init --force --mode worktree`
  then `just dev-sandbox-init`): `CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS` cannot add columns
  and sandboxes never apply change files.
- `endless setup claude-hook` must be re-run once to flip Stop to sync; until
  then the gate is inert.

## Honest ceiling (carried from the analysis, not softened)

A hard gate on the report checkpoint, not a guarantee the urge never fires: a
re-prompted model can comply now and drift on a later turn, and the bounce cap
means a determined violation eventually lands. What changed is the cost —
appending stops being free and becomes "publicly named and bounced, every time."

payload.title: Narrow the e-1906 verify grep so E-1905's historical schema fixture stops tripping it
payload.description: e-1906-verify.sh fails 2 checks on main: its zero-hits grep for needs_recap/summary_seq matches a deliberate historical schema fixture inside tests/tasks/e-1905-verify.sh.
payload.text:
`./tests/tasks/e-1906-verify.sh` reports 44 passed, 2 failed on main:

    ✗ no live `needs_recap` anywhere in the source tree
        got: tests/tasks/e-1905-verify.sh:375:    needs_recap INTEGER NOT NULL DEFAULT 0,
    ✗ no live `summary_seq` anywhere in the source tree

Confirmed pre-existing and NOT caused by E-1901: reproduces identically from the
main checkout, same two checks, same counts.

Cause: E-1905 and E-1906 landed in close succession. E-1906's section 1 is a
grep-based "zero hits in the source tree" assertion for the identifiers it
removed. E-1905's verify script legitimately contains a historical `CREATE TABLE
sessions` fixture that still lists `needs_recap` and `summary_seq` — it is
asserting against a pre-drop schema on purpose. E-1906's grep cannot tell a live
reference from a deliberate historical fixture, so the sibling script trips it.

Fix direction: narrow E-1906's grep to exclude sibling task-verify fixtures (it
already excludes `internal/schema/changes/`, which has the same
period-accurate-schema property), rather than editing E-1905's fixture — the
fixture is correct and load-bearing for E-1905's own assertions.

Both symptoms are one defect and are filed together deliberately: they share a
single cause and a single fix, and splitting them would put two sessions in the
same grep block.

This is also a concrete instance of a coordination hazard worth noting: two
tasks whose changes overlap the same files landed in parallel and broke each
other's verification, with neither task's own suite green afterwards.
